It is important to see others coming from all walks of life(smarter or not as smart as you, richer and poorer than you, attractive as you or not so much…) going through what you have been facing all of your life so you can get it THAT IT ISN'T YOU. It’s a pattern - you didn’t cause it, you cannot control it, and you cannot “cure” it. This is what helped me the most. It didn’t get MY abusiveness dealt with, but for the most part, it DID eliminate abusers from my life. IT ISN’T YOU: Don’t give up. Get support.

Question: Every time I warn my son of the threat of eternal hellfire, he says he doesn't feel God's love or mine? Should this be handled by the pastor instead, since he is a stouter man and can hit harder?
Answer: “Hit harder?” Really? I would just take your son at his word - that he seems to be having difficulty experiencing a felt-sense of being loved by you or God or probably many others. I don’t know how old he is (some ages are more vulnerable to this kind of self-doubt than others. The onset of puberty and early teenage years up into, really, the mid-20’s, is difficult for many boys and young men to negotiate without hellish self-recrimination for not being “all that they can be,” caused in part by a society that follows the prompts of advertising campaigns and marketing efforts based on their claim that what they have to offer is what everybody needs in order to be complete. If your son is in or approaching teen years, I would be taking time with him, and possibly with a good and experienced counselor, to see what he means. he may be just fine, but may need to LEARN about his feelings… things get more complex as we mature… Things are simple inside us when we are very young, generally speaking. But as we mature, the number of things we need to take in to account when making decisions, like choosing friends, or developing interests, or following through on homework, all these things become very demanding. I suggest you take him at his word, put yourself in his shoes (think what that would be like if you were walking around every day not feeling “loved,” and how that would impact your relationships and effort in life. Find a way to make that kid feel loved and quit feeling so put upon when your kid has the strength to stand up to you to speak up for his needs. Your pastor doesn’t need to figure out how to love your son: YOU DO!

Question: What is mother's love?
Answer: The people that have impacted me the most are three women who put seeds in me that were comprised of example, wisdom, and caring investment in me. Certainly, my mother is at the top of the list. But first, a few comments about two others: First, my babysitter, "Grandma" Hatherly. She was like, 110 years old (well, okay, maybe not THAT old), and was an old farm lady... German... She had these funny habits, like twisting her entire dress and bra around underneath, well, body parts that had a will of their own, to make everything straighten out during the day. And, then there was this thing she did with her dentures... but more about that another time! One time, Grandma Hatherly told me, when I carelessly dropped a box of crayons, that I needed to get a spanking. For a brief moment I thought that might happen... Lord knows she was right, but I was pretty sure if she did that, she'd be fired on the spot... for no one spanked me... But it gave me a clue that maybe, just maybe, I wasn't getting "all that I needed." The other part of this which is the only reason anything would stick with a child for 50+ years is the "signs" that she genuinely cared about me, my welfare, and my future. I would catch her looking out over the kitchen dishes she would do through the window to our nice large backyard where squirrels and pheasant and red-winged black birds, and red-breasted robins made their nests, dug in the earth for food, and added their little noises to the ones that came from the breezes and sometimes winds that would roar through the tall oaks and maples. It is like she was looking into the future, while coming from a point of contemplation of the state of my soul... and she was worried. I think we pay attention to people the most when we know that they truly love us, and that is only known for sure if they do what only love is willing to do - to sacrifice for us. Love prepares fields within us to be reaped, when we're ready to pay the price of getting those seeds to grow and flourish. Grandma Hatherly’s seed was concern for me becoming ruled by wisdom; me becoming straightened out and shaped by necessity, not just by desire and impulse, promise and potential. She laid, through her own example of a disciplined and industrious life, good seed! 2) When I worked as a gopher on the sets where my dad produced television commercials, there was an assistant (whose name, I unfortunately do not recall) to the creative director and film editor, Bob Larsen, who could see the teenaged wild girl in front of her who (stupidly and ignorantly) had no fear of anything. Daunted by neither the potential of failure OR the prospects of success, I was more than a little headstrong. She could see it, she could see the dangers that that very “narrow” position was leaving me exposed to. She went ahead, took the chance of offending her boss'es employer (my dad, that is), by discreetly telling me, "Don't ever forget, Maggie, that you can ALWAYS be a lady, in every circumstance and with every person you ever meet. You can always be a lady." THAT seed, eventually, when I woke up, bore great fruit. 3) My mother: My mother was six when she immigrated from Scotland in 1916, coming through Ellis Island. Not much of a change, you say? You've never heard native Gaelic, man! She was the eldest of five children and she got the most beatings and the worst ones, for Grandpa set an example with her. Now, that leaves wounds, I don’t care who you are, wounds which this woman was still struggling with the last couple months of her life. Within days of her passing, I heard her, though she was in a coma of sorts that last seven to 10 days laying in that bed in a west-facing room of Penrose Hospital’s 11th floor in Colorado Springs, dealing with these wounds. “No,” she cried, shaking her head from left to right, “No, I didn’t do it, I didn’t do it….” You could almost seeing her run from her 6′2″ strong, coal-miner father… trying to escape what was coming… “I didn’t DO IT!” It was as though her soul was letting go of those terrible, deep fears that an inexperienced parent was placing in her like a seal to a certain kind of fate in her future. Surely these fears and hurts were not perfectly healed until she went home to be with the Lord at 10:16 pm, on a Monday evening, July 6, 1980. My father, having been with her all day, decided he would leave and run home to 326 Oakhurst, the home they bought on Cheyenne Mountain when they retired to Colorado Springs, Colorado, from our beautiful home in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, in late 1978. He was going to fix himself a bit to eat and return to the hospital. He remarked later that he cleaned the sink from his dinner dishes, and looked up and said, “There, Sal, how’s that?” I am quite sure that my mother saw him do this as she was “going home.” I was in the room, with my sister, Sally, who had her hand on mom’s left shoulder; I was holding her hand, and the room was dark except for a light over a small dresser set into the wall next to the bathroom. The nurse had just advised us, “She’s going…” There was nothing but small gurgling from the lungs that were overgrown with e. coli, a typical bacteria we live with our whole lives, but that gets its way with immune systems that are severely compromised. Soon, the gurgling subsided, as did the small rise and fall of her chest. I felt her spirit rise straight up and out of her body and up through that west window to her more-than deserved, new home, called Heaven. My graceful sister quietly uttered the phrase, “Free at last.” Within moments, as I went into the hall to deal-with and not deal with my feelings, there was my father getting off the elevator. He looked at me, so typical in his well-mannered way, willing to meet me with a smile, but he saw right away, all reasons for smiling were gone for now. He looked with a question on his face, in his heart, in his whole being, and may have said, “Is she…gone?” I said “Yes,” and he went to her room, his beloved there, of 37 years in holy matrimony, another year or more of, well, courting and whatever else that is sometimes… He gathered “Sadie” (the name on her bc from Scotland, her body diminished, her head that was kept full of hair in part by that thyroid medication she took, now nearly bald, from the chemo and radiation, into his arms. He was quiet. For the most part, my father was a mild mannered, and somewhat quiet man. He was very soft and tender in very very very many ways. As the impossibility of the never-should-happen thing dawned upon him, surely his soul was ripped in two, with the one sure thing he knew, the one always-reliable and always-there-no-matter-what, having given up her spot to the future he would make for himself, as it was also so for my sister and myself. I believe deep grief, the kind that comes from losing our loved ones through any kind of separation, but especially through death before its time (if there is EVER a REAL time for death…) is one of the most destructive things mankind faces. If not handled properly, if re-mooring to GOOD people, that is people who hold your welfare above theirs with respect to the position they occupy in your life, is not done correctly, in a way where love can be sustained once again through thick and thin, is horrifically effective at destroying human hope, love, character, willingness to risk, and grow, and a kazillion other things. He held her for a few moments, then the stupid nurse came in - a different one than the one that gave us the warning to my sister and me about my mom being about to die… maybe that one was actually an angel? I don’t recall if I saw that one, the nice one again, and this one, she was heavy set… like me. Bitter, aggressive, and down to business. Like me. My father had JUST walked in and was holding his mate of nearly 40 years, who had given him three children, all her attention and devotion on a daily basis, and kept that house perfect EVERY SINGLE DAY OF HER LIFE, no matter if she was sick, or tired, or just didn’t feel like it - no matter what was going on. And here was this nurse who was gonna get things done… like me. Get that paperwork so that the body could be collected; find out if Dad wanted an autopsy… Where then would the body go? For God’s sake, what is WRONG with hospitals? With people? Soon, that was all that was left: Leaving. Us leaving where she spent her last 10 days. Us leaving her place of departing us until we see her in Heaven, or in the Spirit if we are lucky. Us now being three (my brother was in California). One father, two daughters. I had just graduated from college four weeks prior. My mom got to see her last child graduate from college - a college she surely had envied growing up and attending high school just 10 blocks south of it in the 1920’s. My sister had three sons, a husband, a good career in California, and family issues like most of us. One father, who had already buried his elder brother 25 years prior, and his father, then his mother. Two daughters, who, for the most part, had carried on the most critical parts of their conversational needs with their father THROUGH their mother. Now, it was just us three. Grief and loss are not likely bedfellows for great emotional transformational shifts. Shortly, that is about 90 days later a woman 16 years younger than my father would jump into our dad’s bed, and in relatively quick order, set up an alienating atmosphere that reduced our contact with our dad to next to nill for my sister and at one five-year span, to absolutely nill fo rme. Eventually, the woman would steal the entirety from us and our children, and from our and their futures, the estate that my mother helped build with all life. It took me four years to begin to cry about losing my mom, and it took decades for me to understand why my life so utterly tanked, hit the skids, and was seemingly so permanently broken. My mom was the tether of Love that is necessary for a family to BE a family. Ground out by those unfortunate excessive disciplinary actions by Grandpa, and in the training ground of Grandma's kitchen, laundry line, home, and then going to work early, at age 14 in the Antlers Hotel in Colorado Springs, then having to quit school at 16 to work full time to help the family out, there was no fluff in my mother's life. She absolutely laid down her life for all of us. All her choices, not unlike my father’s in the larger world of advertising, were about how to fit into what her role, her main purposes and functions in life were. She laid down her life for my father, who, thank God, wasn't a "striker" of people, but who carried a critical spirit and was aloof in ways that he probably didn't even understand the impact of. She laid down her life before marrying our father for a first husband whom, thank God, even though it was in a time when you DON'T DIVORCE, 1939, she divorced as he probably would have killed her (he was a drunk and a beater); then she began laying down her life for our father, as she continued to try and handle her first two children from her first marriage - Jack and Marilyn. Then, when her offspring from my dad, my brother, Donnie, and only a year and a half later, my sister Sally, and much later me, were born, she kept laying her life down for all of us. Love, the bible says, (from the Passion translation) says in 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 is like this: 4 Love is large and incredibly patient. Love is gentle and consistently kind to all. It refuses to be jealous when blessing comes to someone else. Love does not brag about one’s achievements nor inflate its own importance. 5 Love does not traffic in shame and disrespect, nor selfishly seek its own honor. Love is not easily irritated or quick to take offense. 6 Love joyfully celebrates honesty and finds no delight in what is wrong. 7 Love is a safe place of shelter, for it never stops believing the best for others. Love never takes failure as defeat, for it never gives up. 8 Love never stops loving. It extends beyond the gift of prophecy, which eventually fades away. It is more enduring than tongues, which will one day fall silent. Love remains long after words of knowledge are forgotten. I find these words to be true in my own life; where I have succeeded at love, it looked like these words, like my mother’s love, and my father’s as well. recall the unfortunate and presumptive error of ignorance in my youth where as a teenager how I decided to align myself with my strong-minded father, and was critical of my mom’s seeming weakness in not standing up for herself more, not "getting" more for herself. Only recently have I taken to heart that which corrects that error, the biblical admonition, “WITH ALL YOUR GETTING, GET WISDOM...” My mother WISELY secured her permanent home in Heaven through her investment here on Earth in the one thing that endures - LOVE. These three ladies set good examples for me, laid GREAT seeds in me, and I consider it a heavy personal obligation, even a DEBT, to do them right by becoming all I can be, doing all I can do, to ALSO love, and to leave a legacy, thereby, that is both presently impactful and permanently worthy of emulation. Especially in the area of LOVE.

Question: When do you use “there,” “their,” and “they’re” in a sentence?
Answer: Dearest Quorian, Who dared to ask this question: “there” is a place, like “Unless you give me my alimony check, right now, I”m going to make you go over there, across the street, and rob that bank to pay me off what you owe me so I can take care of that child you haven’t cared to give one second of your life to ever since…” But, if you stopped me, and broke down in tears when I yelled the above in your ears, I might reverse direction and pat you on your head and say, “Now, there, there, Jerry…” to comfort you; and as if to bring back your attention from your dismal prospects of getting out of whatever I might be really angling for, and at this point, it’s probably WAY more than MONEY… And then, if it seemed to my liking, I might continue and say something about a type of place, but it isn’t really geographic, yet it does imply something related to the existence of a thing…. “There isn’t any reason to fret and fume, I am certain we can work something out!” You look up at me with the wet eyes of a basset hound as if to say, “Really, mum, there isn’t???” “Why no, Jerry, there isn’t. Instead of breaking into Wells Fargo today, GO AHEAD AND GIMME THE KEYS TO YOUR MOTORHOME, RIGHT NOW!!!” “WHAT?” you say as the puppy dog fleas under the bed behind the quilt hanging over it. “What do you mean? You know that’s not mine!” “I don’t care,” I say, ever vindicated by malicious voice tone alone… “Get it from THEM then! Get the keys and gimme that thing!” “They’re not even home… they would flip out, man, you’re crazy!” “Nonsense, Jerry, their time to make use of that thing that has been sitting in your backyard for three years now has gone away… it’s a mist. They’re going to be sorry, for sure, but do you really think they’re going to be THAT surprised? It’s THEIR STUPID FAULT!” “Besides, Jerry, there really isn’t any other way to solve this dispute today, and you’ve been putting off the needs of your son far too long… Today is the DAY! Rejoice and be GLAD in it! Their day will come, but not at my expense anymore!” There - a place, literally, physically; or perhaps as a point of reference to draw the listener’s or reader’s attention to another place. Sometimes used to comfort the mournful or hopeless. “There, there, Juliet; he really was a bit of a dufus to drink that poison, don’t you think?” Sometimes, the urge to comfort another may not, however, be met with glee. They’re - a contraction of the plural noun THEY with the verb ARE (present tense). Their - Modifying an object showing possession by another, though not YOURS, so give me that alimony right now! Nice to hear from you JS! Keep on keepin’ on! Blessings!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: My friend hasn't been answering his phone for 2 months saying he's going off the grid. I know I'm not the problem but I am really worried about his mental state. What should I do?
Answer: Be normal. Be normal person during an abnormal time. Many people are nervous, depressed, anxious, uncomfortable, at time feel like they’re coming apart at the seams. Be the normal friend. Don’t worry about him. Establish a routine of emailing, or drop him a funny meme to his home address. Emphasize when you do talk to him that while things are still very weird, they will not stay this way forever. If he’s up for a joke, tease him that they’ll probably get worse… but only if he’s up for a laugh. You still care about your friend; that is normal… And then, try and see, if he does return the favor of contacting you too, get him to talk about something he is interested in. Your job is just to be a friend.

This sacrament when taken seriously and, as instructed by Christ to do so, to take it OFTEN, allows believers to more fully live out all aspects of the redemptive process that Christ’s birth, life, sufferings, death and resurrection have purchased for us. I am indeed a blessed person for having these incredible gifts dropped into my life by people whose righteousness yet exceeds mine; yet such seeds cannot help but to return to their Creator joyous cheers and praise at all times. I praise the Lord here and now for the Gift of Faith that He bestowed upon me and for every other good gift he continues to supply without expectation of return. I dedicate myself again here and now to serving Him in every single situation and moment that I find myself in, as he is worthy of ALL PRAISE, HONOR, and GLORY. Thanks for the ask. Celebrate Him throughout 2021 and it can’t help but be a Great New Year for you and yours! Blessings from Colorado Springs, at the foot of “America’s Mountain.” Credit for photo, Gazette Telegraph.

Question: Why is fornication so destructive to one's family life, character, reputation, social standing, and self-esteem?
Answer: Fornication is an act of rebellion against God and most common sensibilities that respect that nature of things - that things, all things, are created with specific forms for specific functions. Fornication is the pursuit of temporary gratification, and, like an overeater pursuing serenity in a bowl of pasta due to the rise he or she will get in the mood after consuming highly refined carbs, will lead only to a temporary ‘hit” of good feelings, WHILE also at the same time EXHAUSTING the body because without heart soul and mind fully engaged, the experience pulls the body out of balance and ultimately weakens it. Thanks for the ask. Make it a good 2021!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Do you think going to church makes you more peaceful?
Answer: Perhaps yes, perhaps no. Why yes? Because the overt intention of most church organizations is to promote a general outlook which looks toward the benefit of all - walk in goodness, in light; be kind; forgive; remember your Creator, and so on. These are certainly good elements of most churches just as prayer, singing, study of God’s word and drawing close to the knee of Wisdom are present there at most church services to help one keep one’s promises to self and to God. Why no? Well, in terms of any particular service, as opposed to just over all feelings or intentions, there are churches and Christian events I have attended which were successful in bringing in the presence of the heavenly host where peace does descend, gentle as a dove, as well as firmly embracing like a mother lion around her cub; when those events happen I would definitely say THAT event, that happening makes one more peaceful, if one has learned to trust and receive. Most churches I am familiar with today, however, fail to keep an open line to heaven, nearly always due to the failure of the pastor and his or her leadership to break through their own religiosity in order to secure a permanent foothold in terms of connection with God the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, as well as with the heavenly host. Therefore, on a whole, at least in my experience, attending any one specific church service does not make one more peaceful, while learning to practice what is preached at most services, even if those preaching it are unable to maintain a very good practice, can be beneficial, MOST church services do not lead to the kind of peace that God promised when he manifested as the Son.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What youth mentoring programs have shown to be the most useful and/or effective?
Answer: This answer is not research-based, but it does respond to the broader question of how, in general, people develop into effective adults, using this definition for effective: Happy, industrious, productive, capable of running their own selves and activities well enough to select suitable paths of employment, as well as the right people (for them) to befriend, and to develop some of those relationships into long-term ones that are mutually supportive. When I think of what helps youth grow into effective adults, what first jumps to mind is what Chicago, Illinois (USA) educational reform leader Marva Collins said in one of her books (Ordinary Children, Extraordinary Teachers): “Children succeed based on the numbers of patterns (she specifies, if I recall correctly, social, emotional, mathematical, and linguistic patterns) that they learn, practice, and master.” Then I can’t help but think of Benjamin Franklin who was born into a family with 16 older brothers and sisters. Before he ever penned what we today call its descendent, The Farmer’s Almanac, Benjamin Franklin’s little “village” of a family schooled him up close and personal in politics, economics, culture, family, psychology and sociology. One thing he must have learned is how to say ‘No,” at least eventually, because when he worked for his older brother in his print shop, and got beat mostly daily, sometimes severely, he finally said “No,” walked out and benefited the rest of us with his many independent contributions to science, culture, and the principles found and thought to be at that point, legitimate to guide the governing of a new nation. Patterns; how many patterns did Benjamin Franklin acquire, I wonder, before he ever left home? Therefore, we can certainly suppose that for those children being raised in pattern-poor environments, the many mentoring organizations mentioned by others would be better than nothing. There actually are statistics on Marva Collins Preparatory School - the last ones I heard, in the early 1990’s, is that out of all the children that had graduated from the two high schools that were running at that point in time, every single one went to college self pay, or on a scholarship, and graduated from college, and that not one had an out-of-wedlock pregnancy. For older youths, National Outdoor Leadership, teaches teamwork, leadership, real-world skills in outdoor environments as well as self-awareness and self-management skills. And, can arrange with the participants in advance to seek college credits in outdoor education and biology.

There is no one who can answer this for you outside of your own conscience. Get your head into that bible and SEEK HIM DILIGENTLY. Nothing you did or did not do will make it or break it. You’ve got to look at the truth in your heart. Repent while there is time. SEEK HIM. DO WHAT PLEASES HIM

Question: What are some ideas about how to talk to kids about the evils of voodoo?
Answer: Thank you for including me in this A2A. Hope your family, friends and co-workers (if you are in the working world) are safe and well. My only child, a son, has seen into the Spirit realm since he was very young - starting before he could talk, and NO, I wasn’t reading to him out of Christian books describing the feathers of lurking demons either. So, I’m lucky. He kind of knew. But I think I would use the metaphor of a seed to help a child see - and I would alert them to begin using their capacity to sort out the weeds from the grass in the lawn to be aware of the origin, purpose, and end point of all ideas, for nothing in the Created Realm is neutral. Now, then again, when we are talking about physical things, we are going to be driven to the conclusion that it is in how it’s going to be used that counts… even Jesus says that. But, IF the child has been allowed to be aware of the spiritual realm, and IF they know, even on their own level, how to take cover under the arms of God (which, of course, often means under the shelter of the wings of His gigantic Angelic Armies), then I believe they should be ready to understand the difference between being a servant of God, versus being a manipulator. At their core, all the witchcraft groups, and it’s Big Brother, satanism, are focused on POWER, getting power to control events and quite often other people. This is what makes ALL witchcraft wrong; it is NOT in the intent of the heart. On a “non-spritual” level, I can be well intended, but answer that ONE text on my cell phone in the car that ONE day, and end a life. That’s well meaning, but NOT well doing. Some witches are just plain ignorant, and some know precisely what they like about their “craft.” All are deceived that they can get away with this sin against God, this sin which is as the sin of rebellion, without recourse or bad effect on their lives. Ask witches who have left it all behind what kind of price they paid for their participation in the occult. So, to teach a child about the evil in this world is a very hard burden and makes us sad, but forewarned can be forearmed. I would be careful to accompany any conversation about these things, or anything in the occult, with three times as much info on how to walk so close to Jesus that these things don’t come nigh us. It is important that we all learn as early as possible how much more fun, joy, good results, prosperity, meaning, knowledge, insight, wisdom and so on, the Kingdom of God has, over everything else, if we are to keep others and ourselves motivated to keep growing, keep going after the NEXT thing that God wants to teach us, both for our own welfare and for, of course, service to Him. Last, I would not introduce ANY symbols, or go into the depth of objects or rituals used in any rites of these groups unless there was a real reason for it. These things, through demonic activity, can attach to undeveloped or malnourished parts of the soul, and be a “seed” for worser things as the child matures. Witchcraft is full of seduction and children need to be protected from it at all costs.

Question: Has the pandemic gotten to where people are scared to be around any people?
Answer: It certainly has moved me into the direction of stopping assuming that everybody is my best friend… or even someone I’d like to meet. I think the pandemic has awakened me to the fact that we have as a society in the west continued to operate with one another at a near-familial level the last 200 years, despite the advances in medicine that have revealed the considerable dangers involved with making assumptions - we ASSUME others are as conscientious as we are being; we ASSUME others want to continue to live as much as we do; we ASSUME others are well-intended - and we like to forget the FACT that many are not, that some are drunk, some are on drugs, some should be on drugs and some are on the wrong drugs, when we visit the grocery store, the gas station, the fast food restaurant or other places that may contain the biggest variable in this pandemic… PEOPLE! My son and I visited a bible study at one of the local Salvation Army residential centers in our town the other night. We hadn’t been since last February when COVID 19 was beginning to break out. After all, those employees NEED those jobs, or else they are on the street. I might lie about it if it were me. And the residents? They KNOW what it would put others through, if not also deliver them feet first to the nearest and busiest emergency room in the city to whatever fate has in store for them. You don’t think THOSE people are hiding their coughs? So, while I’m not particularly afraid of behavior, their behaviors, attitudes, and whatever may be hitchhiking on their clothes or in their lungs, yeah, I’m a LOT more cautious and suspicious than before COVID 19. Thanks for the A2A.

Question: What happens when I pray for someone else's good?
Answer: It’s funny to me looking at the results about this issue in Wiki, because the VERY limited number of “scientific” studies that have been done on prayer in any systematic way often indicates prayer for someone else does not impact their welfare. Yet, a Christian man named John G. Lake, who in his later years had a ministry in Spokane, Washington, where he was hated by the medical establishment because every time he prayed for people, the hospitals would be emptied. Now, even if we credit the angry doctors with good intentions (“How can you deceive people like this? This is only ‘placebo’ effect and in days their welfare will be worse than ever, and some may even DIE!!!”), we gotta ask, ‘What was really happening?’ It was also John G. Lake, mentioned recently (Mar 17, 2020) in the Times Advocate, who took “plague [that] was very much alive…in his hand and held it under a microscope. The plague bacteria instantly died in Lake's hand.” This isn’t made up, it is true. Thought itself, whether or not it is “prayer” has an energy in it, and therefore, of course, can manifest something. Question: How do I help? My mom keeps crying as my grandma is critical in the icu and she can’t go see her in Canada because of the 14 day quarantine. We all needed to go to the funeral and I’ve never coped with a loss.
Answer: What a tragedy this is for you, your mom, your grandma, and others in the same situation! I am so very sorry for your situation. There hasn’t been much in mainstream news about family members of people who are in the hospital and cut off from direct contact due to restrictions based on keeping others free from the virus that causes COVID-19. If I were faced with such a situation, I would be trying to contact attorneys for help. Know this, that while you feel so terribly alone with this problem, you are not the only one facing limited options to deal with such vital needs. When someone else controls your access to something, your legal options are to press for permission through channels such as the Board of Directors of the hospital your grandma is in, or through some part of, in your case, the Canadian government. The best way you can help your mother is to be understanding; to sympathize with her; to spend a few minutes every day with her praying for your Grandma; to urge her to call whomever she can for help. And, moreover, to suggest to her to do as much as she possibly can to get ready for a trip, at least for herself, in case Canada LIFTS the quarantine protocol. Perhaps if she can get a hold of a complete, and brand new suit of Personal Protective “clothing,” and she took a photo of it and forwarded it to the facility your grandma is in, they could at least begin to set up the ability for her to be as close as possible to Grandma when she gets there. I pray that instead, your grandma heals. Even a 104-year old woman after suffering with COVID-19 for many months, even SHE got well. So can your grandmother. Thank you for being a child who cares so much about your family.

Because you see, if they can’t understand why masks are helpful, and how TRULY “inexpensive” a precaution they are, and if they do not understand, just by thinking, about how the constituents of exhaled breath CONCENTRATE when people CONGREGATE in close quarters, and that suffering COVID-19 is related to many things, INCLUDING VIRAL LOAD, then why would I risk hanging around them on ANY day? Name: Sara Stone
Question: Since I moved back to my parents about 4 months ago, my father keeps getting really angry and talk pretty ugly to me, and most of the times he's around I feel like he really doesn't want me to be here. What's wrong with us…?
Answer: Sorry to hear you are facing this kind of stress in the midst of an already weird and uncomfortable time. When my child was very young, say between four and six, we visited a store on the westside - a discount, re-sell place. They have the old circular clothing racks there, perfect for a child to hide under….! All of a sudden, though I kept really good watch over my son, he was gone! Inside, of course, I panicked! Then I saw some clothing moving under a rack a good 15 feet away from me, and was so relieved to find him under there. I remember doing the same thing myself when my mom would drag me along to stores. BORING! And that’s what I thought this kind of behavior is about… just being bored and looking to play. Years later, however, my son told me one reason why kids might do that behavior. The young of other mammals, and our little children as well, “know” when mom, their chief protector most of the time, is TIRED. Running off to a safe, sheltered, dark place and hiding can be a defense mechanism that is based in instincts! What an insight! Makes total sense to me now! What does this have to do with your Dad? I’m thinking, instinctively, he is pushing you away and being hostile due to CO-VID 19 and its very real threats against your life and his. It is entirely unnatural to keep social distances up, especially with people we know… Doing so causes tension, and keeping on our toes about this practice makes many people (might I say ALL?) uptight. I think you might want to consider that your dad is worried, and at moments he might not even admit to himself, he is worried about somehow hurting YOU by being sick himself and not knowing it. Words won’t comfort him - he’s your dad, and if he loves you, he is still going to NOT want you to get sick or worse. Wear your mask, even at home… research shows there is a big spread amongst families whose members eat together and do things together, live watch tv, if they do it without masks. It seems weird to do it, but my family is doing it. Masks cannot control every little risk about this pandemic, but it slows transmission rates, even at home, among family members, as does the hand washing for more than 20 seconds… and keeping up with other hygiene, and laundry cycling on hot water and hot air for drying, and disinfecting high-touch surfaces like door knobs, faucet and drawer pulls and handles, light switches, electronic devices, and so on and so forth. See what you can do to contribute, and find sources of real support where you can let your hair down and get things off your chest… don’t try to resolve a bunch of family stuff right now. We’re all on docks that are shifting in the water and some of our docks’ posts are coming loose from their mooring. Give things time… I think Fall 2021 we will all be much better off and wiser. Now, however, is NOT the time to let up. Keep up all your efforts. In your heart of hearts, try to just take time to remind yourself of all that you value about your dad and other family members, and how much you have to look forward to, to live for, and to do in life, so that you can keep your motivation HIGH (and your example SUPERIOR) til this thing is over.
