Name: Sara Stone
Question: I’m so emotionally drained after bringing my newborn home. I haven’t slept, or actually took a proper shower. Sometimes I just want to run away for a couple minutes but I feel trapped. Any advice on how to handle this?
Answer: Would you please call some people who are known as midwives? Families often used to reside in the same geographic area for a few generations, allowing the moms to pass on important info, personal info, about how they got through stuff like being a new mom… including what they did to deal with the underlying imbalance of hormones and other things going on in some of our bodies after childbirth. Plus, if this is your first child, which I presume it is, you have ALL the stress, anxiety, along with the wonderment and awe of what just happened… and you are caught up in, as well as trapped by, the event and all it portends. This is the biggest change you have ever gone through in your life. You need input; example; plenty of choices. La Leche League has moms that function together as a support group for breastfeeding, but you don’t actually have to be nursing to take advantage of their help and it’s either really cheap or free. Typically, they meet once per week, and moms share tips. IT IS SUPER IMPORTANT to nip this in the bud. YOU ARE EXHAUSTED and no one is showing you the ropes. Please reach out. It will make all the difference in the world to you AND your baby. For me, I didn’t do this. And I was EXACTLY as you are now; exhausted, getting progressively drained, not showering… and so on. Thank God I did nurse, because then you have the advantage of prolactin (the perseverance hormone), and oxycotin - the relaxation hormone. It’s what got me through it all! ScienceAlert.com: “Oxytocin is released during both orgasm and breastfeeding. Secreted by the pituitary gland and released in the hypothalamus, this hormone makes us feel close to others and promotes affection.” Glad you spoke up, now go make a friend. Your baby will thank you!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What have you learned about your own mental health and that of others from the Covid 19 coronavirus pandemic?
Answer: I know what anxiety is now; I know how it builds up, how it ramps a person up, how hard it is to control when it is being caused by fear that’s just under the surface about something important that you have limited control over. I know some people don’t share their tensions or worries very often… they go it alone. I’ve relearned that getting out of the house and taking a walk, getting some fresh air, and OH NATURE, are all really good for a person, Co-Vid times or not. I learned some people (like President Trump) use denial REALLY REALLY WELL, but that in the case of Co-Vid 19, denial (of possible risk) is NOT good for the people around you. I’ve learned a lot about some of the specific ways in which our nation’s culture and political system is just junk; we are in far more trouble than I thought. The fragmentation of manners, the lack of facility with gathering knowledge, performing sensible analysis, then making cohesive summaries that hit on the important and don’t leave things up in the air in the readers’ minds, and the abandonment of just plain common sense is what characterizes America today. Whatever that horse was, the prized stallion, that kept us in the lead, he is so far out of the barn now, well, I don’t think we would recognize him if he trotted back in.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: I just got baptized. What should I know? No turning back bc it's blasphemy.
Answer: SOME people receive the baptism of the Holy Spirit at the same time as they come to Christ, repenting of their sins and turning their life over to Him. I assume your baptism involved at least repentance and coming under the Lordship of Jesus Christ. IF you did not also receive baptism of the Holy Spirit where you got the gift of tongues activated in you, go ASK for it. If your pastor isn’t “for” this gift, get away from him and go get someone who knows more and has gone deeper, for it will keep your growth at bay, generally speaking. I know some who refused this gift because they specifically believe it passed away with the last death of the last person who knew Jesus or knew his disciples and apostles. Once you have this gift, use it OFTEN. Paul himself said he “prayed more in tongues” than anyone who was around him. Yet he had the gift in place and perspective, but he DID employ it CONSTANTLY. So do the people alive today whom I respect the most in the Christian walk of life: Heidi Baker of IRIS ministries, for instance; Jerame Nelson; Todd White; really, anyone who is walking in miracles and healings, and most importantly, who have really submitted to Christ’s yoke and hold nothing back from him. The second most important thing to know is that rejection and criticism and ignorant remarks from others can only STOP you and your progress if YOU let it; earnestly pray, constantly. This is THE most important advice I can give you, even more important than reading the bible: PRAY PRAY PRAY. This is what keeps us in that spiritual realm, and accessing so many things that otherwise the darkness of this world, like hope, healing, health, strength, power, sanity, wisdom, charity, and so forth, will choke right out of our consciousness. And YES, you really are saved; you really ARE HIS, and IT IS DIFFERENT. Congratulations!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How confident are you as quarantine restrictions are being lifted?
Answer: Totally - I am totally confident that this bug has not seen its last day, last death, last chance to damage the internal organs of any one so unfortunate as to be hit on by it. I am totally confident that RAMPING UP, not down, is the way to go, with efforts to self-protect. I am TOTALLY confident that, like my own inclination, it is MUCH more fun and attractive an option to think this thing is done and that we can “relax;” I am TOTALLY confident, as I saw three dozen cars parked at the bar closest to me last night (Juneteenth), that the LEAST symptomatic groups (ages 10–19 and 20–20-something) will absolutely be ready to have a good time and share everything they got with others up close and personal in enclosed, not-well ventilated places. I am sure that the older group in particular will increase the spread among their own age group, families, and once their family members get it, if they are asymptomatic as well, then they will be carrying it to grocery stores, other places of business, medical offices, dental offices, government offices, and work places. That’s why, at our home, we are instituting some NEW and improved practices… more stringent cleaning and disinfecting; even catching stuff on clothing that has seen the big wide unquarantined, ”I’m dying (hopefully not literally) for a break, from the masks, from being alone, from not doing what I want to, from having to think about it, from being afraid… cautious, intimidated by this THING” before it sheds on floors, walls, furniture, beds. That’s why I am looking for inspiration to TOTALLY sit this one out by packing up and going around country, carefully, in a well-planned manner… camping, hiking, fishing, visiting. Doing some good for others. Working remotely possibly throughout? Life is good. Preserving it is a good idea. Running with the crowd on this “opening up,” in my opinion, not so good. Be safe; wear a GOOD mask; wash your hands; don’t congregate. Take care of your health.. Be careful.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How do I tell my parents it's still not safe to go to church during COVID?
Answer: Provide statistics about the spread; make sure they understand the “novel” nature of this bug; you can show them photographs of the dozens of pastors who have died (and rabbis) since this scourge came to our shores, and then, if they continue to see it as a matter of faith, discuss “not tempting the Lord they God…” Finally, ask them, WHY DO YOU WEAR SEATBELTS? See if that can stimulate logical self-care and remind them that their faith is nothing if they are dead.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: When a vaccine is available for Covid-19, will you be comfortable enough to get it? What would your reason be for not wanting it?
Answer: The last time I was seriously ill with a contagious disease was in Fall 1993; it was some sort of flu, and the coughing was horrendous. I sat on the floor in my bedroom, trying to decide between calling the ambulance or chancing dying, the coughing was so bad, it seemed my lungs were closing right up. I was praying like crazy, and it was either this stops or I have to call an ambulance. OMGosh I was fearful, for sure. And all of a sudden, it stopped. I wasn’t all the way well, but that coughing stopped. Today, 26 and a half years later, I sit being para-symptomatic… where I “think” I may have “caught” “it;” where my throat or lungs “just don’t feel right,” or maybe I’m slightly hot, or whatever! I have never relied on the flu vaccine to not get the flu; but I have always been careful to keep my distance from other shoppers at grocery stores, and other places where folks congregate during flu season. So, while I may have skipped the flu vaccine from time to time, if the scientists come up with a vaccine for this bug, tell me when and where and I’ll be there. The risks of the downside of this bug are just to severe, uncontrolled as of yet by any therapeutic process in a reliable manner, so to me it will be quite well worth it. Meanwhile, I’m masking up and staying home and bugging my essential worker roommate to take off his shoes and clothes at the door to have them sanitized while he jumps in the shower. It isn’t over yet, and I do not want to become a proverb of being unwilling to suffer a little to avoid all this plague’s disastrous potential. It is nice, however, to think of a time when we will no longer have anything to fear about SARS2. Thinking ahead to a vaccine helped me do that tonight, so thank you, Perry, for including me in your A2A.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How do I tell my parents that something is difficult?
Answer: Ask them advice. Let them figure out you’re having trouble by asking them advice for situations similar to what you are facing. Do it in a way (if you take time to think about it I bet you can figure out how to do this..) where they won’t minimize your issue; if it’s about friends, ask them about their experience with people in the same situation. Make the example you ask about not directly in line with your situation, and just draw on their wisdom. Later, they may wonder if you are going through something and they may want to add some input to what they said. Then, ideally, they will ask you how you are. Make it a light message, if you want them to treat you like an equal. If you are seriously concerned about your mental or emotional state, please don’t ever hesitate to call 911 or a suicide prevention number serving your area. Most things work themselves out over time, and generally speaking, if we pay a little bit of attention, we all learn to do better over time.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Would you return to church if social distancing guidelines were in place?
Answer: My personal belief is that, spiritually speaking, the church and its adherents are being asked to draw closer to Jesus in all aspects of their individual and corporate walks during this time period. The very first thing that means, in my opinion, is leading the example when it comes to Wisdom as to how to best meet the challenges inherent in these Co-Vid 19 times. The EASIEST thing in the world to do is to not meet; the second easiest thing to do is to wear a mask, out of respect, even if you’re sure you can’t get it, don’t have it, will never have it, are cooler than mint chip iced cream on a hot August day. To me, it is foolhardy to brandish one’s faith in Christ by insisting that everyone around you be as big and bold as you are, and gather as though there is not serious threat to human life, and to be as cozy with one another as always. That is NOT the “message” I am getting. The message I am getting is about taking things MORE seriously, not frivolously; be MORE diligent, not less. The answer to your question from me, is no, I will not be going back to church until Co-Vid 19 is over, or until the church shows itself a worthy workman, putting its shoulder to the wheel of helping all, not just themselves. I am not hostile toward the church, but I am in COMPLETE disbelief of the lack of caring towards the larger body to not be as careful and cautious as possible. Their prejudice in favor of President Trump and their lack of logic in how their worldview is built (speaking of those who are flaunting their illogic in the face of this pandemic) may well lead to some disturbing results; I hope I am wrong.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: I've been disowned over money my dad stole from a bank account. At this point, I just want an outsiders opinion on what all is going on and maybe advice?
Answer: It depends: One, is the reason you were disowned is because you still love your father and are maintaining a relationship with him? If so, keep loving your dad and grow into becoming a peace maker. Building bridges is not about making one side of the bride into the other side; it is about helping EACH side decide upon what terms they are willing to be connected. If your father has an addiction or drinking problem, or other serious problems, other than highly unusual, circumstances of stress that contributed to your father’s illegal activity, your dad’s will is being controlled by forces larger than himself; so he is a danger to everyone. That will make your “job” harder; and you will not want to let your father destroy your life, because, then how could you ever help him to grow and become a better person like you want him to be? Two, if the other people involved in this are completely unwilling to see you as a separate person from your father, you will need to wait to have a relationship with them until they have grown up a little bit. No one else can tell us who to love or why; that is our own free will and others must accept our choices on at least some level. Good luck!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What do you think of this situation? What should I do about it? See link or comment for details.
Answer: Thanks for the A2A, it’s a nice “distraction” from the frustration of things bubbling up from just under the surface of my conscious mind. You have a complicated thing to sort out. I think the shortest path to victory here is to subtract the entire issue and preoccupation with the thing that seems to bother you the most - your friend’s seemingly messed up, and certainly complicated and confused way of dealing with a romantic relationship that seems to hurt him. If you would set aside this issue, and then just think about him without her in the picture. Without his confused thinking and wavering. What is it that you actually really like about your friend? What got you to be friends in the first place? Who is he, apart from his affair? Make your analysis simple. Subtract not just his weird behavior and emotional status due to the partner, but also the unfair “investment” of time and emotional energy that this whole relationship of his has taken from you. Do you like him? Do you respect him? Did you ever? Or did you once, and he has so morphed into something else that you just don’t enjoy him anymore? Or, can you enjoy him on your own terms for a time? Agree to never talk about the relationship and just go and have fun again, based on what you actually have in common… It is nearly impossible to spend much time with someone who is “co-dependently” involved with another person. It would seem that the co-dependence blankets the other person’s personality… like they’re no longer there! I would recommend taking a break from your friend for three to six months… Just seriously, go no-contact, and see if you don’t end up happier than when you’re trying to connect with someone who might be cutting themselves off from the world because of an “addictive” relationship. Then, at the end of your break time, THEN evaluate, what do you want to carry forward into the future with you? Remember, you can’t “force” him to value you on your terms; and he probably, at this point, can’t, or doesn’t care to, mold himself into what is acceptable to you or anyone else. Move on a bit. Your life and time are important; don’t let anybody steal it from you; there is NO payback for that at all! Treat yourself like you are valuable, because you are.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are people getting more aggressive because of the quarantine?
Answer: Subconscious material, conflicts, are bubbling up to the surface, with less and less to distract us. A distraction only lasts a little while… Then one must have a new distraction, at least for a little while; after nearly 120 days of rotating through such “distractions,” it is impossible for most of us to keep that subconscious stuff buried, and with no normal outlets to let off steam and then process, some of us might be getting a little bit more than on edge. And, for those individuals or groups of individuals, or community of individuals who practice repression as a chief way of coping with unpleasant realities, they (or we) may be most apt to “have” more anger than others. Sound familiar? It is DEFINITELY what I am dealing with. And it’s frustrating. Thanks for the A2A. Stay safe, keep wearing those masks!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: I know that watching adult films is wrong and I want to repent when I’m 30. Can I repent still in the future or will I already lose my ability to repent?
Answer: Sin has consequences; the wages, an old piece of writing says, of sin are death. How can that be, some ask, not having sinned so badly that they felt they were The Walking Dead, at least on the inside if not yet on the outside? Sin singes the conscience; a human conscience that is not functioning properly loses its ability to warn its owner of danger. Therefore, sometimes, sin patterns literally lead to not just a “spiritual” or “soul” death, or to the death of a marriage, or the abortion of a child, or the abandonment of a dream, but to death itself. Driving drunk over and over again is an example of how this pattern of behavior can lead one to murder and/or suicide by virtue of being possessed at the critical moment (when the headlights are in front of you and you have only a split second to call out to God to save you or to make the right move with your hands on that steering wheel) that has robbed you of all choice in the matter. A prior version of this question stated that the asker was not “saved,” meaning they lack a relationship with Jesus Christ. Perhaps this is the sin pattern that will result in you calling out to God with all your everything to “save” you from this death-producing behavior of programming your mind to tear apart the wholeness that is the great thing behind the union between male and female, between wife and husband, perhaps this very unclean thing will get you running from ALL those conditions that precede your pursuit of it and TOWARD Christ who can provide an alternative path from this point forward. If you are afraid, I would say, that is a good sign. Use the fear to blow the sails in your ship in the direction of solid ground. Get off the waves of the senses and self-absorption and into a BIGGER life. Waiting for some date in the future is merely a cheap, kindergarten gymnastic move to avoid facing your utter lack of both the desire to stop and the willingness to do anything to be free from it. Also, repent doesn’t just mean to stop sinning; it means to move TOWARD God, to turn your face BACK TO GOD, and WALK WITH HIM. This isn’t some phony, be better than everybody else thing, this is about literally walking with Him. Stop shutting him out. He’s the One that brings the light. He IS the Light. No one and nothing else is. HE IS THE GATE. GO THROUGH THE GATE.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Since Jesus has no sin, why didn't he throw the first stone?
Answer: Because people who love others don’t throw stones at them, period. It’s not about Jesus sinlessness, it is about the call of love.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What makes you scared or happy about your country returning to life as usual post the Coronavirus?
Answer: Business as usual, a frightful sight! God talks to us gently at first when trying to get our attention… A breezy whisper first, a feather’s touch next, a “hand” on your shoulder… then pebbles in your shoes, a rock in your path, a quick towel snap, a 1 x 2, uh oh, then a 2 x 4, then his “voice” just gets louder and louder. If we listen, and COURSE-CORRECT, everything gets good again; but THEN, if we do not, and we just keep on going like we were going, uh oh, both natural and divine consequences and events will take place. What do you think might be worse than Co-Vid 19? SARS 3??? Earthquakes? War? America, at least, needs to make some HUGE course corrections; if we do not, things cannot help but get worse. Business as usual is what I am seeing, and though most people are still acting and walking somewhat “timidly,” there’s no real direction for a more widespread and firm commitment to real change. And political parties do not have the answer either; and neither does the church, any part of it, at present, May 25, 2020. Business as usual, that is what I am sorry to see. Oh, and traffic! Yuck!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are you still attending church services even if you’re doing it digitally?
Answer: Yes, and no. The little church I was attending is meeting now, and I won’t be joining them until Co-Vid risks are drastically reduced, which means after the second wave that I think will come either in late Summer/early Fall, or a vaccine and miraculously wonderful protocols are worked through in the medical setting. During the time that the Colorado safe-at-home rules were in play, the little church did not hold online services, and I chose not to pursue any that did. I do something MUCH more fun, which is study everything I can get my ears to regarding what Ian Clayton, Son of Thunder (New Zealand HQ) has to offer. ZOOM meetings with them and fantastic info and practices to enhance one’s relationship with the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit…! Give him a try! Church will never be the same again! Try putting Ian Clayton You Tube into your Google search bar… the link isn’t live, or I’d do it for you. I’d go there and kick it with “Gateways.” SMILE!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What time is nap time, and for how long do you take a snooze break?
Answer: Funny you ask that. When I was visiting Open AA meetings in the late 1980’s, I went to a group that loosely based its hour-long discussions on a little AA book called Living Sober. It was full of practical suggestion for recovering alcoholics to use as part of their “tool box” for staying away from that FIRST drink. One day the topic was on getting adequate rest. As they went around the room sharing in their little circle, I was amazed at the number of people of all ages and all stages of life… like a 75-year old retiree, and a 37 year old telecom manager, and a young thing in her 20’s… took naps midday! They mentioned that no matter pretty much where they were or what they were doing, they found a way to take an hour for a quick lunch and a longer nap. Recent research I read backs that up: Exploring the nap paradox: are mid-day sleep bouts a friend or foe? Brains Sweep Themselves Clean Of Toxins During Sleep So, NAP AWAY. As for me, I am going to apply this advice daily, by taking a nap midday after a brief lunch. Thanks for the A2A and stay safe and well!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: My teenage daughter is refusing to work during quarantine so I took away her phone. When should I give it back?
Answer: You support her in her instincts around the Co-Vid 19 threat; the moment my son says he has had enough of WAL-Mart, which cares less about its employees than it does MONEY MONEY MONEY, he is FREE to quit… You support her; you don’t punish her. She’s scared, not just “willful,” or disobedient. Give her some space, but let her keep some old habits, or her inner tension will accelerate. Her having the phone is keeping fights with YOU down, as opposed to increasing. Her not working is showing you she is more than a little concerned. Be kind to her; try to bring her out a little bit; TRUST HER. This virus takes the young too.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: As a meat eater, how do you react when someone asks you why you eat meat?
Answer: Sometimes, a question is best left unanswered, but sometimes that is unavoidable. Perhaps answering a question with another question would work. Such a conversation might go like this: Why do you eat meat? Why do you ask? Because I believe animals have feelings. Why is that important? Because THEY FEEL THINGS. Like what do they feel? Everything, they feel everything WE DO! Like fear - they shudder and shake; Anger - they growl and snarl; Love - my dog licks my face to death and wags his butt like there’s no tomorrow when I get home. So, you don’t eat meat? No. Why not? Because animals have feelings. What about you? What? What do you feel? About what? How do you feel about your decision to not eat meat and then miss out on its iron, for building blood, and vitamin B, which is necessary for nervous strength that helps your entire body, and even taurine, which helps the muscle in your heart detox? I don’t know. I get all I need from other food sources. How do you know? I read. What do you read? Vegetarian Recipes and News From Vegetarians. How do you know what they say is true? Because they wouldn’t lie. Why not? I don’t know! Why are you bothering me? Who started this conversation? I did. Who’s bothering WHOM? I, I, uh, I guess me BUT YOU SHOULDN’T EAT ANIMALS. THEY HAVE FEELINGS!!! Well, maybe, but I have feelings too. Right now, I feel like I would like to bid you adieu and return to my very delicious, rare, filet mignon. Well, GOODBYE! Farewell!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: My friend says she's Christian but doesn't believe in God. Is this really Christianity?
Answer: What does she mean when she says that? I couldn’t possibly know unless you ask her, and I couldn’t possibly know how to intelligently answer your question without that information. Maybe it means she goes to church, thinks like Christians in most ways, and identifies with the values of the Christians she associates with through her family and her church. Or, maybe she just identifies with the thoughts Jesus expressed in his Sermon on the Mount - she likes his ideas. The more important point is how you, if she is a valued friend, are going to respond to her. If you are both young, say teenagers or in your early 20’s, this isn’t that abnormal to not have answered all the Big Life Questions. But, if you personally know Jesus Christ, and withhold interaction about Christ from her, for whatever reason, other than the Holy Spirit holding you back for the sake of God’s timing, then you might be missing a chance to help your friend improve her life for the rest of her life right here and now. Good luck, and I hope it all works out!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What little thing has this pandemic ensured you will never take for granted again?
Answer: The second item is what I would classify as the “small thing,” which is the main subject of this Quora question. But, there are a few others I desired to add, as, for me, this has been and still is, a very instructive time. I put them in order of importance to me.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Am I a bad person for not loving anything about my dad? He pays for almost everything, buys me things without me ever asking, but besides his monetary gestures, he's always been aggressive, controlling and lies compulsively. Am I being ungrateful?
Answer: Dear Asker, I sympathize with your dilemma, and with the fact that NOT being or feeling or expressing gratitude in some way toward your Father, or towards God or the Universe, makes you feel rather suspect of your own self! And that, of course, is the GREAT LIE of most exceptional manipulators, to get control over your self concept and how you feel, deep down inside, about yourself. Because if they control that, they truly have control of you, your feelings, your decisions, your thinking, your actions, and therefore, YOUR LIFE. So, I have a way out for you. Separate the terrible, sick burden that this person is putting on you through the heavy handed manipulation you always have to face, from THINGS. Your dad is his own person; he may be, probably is, under the influence of some super powerful forces.. from his memories, from how he was conditioned and brought up…. from the stresses currently in his life (including his own goals and thoughts about what it means to be a successful man and so forth). YOU GET TO BE YOUR OWN PERSON. Depending upon your age and freedom of movement (do you drive, are old enough to determine your own schedule, and so on), I would recommend immediately seeking the solace and wisdom of 12 Step Rooms like open meetings of Alcoholics Anonymous (avoid the groups that are run by controllers… there’s not many of those but sometimes you get a bad apple that runs roughshod over others) and its “sister” program, Al-Anon. While your dad may not be an actual “alcoholic,” I guarantee you you will get wisdom on how to protect yourself from manipulation and control by sitting in those rooms, say literally two or even three meetings a week (I went to 1,000 meetings of these and other 12 step rooms in three years and it changed totally my life forever for the better). It takes TIME to let another form of thinking other than manipulation and control (which is what has been your most prominent form of training in how to live life and how to manage your emotions and the emotions of others) to begin to seep through the clouds of being done under by the unfair and sometimes unscrupulous mental, verbal, and yea, financial, motives and abuse of a strong-willed person). The programs will help resurrect the parts of you that have been waylaid by the controller. I know it sounds time consuming, but how long, how many hours, days, YEARS, have you been under the influence of the wrong stuff? When you start to thaw out months from now, you will have a little bit of freedom to begin to meet YOU, the YOU without being controlled by a heavy handed person/personality. Don’t spend too much time analyzing Dad for now, or even ever. Once you get YOU back, once YOU are running your own show, THEN you can help Dad, if you want, to see a better way of life. Meanwhile, here’s the other key; BE GRATEFUL for EVERY blessing in your life. The material and the good stuff that comes from him… whatever is GOOD in your life, including what is good in you, focus on this A LOT, and it will become greater. It will multiply; the other will DRY UP. I promise. One, get OUT FROM UNDERNEATH THE BLANKET OF CONTROL; Two, ONCE YOU’RE BREATHING YOUR OWN AIR AGAIN, celebrate and learn about how wonderful you truly are. Good luck!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why are people so convinced that going to church in person is essential?
Answer: I’m afraid that I would have to conclude that many people who are convinced that going to church and assembling with others, many others, is “essential,” right now in particular, are hooked into an ego-based conviction, and not the conviction of the Holy Spirit (which is what SHOULD govern their decision-making), and that this ego-hook, if you will, is about proving their faith to the world. Now, many of these church-goers will also state that they are just trying to do what the Word of God says (Hebrews 10:25 King Jim version: “Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.”); In their minds, they are being obedient to a “Higher Authority,” and this too is a wind that serves to fluff their feathers in an effort to prove to themselves at least that they are diligent, sincere, real, Christian men and women. But, interestingly enough, when you feel your status in something is determinant upon what other people see and think about you, you have already lost the battle. Faith is OFTEN NOT what it looks like to others. In the most faithful act in history, except perhaps for agreeing to be born, Christ allowing himself to be put up on that Cross at Calvary, to MANY others, it looked like the work of a fool. After all, if you ARE GOD, why wouldn’t your first act on that cross be jumping down and slaying all the Roman guard around you and then pounding heat against the Sanhedrin that illegally arrested him and saw him punished for no sin whatsoever? But that was not the point. The point ISN’T POWER; if it was, then the world’s constant search, at great expense of human life and national treasuries, would have yielded the world’s best weapon, the way to be permanently secure from attack, and so forth. But that isn’t how history reveals the end of those futile missions, is it? If it isn’t, then what is the point of it all? The POINT is LOVE of course, but other “religions” propose kindness and other things akin to LOVE, AND THE POINT is to LIVE THE KINGDOM LIFE: REIGN FROM ABOVE. WALK ON THAT WATER. REACH OUT YOUR HAND AND HEAL THE SICK. Those things are not accomplished with an earthy mindset, they are accomplished when someone is beyond convinced of the temporal realities being subject to something far greater and that they too are called to subject the temporal world to themselves. These people do not allow themselves to be bound by compunction - by the “order” that comes up inside them to prove something, like that they love God and they will serve God, and they will be at church come hell or high water. Unfortunately, that is still legalism, and has no ability to give lift-off to the truth of the Word of God that came to set us free from entanglement with a hollow virtue that has a hollow ring of truth, but no power within. Diligence is NOT a substitute for relationship with God. Only God can be God in your life, not the bible, not a pastor, not your traditions, not rules, never compunction. Dying to self (including the need to STOP taking refuge or any self-satisfaction from these things) is not fun AND it takes a LOT of work to connect with all three persons of the trinity - with God - and it takes a LOT of work to clear out our stuff, to take every thought captive to Christ, and NO ONE else but YOU can do this work. NO ONE. Therefore, if you’re going to church to prove God’s will today, on Pentecost, and if you’re thinking you’re happily One With Your President, and it all feels good and right, know that there will yet be another football thrown into your end of the field, and you will have to get up again, grab that pigskin, and find a way to get it to the other end of the field. As for me and mine, we will serve the Lord; we will grind out the grist that is unacceptable to him; and we will not harbor illusions that “trying hard,” is what pleases God. He has made it clear, time and time again, what pleases God is FAITH.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: I live with my mother because of my parents divorce, but my big brother forces me to visit my father once a month, even though I don't want to because my father sometimes touches me which I don’t feel comfortable about. What can I do to avoid it?
Answer: Depends on what those “uncomfortable things” are. If he is deep in sin, lewd, crude, violating constantly, or drinking… these things… not so good for anyone to be around. I recommend a way to help yourself to carry out this simple act of honoring your father is to bring a friend or adult consistently with you. That may have the impact of helping your father, at least during your visiting time, to act or appear to act a little bit better. Then, too, it will give you some support. Combine it with an inexpensive meal out, or out-of-doors picnic til the threat of Co-Vid 19 wanes enough to warrant more risk, right after your visit with your Dad, with this other person… who should be compassionate, respectful, engaged in YOUR welfare, not in your dad’s or brother’s or anyone else’s; he or she is in this JUST FOR YOU. It is GOOD to honor one’s father, in pursuit of God’s joy and completion; and to remind your father you were given to him as a gift from God and a chance to glorify God in heaven. It is ALSO GOOD to honor God within you, who, probably like you, does not like these “uncomfortable things.” If your father or brother is not willing to allow you a good, mature, respectful friend to accompany you, they are playing games with you, and trying to entice you into a way of life that you have already rejected. If this is the case, then you split until sometime in the future, God opens up a better door. Good luck. This is suffering, and it is NOT your fault. Blessings to you for encouragement, and later, JOY. Joy comes in the MORNING. Your morning will come.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Can I do communion myself for me and my family?
Answer: OH GOD YES! YES! YES! YES! Just because Jesus showed us an example where it was “formal” and He was “administering” what many denominations call a “rite,” or ritual which is supposed to contain many sacred or most meaningful aspects of our Christian faith does not mean we can’t do this even alone. JESUS IS ABOUT RELATIONSHIP; CHRISTIANITY is about RIGHT relationship with God first, restored through the Hope of Glory, then turning outward to all others with grace and love at all times. Communion is a VERY important remembrance He instructed us to do OFTEN. OFTEN is NOT once a week. That would be called “weekly.” If you were told to eat OFTEN, and you ate once a week, would you not perish? Of course! So why do we wait for once a week, or worse in MANY churches, once month, once a quarter…. Whenever we think to…. ???? It’s atrocious how we avoid it. Communion is about getting ALL the brilliant miraculous powers and implications and revelation and earnestness possible at our command to internalize and then to live out of the incredible wonderful, time-surpassing, death-conquering GIFTS that God gave us through Yeshua’s incarnation, life, ministry, apprehension, unjust imprisonment, wickedly painful scourging, mocking, suffering, then his surrendering his life into the Father’s hands, then submitting and yielding to the marvelous divine process of resurrection! We can’t just read the bible and listen to others tell us how to think. We need to drive ourselves into the bosom of God and GET HIM to tell us MORE. To GIVE US MORE. TO TEACH US, MORE! Here are two who would have you do communion on your own (as well as corporately) as often as possible: Joseph Prince, (Singapore) New Creation Church, The Power Of The Holy Communion | Joseph Prince Ministries Ian Clayton, Son of Thunder ministries in New Zealand, teaching on the Blood and the Thorns at a local church 11 years ago. Ian, Friend of God.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How does your religion affect your life during the covid -19?
Answer: My relationship(s) with the Father (Yahweh), the Son (Yeshua) and Holy Spirit are being developed through the crucible of seeing and feeling the reactions my soul, body and re-born Spirit have been having to the entire phenomenon called Co-Vid 19, or SARS-Co-V2: The ancient bedding of an unreasonable, persistent suspicious nature that found a home in my imagination many years ago is being uprooted by the necessity to meet the ferocity of my fears with immediate action to reduce and to the best of my ability, eliminate them. For, otherwise, this fear might completely paralyze me. Now, first, it is important to notice that this is not about fear always being bad, in fact, fear is useful. Even as believers in Christ we are supposed to allow, yea, even embrace, the human emotion of fear in certain cases where the action such fear will prompt us to will indeed farther extend the boundaries from within which we shall be free of ALL fear: Don’t forget his benefits… the BLESSINGS of knowing and being in relationship with God. FEAR HIM, and embrace the Fear of the Lord, as it is the beginning of Wisdom. Have reasonable fear of things you know nothing about…like a chainsaw, for instance, as a good pastor told me he remembered to have almost a little too late: It hit him when he was nearly in the top of a tree in the forests of northern Arkansas near Hope, that NOT knowing anything about the tool he held in his hands and that was now whirring with power would have been ameliorated if he had remembered this sage advice BEFORE he climbed the tree with it. But, with respect to Corona Times, while a basic fear of physical potential of the virus for ourselves and others is good, fear is a wind that can whip the sail of one’s life into such a frenzy that it is ALL that one can think about. Thus, limiting the rational fear to a prompter of GOOD action is our first objective. For example, having read the tragic and alarming stories of people of all ages who, during this crises, have walked into a hospital alive but suffering, and then died within a few days to a few weeks brings up that awareness of death that most of us prefer to keep at bay. But it is a truth: At any one minute, we may be taking our last breath. This brings up two basic considerations: How will the people who depend upon us deal with our departure? Will they have the resources to meet it without it tanking their lives? Will there even be money to bury the dead? The other main consideration it brings up, on a personal level, at least for me, is, Oh my God, what have I done with my life and what can I do to change that record NOW, if anything? This consideration, which should be with many of us more often, is a valid, and can be a life-altering guidepost. What will my record be? Who have I helped? What difference have I made? And to be corny as heck, but it’s such a good way to put it, what songs or what music have I left unsung in me that needed to come out, that were put into me for a purpose, a reason, and a season? So, with respect to the fear of getting seriously sick, I myself have been crucifying that terror by going to God frequently and examining and declaring my need for Him; my utter, total, unabashed and unashamed dependence upon Him, for NOTHING puts me in a safer place than THAT PLACE, at His feet, under His wings, WITH HIM. Then, with respect to moving my life forward to yet have the right, through God’s approval and empowerment of me, His desire and actions to sustain even my physical being through more days, yea, decades of life, I labor, EARNESTLY, to turn that ship around. That’s hard to do; some of us give shelter to a lot of undesirable, heavy things that weigh us down, and to turn such a ship around, it’s hard; the rudder would break, if not for some favor granted us from on high, via the wind, the waves, the swells and squalls, and lack thereof. To wrap it up, my faith has been stirred by Co-Vid 19’s impact upon my soul, and upon my Spirit to grow in self-responsibility and in the awareness of other people’s needs.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: When in the Bible does Paul say that we are not bound to laws from the Old Testament? I saw this in my devotional (it was on a message about tattoos), but he didn’t say what verse it was.
Answer: Paul, quoted in Romans 6:14, reportedly said, “For sin shall not be master over you, for you are not under law but under grace.” People however need to remember who said this, and that He has greater standing in all ways than Paul: Matthew 5:18 “For verily I say unto you, Till. heaven and earth pass, one jot or one. tittle shall in no wise pass from. the law, till all be fulfilled.” So, if Jesus himself said NOT ONE JOT OR ONE TITTLE shall pass from the law until all be fulfilled, then let’s make some necessary effort to more completely understand what Paul means, assuming he didn’t forget or not know what Jesus said about the Law. Being “under” something means to be ruled by it; our compliance, Paul points out in the rest of Romans 6, is now of a higher order - it is that which is run by a conscience of righteousness, toward righteousness, and resulting in righteous thought and action. We now EXCEED the demands of the Law, thereby fully fulfilling it. Paul continues to explain the miracle of our transformation in his letter to the Galatians, 5:22–23, “22 But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, 23 gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no Law.” Therefore, if we are always, moved by love of God and powered by Holy Spirit and the very Power of God moving in our most inward parts, manifesting love, the law is fulfilled, not ignored. Remember, it is the Law whose power stopped at showing us where we were wrong, not providing a way out of our wrongness within and without: Romans 7: “Well then, am I suggesting that the law of God is sinful? Of course not! In fact, it was the law that showed me my sin. I would never have known that coveting is wrong if the law had not said, “You must not covet.” (New Living Translation) So we see here that after all, Paul’s “theology” does not differ from Christ’s, and we can gain great help by regarding his other reported statements that take place within these passages and others to help us clarify how we are to divide and apply his words, and The Word, to our daily lives.

Name: Sara Stone

Thank you for including me in your good question, and hope you stay safe and well.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: I've been an atheist my whole life. I'm a teenager and I want to read the Bible because I don't think it's fair to reject Christianity without trying it. Why am I so nervous to start reading the Bible?
Answer: It’s a big book! One version I have is 1253 pages long. That’s a lot of reading. So, the first thing that might make you nervous is how do you read that? I read a trilogy of books that were 650 pages each, one per weekend, but reading the bible, with so many things I don’t have first hand experience with… like the geography, the history, the language reflected in the names of groups of people and nations and so forth, it’s a lot to take in. So, the first thing I would do, regardless of whether or not the above is THE reason you are nervous, I’d break this project down into a couple of parts: One, the reading… I recommend you get a version you like, buy it, don’t just check it out of the library and get some colored pens to mark it up as you desire. Remember, you’re doing this for you, not for someone else, and it may be a “project” that ends up giving you more questions than answers - that’s okay, again, this is for you, and you have nothing to prove. The second most common reason someone might be nervous about reading the bible or giving Christ a chance is the fear of the unknown. You are admitting you don’t know enough to feel that you can entirely reject this kettle of fish, so, you are going to be walking into unfamiliar territory. So, perhaps treating it like an adventure and keeping a small journal that you might write a line or two or three at most at the end of the day about how what you read in the bible that day impacted you or made you think… Then, regardless of how this adventure turns out, you could have something to refer to later that would be at least, fun, as it would provide a “snapshot” of how you were when you did this great experiment. May I also recommend a series of videos a guy made about his journey away from Christ exploring everything under the son and what he discovered? I found it interesting. Here is it, hope you like it and good luck on your studies: Nathan Wheeler’s truthmefree. He’s even got a video on how to study the bible too. (oh, BTW, may I URGE YOU, don’t take all the comments you’re going to get from friends and family about your project or our thoughts too seriously, just try to remember, this is YOUR trip, not theirs; YOUR opinion is what you should value the most. Good luck!)

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Should I worry that I actually personally like the quarantine, besides all the economical problems?
Answer: Oh, no, you should not worry, Giorgio. The unusual circumstances surrounding Co-Vid 19 provide a window to the things our souls are longing for: A less rushed pace; a more-human centered, and animal/planet-friendly framework for the structuring of our time and efforts, quality, not quantity. Facts being what they are, if we don’t change, we are done for. So, don’t worry, be happy!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What would you do if you found out your spouse was hoarding $20k that you didn’t know about? And during that time, whenever you asked for child care help or anything else that could give you relief because you were depressed, he claimed he had no $?
Answer: PRAISE, PRAISE, PRAISE, PRAISE THIS SPOUSE for being so SMART, disciplined, self-sacrificing and for not letting you break down their commitment to a very decent, loving, incredibly helpful thing to do. Name: Sara Stone
Question: My parents might be worried, or even worse, depressed because of the pandemic. They haven't been themselves recently. What should I do to calm them down?
Answer: Do what my son does with me: Regularly remind them that many people who have all the known risks for complications or lasting injury or even death from Co-Vid 19 never catch it, and if they do, are handling it at home with patience and communication with their doctors. Remind them how many people ARE NOT SICK, and how many people are recovering. Remind them that every case the doctors and hospitals DO deal with, is one more piece of the puzzle, and is gradually helping the doctors develop better ways to treat each individual who ends up struggling with this virus. Ask them is there are things that they feel need to be done, right away, in case they had to go into the hospital suddenly. Essentially, are their affairs in order? Life insurance? Wills? Medical directives? Help them talk about what is bothering them. You didn’t mention how old they are or how fit at this point in time. If they are fit at all, make sure they are getting out for walk on a daily basis if possible. This helps oxygenate their blood, which helps the mind not dwell and not fear so much. Find out if you could look at some old pictures with them and stop by and spend and hour or two, if you’re nearby. Make sure they’re not alone in that house or apartment all day long! That will drive anybody nuts, Co-Vid or not. Send them flowers and make them some food; offer to help clean the garage or attic; make sure they’re okay financially and not actually falling behind in bills. Use your intuition about what’s just under the surface and see if you can help them admit it to themselves what exactly are they afraid of. People may say they’re afraid of dying, and who isn’t, but what if they DID die? What would they be leaving behind undone, or unforgiven, or unsaid? See if you can help them tie up those loose ends, then, Co-Vid tragedy or not, they will be walking more freely and joyfully afterwards.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: When you describe what you are feeling like, in this pandemic, going through isolation/quarantine, what do you say?
Answer: Thank you for this ask, Donna. The first word that comes to mind when describing what I am feeling like in this pandemic, going through isolation/quarantine, is WEIRD. It is WEIRD because it is truly unlike anything else I’ve ever gone through before. It is WEIRD to see the streets empty; all the businesses and restaurants closed; it is WEIRD to listen to news reports which make no sense; announcements of one policy in New York, and totally different policies in Texas; it is WEIRD to try to connect the dots to why THIS TIME would be the time NRA puppets would storm the state capital of Michigan and tell everyone they got rights; it is WEIRD to not even hug your adult son when he comes home from his “essential” job at WAL-Mart because both of us are aware of certain risk factors and how MANY things are completely NOT under the control of management at WAL-Mart that are related to the possibility of spreading this virus. Not seeing a lot of other people right now (no thank you, local church, I am NOT interested in “Opening Up Those Church Doors” right yet, I am noticing some throw-backs to missing people who died a long time ago… my mom in 1980, for instance, my dad in 2005. It’s like some of the more important losses in my life are competing for attention again. Clearly, the isolation and lack of contact is making me think of those who have been the closest to me. So, the feeling, the description, is WEIRD. It’s weird that our government has lost its ability to work for the people; it’s WEIRD that so many people don’t give a damn, or didn’t get the memo about masks and other methods to help prevent the spread of something that kills some people some of the time; it’s WEIRD that so many people, usually Republicans, think this is all made up… It’s like, What Are You Eating To Make You So Crazy???? It’s WEIRD AND SUBLIMELY beautiful to see dolphins and alligators in the channels in Venice Italy, and other wild things moving through delightfully barren downtown city streets. It’s SUPER WEIRD (and wonderful, and illuminating, and inspiring, and hope-filled) to see so many different professional in the scientific and business fields work across national lines to come up with answers… this is truly one of the best things in this time period, along with seeing animals feeling safe. It’s just, all in all, pretty darn WEIRD. Yup, that sums it up for me in a word: WEIRD!!!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Has the COVID-19 lockdown been kind or cruel to your waistline? Can you elaborate?
Answer: When it all started, I had been going down, but then I went up. And up. And then got a grip, and took those pounds off… I began walking, 10 minutes slowly, then 20, about four times a week, then after about six weeks, got up to 40 minutes, walking 25% of those minutes in a brisk way, then, as I am wont to do, I over did…. And the past two days could hardly do anything. One more day of rest and I’ll get back on that horse that knows how to stay at a trot, thank you very much. Health is a gift well worth taking good care of; Co-Vid 19 has made me very aware of how important my weight loss and cardio conditioning are to my overall health and welfare, and to controlling many risks, including the risk of being done-in or severely damaged by Co-Vid or some similar viral threat in the future. Thanks for the ask, Don. Keep that mask on!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Is a daily nap during quarantine going to have benefits, or is it bad for you?
Answer: A daily mid-day nap, after lunch, us HIGHLY recommended by many, including brain specialists who say the brain likes a rest half way through the day to perform an internal clean-out… a “sweep” if you will, of useful and non-useful material, and an incorporation of new info that is desired into a proper place within its rows and rows of data and experience. So, like during non-pandemic time periods, a short, say 40 minute nap after lunch, is a great idea. Glad you mentioned it! Stay safe; wear a mask; save a life!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why is there silence on the tragic journey of migrant workers in India after the Coronavirus lockdown?

What you are referring to is certainly a tragedy, of huge proportions, in terms of the impact on the number of people in this situation in India. There are many things going on around this world that are not being brought up to the surface, or at least they don’t stay there for very long, because of the incredibly tense and natural focus on one’s own safety… everything keeps most of us coming back to our own personal lives. How do I pay my rent with no hours? Whom did I last have contact with at the doctor’s office and are they still Co-Vid free? As a United States of America citizen, I am doing my best by trying to get myself healthier and not get sick; and get along with my adult son roommate… That’s about all I can handle. The delivery of appropriate goods and services to meet the Co-Vid 19 threat to lives and to the permanent quality of lives of those who survive their experience with the virus, this is complex and is taking time to evolve in the U. S. And we are only 1/4 the size in terms of population that India is! And, that population is running around in more than THREE TIMES the number of square miles that India has. This so utterly compounds the equation of the sheer volume of details and human acts that must take place to meet the challenges and suggested protocols for dealing with Co-Vid that enhances the chances of survival and that decreases rates of transmission that it is MIND boggling. It’s a horror story, what is happening with the migrant workers there. There is no easy answer. There is no clear way out. And how can I contribute, even sentimentally, to this situation, there, 7,500 miles away from me, when my own life and that of my son’s seems to hang in the balance of how this Co-Vid threat continues to develop over here? Here are some articles, in case anyone would like to, for a moment, take their mind off their own problems: As migrant workers struggle for lockdown aid, India seeks to count them India: Migrant workers' plight prompts UN call for ‘domestic solidarity’ in coronavirus battle The Pandemic Exposes India’s Apathy Toward Migrant Workers Migrant Workers in India May Shun Cities After Lockdown Thank you again for including me in this ASK, and please, stay alive.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the most poignant moment you've experienced since the pandemic lockdown started in your area? What made it bittersweet?
Answer: Thank you, Don, for including me in this question about Co-Vid 19. I supposed the most poignant moment I’ve experienced was when “it” got real close to me… much different, of course, than for people who are health care providers, or for people who have had loved ones or family suffer from this disease, or be tragically cut down by it. It was when I found out that a friend of mine had a sibling who works in a hospital. It just put everything in a different light; made it come closer to home. I was already aware of the threat and taking my own precautions, but this increased my awareness of another part of the world that was having to change their entire lives as well in the midst of being surrounded by the threat of Co-Vid 19. This made the whole thing more serious for me, I suppose. More real. That was the “bitter” part; the “sweet” part is that I love anything that makes me more aware, that makes me think, that calls me to be careful… So much in our society is based on shallow interactions, even our hygiene, at least mine, has needed a tune up, and this darn scourge is bringing that. THAT part of this monster’s impact is very good, and I desire correction, so that is the “sweet” part. Thanks again, and stay well everybody! Wear a good mask, save a life.

Question: What are you going to do once quarantine is lifted, and social distancing is done?
Answer: Thank you for including me in your quest for answers! Hope you and yours stay safe and well throughout the coming weeks and months til this thing is tackled! My list of what I am going to do once the threat of death or organ damage or the threat of giving this vehicle of the messenger of death to someone else is over, is not do’s, but rather NEVER AGAIN WILL I…. Name: Sara Stone
Question: What things will you miss when quarantine ends?
Answer: Nothing… at least in how my personal world has been restructured, I will miss nothing. I’ve learned my lessons, I’m taking them with me, and I am anxious to get out of this box. The good habits that have been birthed or resurrected - the walks in the park to get the heck out of fear; participation in a fallen but seemingly necessary medical system; more structured time with my higher power; a stern look at my destructive ways of trying to force issues, and other parts of myself that do no one, including me, any good; the organization of my home to sufficient degree that cleaning and even, yea, even disinfecting, can take place on a regular basis - these habits I will retain. But with respect to how the greater world around is functioning, there are several things I do not want to see go: When Co-Vid 19 is corralled and its more devastating features ameliorated, this time of social distancing, this near stoppage of business as usual, perhaps it will have worked out sufficient change within enough people, that the “we” on the Earth, will rise up, and the over inflated, unhumble “theys” will go away, for good. Sounds like I need to take a walk again. Thanks for including me in your question, Wayne. Wear a mask, safe a life!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why are so many people experiencing anger during quarantine?
Answer: This time period is one of the oddest times periods the American public has experienced, and surely it is also one of the oddest times for every society and nation who has been reached by the news of this virus that yet contains so many secrets. Wouldn’t you think that most of the anger, that is to say the personal anger, people are feeling is due to the tension caused by “no way out?” There’s no “deadline” on this threat to our lives… No real ability to predict when we will, at least for the most part, be “out of the woods,” and these are woods we never realized, back in January, for most of us, that we were wandering into, right as the sun was about to set on our normal way of life. For how long? We just don’t know. This uncertainty leaves us without brackets or boundaries for what regular and routine activities we were participating in up until this last quarter; we have no “borders” around our hours. We can’t really even “transition,” because there’s no shore on the other side of this ocean of the unknown, the unmanageable, the unconquered demand on our faculties. And, boy, would we rather just be done with it! Kill the thing already! Get rid of it! The anxiety! The purposelessness! My defects of character! Uh, I mean, that darned virus thing… We’re face to face with the worst of all monsters in the dark, I’d venture to say. We’ve come round about to ourselves, and perhaps we just haven’t kept up with the unpacking that we should have been doing all along, some of us for years, of our subconscious junk that piles up - the let downs, the fears, the abandoned dreams and deadlines. But now, there they are, looming, leaping, lapping at the fine white sand of our unconscious, our subconscious, and breaking through the all too well, veneered layers of our best defense patterns. Interesting, isn’t it? Looking into infinity with no one to hold us back from seeing what’s just right under the surface… We’re ill at ease; not sure what’s next, can’t piece together a short-, or long-term plan. Can’t make plans with others. No poker games, dance halls, dinners out, races against the clock for special projects at work. Nowhere to show off, to show up, to trade, to make noise, to grab, prod, poke our fellow man. And it’s well nigh driving us nuts. We’re like a squirrel in a cage who hasn’t seen a nut for 10 days. Round and round on that spinning wheel of a brain that refuses to stop even though, or maybe just because it has NOTHING to do. Therefore, instead of pausing, deepening, sweeping house in that rat trap of a mind of ours that’s so overrun with the thready weeds of unnecessary action, thought, delay, purchase, creation, muse, letter, post, tweet, we run, to something, something to give ourselves familiar structure, a rail for our senses to hang onto… But somehow, the comfort we expect, it isn’t there… we’re still bothered, we could still… Tomorrow, tonight, the next day, run into a fever, a sore throat, a cough? Will it happen to me? To you? To someone we love? THEN WHAT DO WE DO, THEN WHAT??? THAT’S why we’re angry. We don’t like THAT outcome, THAT maybe, THAT possibility. Even though it’s always been true, everyday of our lives, that the next breath could be our very last, THIS IS SOMEHOW DIFFERENT. It’s like the gambler’s dilemma… He THINKS he has a chance, but he has to play his “odds” right… watch the other players, not look to nervous, be slick enough to make his play, but not so smart he gets kicked out. He’s got faith, style, savior faire, but is it the right time? Does he take the roll now? The next card? Pull the handle? Chalk the cue stick? Kiss the girl? Tension is a form of stress that, when continuous, builds up over time, and right about now, May 15, 2020, we’ve been playing THIS game, in OUR neighborhood, for nearly 90 days. That’s a LONG time. It’s not bombs bursting in air, or drones overhead, but then again if it WERE, at least we could RUN and delight ourselves for a few minutes in escaping THAT swing of the enemy’ fist. This OTHER enemy, this SARS-2 thing, it’s got us under a bell jar, until God or Science, or both of them, make their minds up about letting us out to BREATHE AGAIN!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How is home quarantine responsible for stress in mental health and personal relationships?
Answer: Stress is pressure - change brings pressure to our minds and bodies. We are being stressed to think about something we usually avoid: Death. Depending on one’s age and physical condition, it can cross our minds against the background of this Co-Vid 19 threat everyday, every hour, or just when we have a cough out of nowhere or even a “minor” sore throat. Because with this particular threat to mankind, everything can go from minor to major real quickly. Personal relationships with the family can be strained because we “see too much of each other,” or because, as in my case, we have an “essential worker,” in the house who is fearful that he is going to bring something home and get his mom sick, or himself. So he comes straight in and goes to his room, every night. And he avoids me in the morning as well. Last night I told him how fearful I was becoming… that he’s all I got, which is true in terms of family connections here in Colorado. He opened up that he doesn’t know what to do about anything… his job, which he wants to leave, because WAL-Mart does NOT enforce mask wearing of its employees, because WAL-Mart WOULD rather lose a few employees than any customer whatsoever, and because it’s a dead-end job. But he doesn’t want to risk losing our major source of income. He’s worried about the car we got - the loan payment and the insurance and the costs, as I was job hunting before Co-Vid and should have had income by now, but instead I’m still on a small stipend from the state of Colorado. He’s worried about where we live, as the landlord has trespassed and we are unsure of how deep this man’s “stuff’ goes… Should he/we move? So, we clam up to protect others and to minimize stress and conflict, and then become highly pressurized on the inside…. bad combo. Add to that the emotional stress caused by worrying about loss, losing one’s life, or one another. It is very scary and is super hard to bear alone. That’s why, I think, there’s so much stress at home during Co-Vid 19. It’s sad. I hate it. I was all up for a “challenge,” and using this time to seek God, and that IS a good approach, at all times. But, I hate having to consider the potential heartbreak. I hate to think about it, but it comes up and I just have to get it out and give it to God and keep trying to move forward. Thanks for including me in this A2A… I’m afraid my response won’t be the most stalwart or resilient one. Stay safe, wear a mask, save a life!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are you currently sequestered in your home, and are you apprehensive?
Answer: Thank you for inviting me to participate in the Quora chorus on your question, Jim. Hope you and yours are safe and well. While I am not forcefully sequestered, I am home alone quite a bit, and indeed I am apprehensive. The tendrils of the Co-Vid 19 fear monster do invade, what with a lack of resources preventing my son, who is an “essential” worker at WAL-Mart, and me from just packing up and choosing to live in the beautiful Rocky Mountains for a few months or a year or 18 months or whatever this thing takes…. A lack of choices allows those tendrils to come up and choke me around my neck every so often with an unallowable fear because you don’t want your adult son who already helps his mom out a lot to be more scared than he is of bringing home something from a place filled with customers who fail to wear masks and co-workers who cut holes in theirs so that they “can breathe more easily.” Oy vey. Gimme a flippin’ break. So yes, I am apprehensive, though most of my focus is on responding to the fear in ways that can let both my son and me move forward throughout the crisis and after. First, about eight weeks ago, I realized how nervous, fearful, uptight I was getting… I was walking in my neighborhood and running errands, but that was about it. I decided to get out of the neighborhood and walk in a national park that is historic and beautiful on a nearly daily basis. The park is large… miles long, connects many parts of the west side of Colorado Springs together and even connects to downtown and my alma mater, Colorado College. Every walk can be an exploration. Choosing to spend the time and the gas money to go and soak up the atmosphere of this bigger-than-you-or-me place has lifted my eyes, and my spirits, up. And physically, I can attest to it also working wonders: It’s raised my heart rate on a daily basis, it has eliminated the pain that was keeping me awake on the sides of my upper legs and on one ankle completely,, and fortunately, it also eliminated anxiety I felt about my breathing by making it more regular. As to mood, I’ve had only one 90-minute downturn in mood since I turned over this new leaf, whereas before, it was an almost daily thing. The Co-Vid Fear Attacks also led me to be serious about getting good medical help. I had my first consult with a physician in close to 20 years about a month ago, then got blood pulled for cardio and overall functioning; then had another phone consult to go over that blood work; then set up and had a very brief EKG; then got more blood pulled to look at absorption of nutrients, and last night did an ox test where I think those oxygen sat rates dropping to the 80s from time to time might just warrant getting some oxygen pumped into my system via a CPAP hose. I’m hoping they can find me the elephant trunk version, not the whole hockey mask thing. Having seen some of the ox numbers in the night provided great insight as to why several things have not been working for a long time. Anyway, all this is to say, for anyone who has read this much boring detail already, the very personal ways in which the Co-Vid 19 Threat has touched me has forced me to engage with more realism and take MANY more steps forward in my personal life than I have in AGES. And for that, I am very grateful. Thank you again, Mr. Killeen. Wear a mask, save someone’s life.

Question: How accurate is the U. S. Covid-19 death toll?
Answer: Not very. The only people getting tested until recently were people who were in the middle of extreme illness and those are the ones who have often, unfortunately, and tragically for their family and loved ones, passed away. That means for anyone who did not know they had Co-Vid or who do not have access to health care providers, or anyone who was under someone else’s care like a nursing home, or anyone who had it, but didn’t know it, but presented to Emergency as a heart attack or organ failure actually caused by Co-Vid but either never autopsied for it, all these deaths have not been counted. Apparently, when the number of deaths of H1N1 were estimated by the CDC during 2009*, there were the same worries, that not all the deaths were being caught or counted. A, shall we say, “more robust” figure was reported in 2013 to the tune of 7 to 10 times the original number. If that is any good guideline, it means more than a half million United States citizens and residents have died from Co-Vid 19 so far. *2009 Swine-Flu Death Toll 10 Times Higher Than Thought

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is holding up COVID-19 testing in the U.S.?
Answer: Mayor Cuomo’s daily reports have been interesting to take in. He puts forth logical explanations for things the public isn’t all that tuned into. For instance, when it comes to test kits, (and ventilators) as he said, more or less, we’re asking manufacturing companies that are used to, say, supplying 1,000 test kits per month to go to 10,000 or more per month. This puts pressure not just on that company’s natural resources (their employees), but on their suppliers as well. And some of these suppliers, Cuomo recently pointed out, are in other countries, which complicates both timelines and availability of those companies to be able to fulfill the new, larger orders. Recently, the State of Colorado purchased 120,000 Co-Vid 19 test kits that test the presence of the virus in people via nasal swab from South Korea’s tech giant, SolGent. The test I took recently was one of those. Thankfully, my test came back negative. But it was amazing to me that I was the ONLY person in line at that drive through testing site. I thought every one was anxiously awaiting the chance to get tested… of course, most asymptomatic people aren’t going to take the time on their own, I suppose, to go get one done. At any rate, the logistical reason for a lack of testing kits is the ramp up time it takes for manufacturers and labs to reorient themselves to a new, much much larger demand. The political reasons? Well, that’s for another author to address. Thanks for inviting me in on this question of yours and I hope you and your loved ones are safe from this very difficult pandemic.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: My 35 yr old sister has to have cemo during Covid 19. She lives 2 hours away and can't leave her hse for the 3 mths of treatment due to the virus. Has anyone any ideas how I can cheer her up and support her without be able to spend time with her?
Answer: Wow. I am sorry for your sister’s sake, both that the best medical practices around her illness requires chemo right now, and that Co-Vid 19 measures to protect her compromised health mean that she will be isolated right when she could use a hug, a kiss, and an arm around her, as well as companionship to pass the time. You could plan a few visits to her… and “social distance” by singing to her from several feet away from her window… bring balloons and dress up like a fool and dance just for her. The two of you will never forget it. You could also give if your budget allows it a few unusual gifts: A hundred flowers… of your choice; a gift certificate for a ride in a balloon, attached to, of course, a hundred balloons. Cards, specially good crackers to help her over those times when she is not going to feel like eating, and organic applesauce if she likes that. A BIG card that has to be special delivery, signed by a hundred survivors of cancer - if that is what she has. You could pay three months of internet for her… if that kind of help would be appreciated and set up some family sing-a-longs, or even “fake” campfires, via ZOOM or some other internet medium to help all of you not feel so far away from one another. You could ask her what are her greatest fears, if she wants to tell you. You could send her a pink rose, just a single one, and tell her that is what your life is like not being able to see her right now - still nice, but very lonely. You can tell her you’ll miss her more because she’ll have her disease and its treatment to deal with, but you’ll only have your own boring life (even though, I am sure, your life is not boring, but you probably get my drift). You could ask her if she would like you to help her keep a daily journal of her journey during this time period… you could scribe it for her with a daily or nearly daily call each of the 90 days. You could then look for photographs of beautiful and interesting things, even things she might suggest, to go with her descriptions of what this whole thing is like. You could take some friends or family and all of you sleep on her lawn if she has a house, or around her apartment somehow, even though distant, what a treat it would be to know someone is there, just for you. Anything you do will be appreciated, but if you can afford the time, I think it might be quite helpful for you to take on one hour of every day to be there for her, so that she knows that one hour, she has somebody all for herself… You are so kind to want to help your sister, I hope the many suggestions you get here will help you provide a trampoline of support that will bounce her right back up on her feet. Oh, another thing. When we get weak and tired and worry and sore and nauseous, we don’t advocate, clean house, cook, or pay bills very well; so if she doesn’t have someone with her who will be doing that, perhaps you can develop a game plan for her and maybe even help her watch her accounts online to get everything done. Good luck. You are a good sister.
