Question: Should charity continue to be a State issue or should it go back to being a person to person situation? I.e. govt funded food stamps vs. donation supported food banks
Answer: The only reason the USA does not have widespread chaos (more than it already has), violence (more than it already has), crime (more than it already has), hunger (more than it already has - please note, when my now-25 year old son was in grade school, fully 1/3 of the children in the county we live in, where the United States Air Force Academy is located, were classified as “hungry.” This classification was not based on the number of people who received Food Stamps, but by how many children were exhibiting characteristics of hunger… low weight, inability to sustain interest and effort, and so on), rampant disrespect for ALL kinds of authority (more than it already has), and finally revolution is because of food stamps and other governmental aide. And heck, according to this “conservative,” “born-again Christian,” Republican administration, Big Business needs more charity than the poor folk to stay afloat. This does not, however, answer your question, for your question is a question related to ethics, morality, philosophy, religion, and political theory. The most common element of statehood (speaking, nations here…being a nation-state) across the globe is a coming together in order to have a common defense against intruders, invaders, attackers. Without borders, there is no country (typically, setting aside islands and territories for now). AFTER that comes everything else. The people in such a nation state may not originally gather for that purpose, but they increasingly become defined by this ability to survive as a unit under those original geographical boundaries. This is certainly true of the United States of America. Setting aside First Peoples for now, as well as excursions by my ancestors, the Vikings, to possibly as far south as New Brunswick, Canada,* and recognizing that what brought the “invaders” to the Americas was the rampant appetite for gold and other riches, the actual organization of the initiative for the creation of these United States was found in the hearts and minds of educated men who delighted in the bold new ideas of the Enlightenment and who idealized self-government as the best kind of government of all. Whether this idea, of a new country, a new TYPE of country, sans royalty, sans too much pomp and circumstance, could self-replicate has been the lost pursuit of a nation of citizens whose majority now can hardly recite basic American (US American) prayers, historical essays, speeches and documents, without consulting Google. Today, I believe Food Stamps, which are not “charity” from the government, but are stipends from the government, which is made up of CITIZENS, for the citizens, as part of a chosen public policy that values, for whatever reason, feeding its poor, its aged, its ill, its young, its very most vulnerable, are helpful to all of us. This form of support did NOT take the place of charitable donations into Food Banks… or into Christian ministries that provide helps for rent, utilities, counseling, meals, and so forth. It isn’t an either-or. But, all this said, even this does not answer your question, which, really must be broken into two questions, in my opinion, in order to address it properly: I believe charity within our borders, and without, is indeed a legitimate function of our government, and I am founding this conclusion upon the intentions so stated in our original governing documents, even including what the courts will not include, which is the Preamble to the Constitution. containing the most beautiful ideas and ideals by which and for which our government is to function. This part of our national treasured historic document most broadly and poetically states what some think of as describing the most beautiful ideas and ideals by which and for which our government is to function. It so states: “We the people of the United States, in order to form a more perfect union, establish justice, insure domestic tranquility, provide for the common defense, promote the general welfare, and secure the blessings of liberty to ourselves and our posterity, do ordain and establish this Constitution for the United States of America.” The history of our country that has unfolded since, however, has contained in it violence by our nation to its made-in-the-image of God residents, beginning with the continual and persistent exploitation of the Native American First Peoples, and propounded by the enslavement of many a “First-Peoples” who were kidnapped out of their own nation-states, if you will, and brought to the Americas against every fiber of their beings. Therefore, with the exponential growth of our population, and the onset of the industrialization of our economy (and presently, with the switching over to a highly technological and robotic work environment}, injustices occurred which were insurmountable by the regular people of all these categories. Leftward-leaning sociologist author Malcolm Gladwell elucidates the truth behind social programs that aim to level the playing field for competitive success through providing means to opportunities, whether that means is nutrition, medical care, education, training, practice, or what not. Google Gladwell’s book, “Outliers - The Story of Success,”* and you’ll find one page with several hundred quotes from the remarkable book, but, interestingly enough, many of the “favorites” are born of the same litter that his entire thesis is against: The MYTH, that people aren’t SELF-MADE. Well, while that has its place, it is not exactly the whole truth. Gladwell acknowledges grit, determination, imagination, dedication, and of course, parlays researchers’ discovery that it takes about 10,000 hours of “practice” to become really, really, really, good at something into a dictum that surely many people and parents have followed since. Who advances the most, in life, in a competitive society, are those who get those hours under their belt. Therefore, the younger kids who try out for hockey he points out that are old enough to get on the team, as opposed to those who might be a couple months younger than them and have to wait an entire year before starting to get regular practice and coached, are statistically, and he points out, significantly statistically, more likely to become “winners” in the sport. To wit, from Outliers: “The lesson here is very simple. But it is striking how often it is overlooked. We are so caught in the myths of the best and the brightest and the self-made that we think outliers spring naturally from the earth. We look at the young Bill Gates and marvel that our world allowed that thirteen-year-old to become a fabulously successful entrepreneur. But that's the wrong lesson. Our world only allowed one thirteen-year-old unlimited access to a time sharing terminal in 1968. If a million teenagers had been given the same opportunity, how many more Microsofts would we have today?” So it goes with every other avenue of self-support, and most other human activities. This comes from the differences through DNA, circumstances, culture, parental skills, and so forth, from the bank of data and abilities and tendencies that are carried by us all in our DNA and in the DNA of those around us. BUT, IF you believe that our DNA is not to rule us, that there are principles so attractive to our minds and hearts, such as fairness, justice, equality, liberty, peace, that other things must set the standard for collective life together, THEN we step out into an open invitation to restore, perhaps, or at least to inspire mankind to a better way of life. So, I do not believe government’s CHIEF job is “charity,” but I do believe a government of the people, by the people and for the people, can embrace reasonable programs, including supplemental nutrition, to help give our neighbors more of a fighting chance. Thanks for inviting me to contribute to Quora’s bank of answer on this topic; it deserves far greater depth of treatment than I have given it here, but it is a basic summation of this writer’s opinion on the advisability of the SNAP program in the USA. Godspeed to you and yours and may Co-Vid 19 be vanquished forever from the face of Earth, sooner than later. *Why this retired archeologist is convinced New Brunswick is home to a lost Viking settlement. Excerpt: “If confirmed, Hóp would become the second Viking settlement in Canada, the other being L’Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland...(archaeologist) Wallace also found remains of butternuts and parts of linden trees, species native only to New Brunswick, while researching in L’Anse aux Meadows. The materials had to be carried to L’Anse aux Meadows by humans, she said, proving that Vikings also stayed in New Brunswick.

Question: I feel like my church has betrayed me. Is it possible to request a return on the tithes I gave them?

Question: What do you do about a neighbor you go to church with that gets chummy with another neighbor thats abusive and youre afraid they'll be bringing them there? And yes there is one church in my area thats still holding church, should I quit going?
Answer: Question number one: Rejoice that your neighbor who is getting chummy with the person with a problem for what the “problematic” person may learn in church through instruction or example may free them from their problem, then “Voila!” you have a better neighbor. Jesus didn’t die for us to be beholden by the error of man - by any error. You can be a good part of a basically good group of people, and retain your self respect best by doing what your conscience tells you. It is my personal opinion, that some of the churches that continue to have large assemblies meet have problems with pride. The most formidable people I know in Christian ministry today are abiding by governmental guidelines. You will feel freer if you go to God for these answers, now that you’ve had some hopefully good input and ask Him to help you, to tell you, what would he want you to do. Question: Has quarantine life made you realize how little we need? How family values and togetherness matters. No need for lavish life, We don’t go out so no need to compare and be like people next doors. Less anxiety. Are you enjoying this?
Answer: Oh gosh yes. It is ASTOUNDING to me how EASY it was to get the world to be quiet for a few days… I am utterly amazed and wish that there were reasons to be confident that a new attitude about priorities would be birthed, but I do not think that will be the case. Repentance of, for instance, being superficial, wasting time, doing what we are TRULY being asked (by God) to do, generally, to stick for the good and all, takes a lot longer and the knife has to cut a lot deeper; but I hope some at least will permanently revise their habits. We make things SO HARD ON OURSELVES as a species, it is quite alarming, disheartening and makes me marvel “at their unbelief…”

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How do I stop sinfully talking? When I want to speak, and when I joke around, I keep having sinful ideas and thoughts, how do I stop having these thoughts and sinful talk but also being able to engage in conversations and joke around?
Answer: There are a few things going on when you find yourself in this kind of pickle! One, literal (in the spiritual realm) darts are flying through the air into that grey matter… they can be to just provoke you and irritate you so that you want to say something worse than “Drat, Batman!!” AND/OR they can be those literal words or phrases that you are saying, and they’re flying in to your being when they think you are vulnerable to their influence and control. Two, you have been progressing in your spiritual walk, and aspects of your sub- and un-conscious mind are coming up for air. They’ve been wanting to tell you somethings for a while, and now is there chance because you’ve begun to let your “upper-ego” get right=-sized a bit; they think you might now finally listen. Three, you’re angry about things in your life… your job, your relationships with your friends or family, circumstances at home, being constrained due to CoVid-19 if that is what you are dealing with as well, some limitations, OR you are angry at yourself. That last one is usually my issue. But whatever the source of these expletive deletives, as you already know, YOU are he one responsible for doing something about them. Here’s some ways I believe that would lead you into a head and heart space that will reduce the generation of that “junk.” Think of it as a spiritual awakening that will help you keep your heart clean and your hands ready to be of service. This can’t happen without being sanctified, and that doesn’t happen without disciplining the flesh. There is also, a “ thing,” a baptism, WITH HOLY FIRE that comes to burn that stuff out of you, particularly the DESIRE to partake in sin. This is not something all or even most pastors and churchey people are familiar with, so you will have to look online, YouTube and other places to find this resources, but it is a transformative experience. Go with God, Manny Nick. Stop sinning in thought word and deed!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What made your Easter weekend much better?
Answer: More than 30 years ago now, I learned in the rooms of Open Alcoholics Anonymous meetings and other 12 step meetings that every day is just another day. When we place a great deal of expectations on ourselves and others such as may happen with some families or people on holidays or special events, it can bring us into falling… falling off the wagon, falling into self-pity, falling for the sake disappointments over things and people and their moods and ideas over which we do not, nor should we have any control. While learning that doesn’t mean you have to omit holidays from your life, I have pretty much never gone back except for birthdays for close family members and in some ways, though not at all like I used to, celebrating Christmas and New Year’s. What made this Easter weekend “better” than any other Easter weekend is what makes any day better than any other: Did i take care of me? Did I love my son? Did I reach out to someone else, encourage them or help them? Am I or the world better off, even by a bit by how I spent my day? It was a little better than average day, because I took some action on a couple things I needed to, but it was nothing to write home about. If it was better at all, it’s because I got to spend some time with my son.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Deep inside, do you think Christians feel sorry for atheists?
Answer: Yes, I do. Atheists aren’t my chief “project” in life. Since faith is a gift, from God, I can’t “make” someone “believe.” I wouldn’t however say I “feel sorry” for them. For all I know, someday, before they die, they will become re-familiarized with a faith they actually received in childhood and remember what they lost. For all I know, they are LIVING a life day by day that is FAR MORE EXCELLENT in execution and service to others than I am, every day. It is FAR more important for me to look at what is yet wrong with me than to be an expert on the wrongs of others. There is something else that is far more important than pity, as well. And that is, if we (Christians) were all raising the dead and healing the sick and opening the blind eyes and so on, guess what? Many people who now do not believe, would have a far greater chance of opening themselves to the POSSIBILITY that there is more to life, more that is BEHIND the curtain of Creation (our senses, and any tools and devices intended to increase their reach) than either the curtain, or Creation. Moreover, MANY MANY MANY atheists are brilliant, focused, achievers who are TELLING THE TRUTH about many many facets of life. If our faith isn’t broad enough to embrace that, to learn what others know that we do not, then we are idiots, something which many of us have already convinced many an “un”-theist to contend. I have compassion, I don’t like the word pity for anything… pity in my opinion involves objectifying someone. THE most important thing I can keep in mind with relating to ANYONE is that they are PEOPLE. God’s word says He created us in HIS image. EVERY ATHEIST ALIVE was created in God’s image. Therefore, we begin at a point of honor, respect, and look for ways to proceed together toward honest ends. The rest of it, I leave in God’s hands. It is true, that in my heart, if I think on this for long, it is hard, because God wants all to know him, and wants NONE deceived. NONE. It is his will that NONE should perish, or not walk in eternal life. But to be wise enough to “help” someone who has been deceived by the well-worked lies of the Deceiver of mankind is not an easy task. But, you cannot go wrong treating people, no matter what the label is that anybody uses to describe themselves or that others use to describe who you are looking at, like they’re pretty much just like you, because they are. Everything else, EVERY thing else is just a minor detail. I am glad for atheists… that they exist. They play a very important role, whether or not they come to receive the gift of salvation or not. Many times their eyes are far clearer on what is wrong or what is necessary. And when their accusations fall into the department of “almost right,” all that can do is sharpen our own response to the fallen nature of the world.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Is it possible to stop going to hell and heaven at the same time?
Answer: I think you are referring to the state of being a carnal Christian. This is someone who has believed on Jesus as Lord and Savior, AND has given him the reins of your life, but who has back-slid into patterns that are not serving or glorifying God. This is a vexing, and awful place to be in. It reminds me of the slogan I used to hear in Open AA meetings I used to attend in the last ’80′s and early ‘90’s (usually said by a cowboy type who chain smoked): “Ya know, recovery is like this: You got TWO DOGS IN YA, one is a really bad, beat up, mean, growling sort of thing; the other is the best, most healthy, happy and eager-to-please pouch… (dramatic silence). AND everyday you get up those two dogs gonna be fighting their way to the front door of YOUR mind wanting you to FEED ’em (another dramatic silence). You know what? THE ONE YOU FEED THE MOST THAT DAY is going to RULE YOUR DAY! AND MAYBE YOU TOMORROWS TOO, so FEED THE RIGHT DOG!” YOU, not your mom, not your spouse, not your squeeze, not your cable repair man, not your priest, not you pastor, not your counselor, YOU are responsible for WHAT YOU DO and DON’T DO TODAY. There are WAYS to decrease the sin. Sometimes it involves those people above, but if you are HIS, it will ALWAYS involve prayer and faith. So, GET YOUR GAME ON. And quit playing the cards the Devil is trying to deal you. Also, remember, the demons are watching you, just like the Angels; the Angels can see more, and the demons understand less, but BOTH as well as the ENTIRE CLOUD OF WITNESSES in heaven AND the ENTIRE HEAVENLY HOST is watching you, every minute of every day. So, like I said, GET YOUR GAME ON BOY, or GIRL; BE STRONG, DON’T HESITATE, STOP LOSING, and GO CAPTURE THAT FLAG!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Can a Christian be held accountable for something they accidentally said in their mind?
Answer: God is EXTREMELY demanding. WE ARE SUPPOSED TO BE HIS SONS!!!! We are supposed to do what GOD DOES. THINK like HE DOES. WALK ON WATER like HE DID. EVERY single word we will be held accountable for, including those in our mind… HOWEVER, there is no doubt in my mind that some “thoughts” which are generally shaped with words come in fact into our minds through the very able “darts” of the enemy. I didn’t used to believe this, since I buy into being (unproductively) so hard on myself all the time; but today I have watched and seen this phenomenon operate in myself and in others. When this kind of thing arises, we are responsible as another writer here has indicated for what we DO with that thought. Thoughts are like birds, we can shake em off, let them go, or grab hold of them and let them nest in our heads. Gotta be careful though, because birdies like to have baby birds, and then you get a whole lot of the same up in that head and our heads are fond of manifesting and running the show… hence, thinking on what is pure, what is just, what is lovely (in a PURE way, fellas), these thoughts will help us. Here’s the character we are to WORK to obtain (and this is that which we long for, to be conformed to his image, which, as Jesus points out here in this portion of what is referred to as the Sermon on the Mount, includes loving the just and the unjust, like God does, as ALL were made in his image): Matthew 5 King James Version 21 Ye have heard that it was said of them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: 22 But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire. 23 Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; 24 Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift. 25 Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison. 26 Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing. 27 Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery: 28 But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. 29 And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell. 30 And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell. 31 It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: 32 But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery. 33 Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: 34 But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: 35 Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. 36 Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. 37 But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. 38 Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: 39 But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. 40 And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. 41 And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. 42 Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away. 43 Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. 44 But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; 45 That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. 46 For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same? 47 And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so? 48 Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: As an American, what advice would you give to an immigrant (originating from a third world country) to integrate himself in the American society?
Answer: I would approach a charter school in your area that includes a lot of patriotic focus on this nation’s early history. I would see if they would be willing to share the curriculum with you, even let you borrow it during this coming summer, and then I would also ask if they would meet with you once a week to further explore and even experience what you read. You will find that certain words and themes that are important to most Americans, whether born here or elsewhere, are important to all, but not in the same way: Freedom, Rights, Democracy, the Republic, Opportunity, Self-Made Man, Freedom of Speech, Religion, Freedom of Religion, Education, Law, Justice… and many others. You will be a brilliant contributor to this society if you can research this by getting first a basic outline of our history: And then sharing what you understand to be the main drives and results of each epoch, then sharing and hearing about what others think about it all. You will be a brilliant and good “servant” of what is known by some as “the common good” (See Walter Lippman) if you are devoted in your study of this country, your new home, and you will remind some of what it truly means to be an American. Then, after much of this work is done over a course of several years while building your new life here, THEN you can help us all engage in the more important thing: What shall our future together be based upon?? Thank you for the kind compliment of including me in your question today and I hope and pray (just did pray for you and your future) that you and your beloved family and friends are staying safe and will be protected from Co-Vid-19 or anything else destructive that comes along. Godspeed to you!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Have you repented for your sins, as the Bible suggests we do in times like these?
Answer: Repentence, metanoia in the original Greek, meaning to change/renew your MIND. It is very difficult to do things that we don’t, on some level with some part of our minds, “agree” with; so to stop sins, we must find where we have agreed that it is okay and find a true way to make it not okay. Feeling badly for our sins, that we sinned, (not talking about feeling bad FOR the trouble or hurt we caused others, just the part where we are unhappy we sinned for some reason or other) is not a pathway, necessarily to not sinning again in the future; that’s why and how a drunk gets up after a terrible night of being sick, feeling sorry, making promises, and opens up a bottle of vodka the next day as soon as he wakes up. CHANGING OUR MINDS is a deeper process and usually involves learning of some sort, or bringing our own hypocrisy (if indeed our own version of what we should be does NOT involved doing that sin) under such glaring light of contrast between what we wish/say we are and want to be and just did… That glaring light can come from a peer group to which we belong from which we want approval, or we want what they have so we are willing to do what they do to get it… It can come from a religious or non-religious counselor who helps us see it… Or from someone close to us. There is also another source of, not so much conviction, as that, for a believer is the Holy Spirit, but for our hypocrisy, and that is the Adversary. Taken as a real being, i.e. Satan, or taken as a mechanic of the sub- and un-conscious, the Adversary will bring to our faces, in an almost humiliating way, how completely unrepentant (unchanged in our minds) we truly are, when we persist in habits that make up our hours, days, weeks and finally decades, and when we refuse to forge NEW habits with what we pitifully may decry as unreasonable demands on our old, worn out minds. These kinds of come-backs to the call to repent are indeed just the clamoring of the flesh to not be bothered with things it WISH were insignificant but which are the ones that make up our very character, through behavior, which thereby, with the circumstances and timing and resources allowed around us, make up the records of our daily lives. Have I done this during this challenging time of the corona-virus? I am certainly trying. And, as the Adversary is after me on a fairly regular basis (I praise God for the Adversary as while his tone is unwelcome, the effect of his nasty messages is quite clarifying and produces, by default, good), I should think the longer this time lasts, the better I will be by the end of it. Thank you for this A2A and please be safe and well.

Question: Would you be concerned if you see your atheist friend beginning to pray during the coronavirus outbreak?
Answer: If my atheist friend began to pray during this coronavirus outbreak, I would be concerned, about him, or her. I would wonder where this was coming from and what happened to them. So, yeah, I would be concerned! I’d ask: What’s going on? What happened? Then depending upon what they said, I would “minister” the grace of God to them as best I could, which includes the fact that the rain falls on the just and the unjust… and an unsaved person is by definition, unjust, and many believers, are frankly, pretty unjust as well… so… I would merely do what any good friend would do first which is just listen. Then I would evaluate what seems like my most helpful response could be. Their sudden pleas to God during this viral outbreak would have no influence whatsoever on my sense of security or fear about the outbreak. I take my stuff to God, because my experience is that He’s the one with the shoulders that can handle it. I would just want my friend to be okay, on whatever terms they decide to be okay. That’s how I would respond. Thanks for the request, and please take care of yourself during this troubled time.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Should America reopen for the day on Easter Sunday?
Answer: It’s too soon. Fauci looked like his soul was in pain before the interview I saw of him where he “willingly” announced a downward adjustment of projected number of USA deaths due to an apparent small down tic in the RATE of acceleration of demands for hospital services. There’s just too many areas of the country that haven’t dealt with this; it is starting in highly urbanized centers with dense populations, in general, and then moving to other areas of each state (except when there has been transmission to a specific nursing home). Many problems have a “tail…” - the tail gets whipped by the problem itself it would seem when it is nearly done with, solved, or eradicated. This is true when the body fights a virus as well, the immune system does a full-on attack at first, but the virus while down, then ramps back up to hit it again. That’s when those who get up and go back to work because they’re “feeling better” do themselves and others a disservice because nearly immediately the sick feelings return and the body is even more tired than if the person had continued to take care of themselves at home. I think the timing on Co-Vid-19 is being pushed by political forces heavily invested in reversing the impact of the disease on their capacity to make money. I also think we need more time to prep more ventilators for more areas of the country. On the other hand, Israel says it’s nearly got a vaccine, so… Israeli scientists: 'In a few weeks, we will have coronavirus vaccine'

Question: What can you do if you have to go into a store during this coronavirus epidemic—wearing gloves and a mask—but another customer keeps walking up close to you ignoring the six-foot distancing rule, and ignores your requests to keep their distance?
Answer: You do what I did. You abruptly turn about; get your feet shoulder wide. Put your arms on your chest, even reaching out… And tell ‘em, “BACK OFF.” When they start to say WHATEVER they are going to say other than dropping their eyes and forehead and saying, “You’re right, I am SO sorry…,” you say, “No you didn’t; no you won’t; no you can’t; do I need to get the store manager while you’re on camera here and security is watching you so you’ll be thrown out?” You asked, Cathy, you got it. Grab ’em by the jugular. You just might save someone’s life this way… even maybe theirs!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why can young Americans get very sick from Covid-19?
Answer: Young Americans can get very sick from CoVid-19 because of underlying conditions, just as some older people do. And, age and underlying medical or health conditions like heart disease and diabetes are not the only things that this virus can take advantage of. For some reason, some people who catch CoVid-19 will develop an exacerbated response to the threat to their health and overproduce cells and accelerate processes related to inflammation, making it harder for the body to actually fight the virus. Lungs, even young ones that are not compromised before the virus, can be tread upon by the pace at which this virus replicates and quickly require help to keep bringing fresh oxygen in and pushing carbon dioxide out. Unfortunately for some young people who have had CoVid-19, their lungs and other organs were overcome and they expired before science or medical efforts have become effective enough to help them win the battle. This is ANOTHER reason why we should wear our masks when we go outside to places where we may run into others. It REALLY isn’t a terrible inconvenience. It IS an annoyance, but what’s that compared to saving the life of someone’s grandfather? Mother?? Sister? Yourself?

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How will researchers connect these Covid-19 clues: 1.patients with home care less mortality than hospitalized; 2.virus doesn't enter ambiotic fluid; 3.virus is not transmitted by breast milk, or 4.some animals are more vulnerable to infection?
Answer: Please allow me to only throw my hat in this ring in order to put forward a basic guess which many people surely already have surmised as well, and that is regarding clue 1. : “patients with home care less mortality than hospitalized.” The link to a FINANCIAL TIMES article that evinces a stark contrast between the death rates from COVID-19 in Lombardy and Veneto, Italy; is great, but only remotely touches on the “clue,” listed above as one of four that the Quora writer would like to see how the scientific world will connect the dots. The fact is, in many scientific studies, factors which at first seem as though they must fit together actually do not. And in fact they are not infrequently unrelated altogether; kind of like a man not talking to his wife after work one day. She thinks it’s something she said; he keeps saying, “Yes, dear,” but to his consternation, his commitment to being congenial, agreeable only works to worsen his account of goodwill from his wife, because as the evening progresses, the glass of wine he served her is apparently going to be totally wasted, which is a pity because now that he has figured out the answer to the problem from work that came home with him in his head, she looks pretty much like she’s only going to offer him a cold shoulder the rest of the night. Just under 100 miles apart, the people of Veneto and Lombardy are themselves having some trouble related to a glass of wine - for they are worlds apart thus far with respect to how many people are celebrating over a cup of fine Italian vino or drowning their valid sorrows with it. According to the Financial Times article, Lombardy has lost 8,576 of its good citizens, (which in total number more than 10 million) while Veneto, a city of half the population of Lombardy) have lost only 607 of their loved ones out of 10,824 diagnosed cases. Lombardy’s death rate of 17.6 per cent, in other words, is more than triple that of Veneto’s, at 5.6 percent. But as the FT article elucidates, the key to understanding and therefore avoiding the duplication of Lombardy’s comparative disadvantage isn’t in the detection of some elusive characteristic of the biological treasures within the people of Veneto; no, the answer clearly lies in the cities’ differing attitudes and resulting rates of hospital admissions of those suffering from COVID-19. Again, from Financial Times : “The number of diagnosed patients who were taken in hospitals for clinical treatment at the start of the outbreak was about 65 per cent in Lombardy, Prof Palù said. This compares with 20 per cent in Veneto, where the majority were told to stay at home unless urgent care was required. “There were different instructions given to the sick by the different regional health authorities,” he said. “Yes, there has been more testing in Veneto but people were kept at home and not taken into hospitals. The more patients you admit to the hospital, the more cases you get. You create the outbreak as at the start nobody was taking care of sampling the doctors or nurses, [so] you were taking home the infection. “His observation comes as more than 60 Italian doctors and health workers have died, the majority of these in Lombardy. A group of doctors from the Papa Giovanni XXIII hospital in Bergamo warned last month that hospitals had become the main source of transmission of Covid-19 infections, and urged more patients to be treated at home.”) SO, don’t concentrate the opportunities for infection, or shall we say, infestation. Prevalence of the virus, the viral load, the number of viral particles in the air, on the surfaces, this seems to be the issue most germane to Lombardy’s death rate? And, isn’t the “sub-issue” the way that health professionals are acting as “spreading agents” for the disease as their work environments are massively occupied with COVID-19 positive human beings? If previously assumed models of the distance viral-carrying droplets can spew through your living room or your office have underestimated the power of your sneezing reflexes, (as MIT seemed to have recently shown: [A high speed camera at MIT is showing that a sneeze can travel up to 8m, four times the distance of theoretical models used in the Covid-19 outbreak [Researchers at MIT in the US have used a high speed imaging camera to show that a sneeze carrying the Covid-19 virus can travel up to 8m. This is four times the distance previously predicted and has significant implications for social distances and the design of equipment.] …then aren’t we TOTALLY in the Wild Wild West of Guess Work Ranch when it comes to measuring the viral contamination of PPE and transference from one surface to one human hand, to one human knee, to one bed rail, to a hospital bed and so forth???? I think we are. And of course, the Quora question poser knows that this slice of life is only a teeny percentage of all that might be up for consideration under Clue 1: Home care better outcomes than hospital care for COVID-19′ers. Is it being able to SEE and TOUCH your loved ones when you feel you might DIE that is making the difference? Are we contrasting nursing homes to hospitals? Are we contrasting private nurses and doctors paid to come in to a home who aren’t stressed out with making decisions over who shall live and die every day? And what about that social support? Is that what made the difference with the 17 church goers in Singapore who ALL got better from COVID even after a few got really, really, bad? How They Beat Coronavirus! As to Clues 2 (virus doesn’t enter amniotic fluid) and 3 (virus is not transmitted in breast milk), I believe these will be found to be attributable to physical features of the virus as well as the biochemical mechanisms in the placenta and the fetus. Clue 4, “Some animals are more vulnerable to infection,” since this will first be understood on a macro level, as in which SPECIES are more vulnerable to infection, and is that the same thing as getting sick, as opposed to trying to draw up parallels between individual animals of identical species. Comments, opinions, additions, criticisms, all are welcome on this one. I find the question inordinately tempting to direct my entire intellectual life for a few days. I love puzzles!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: For essential workers (not healthcare), given the choice, would you rather be employed/earning right now, knowing there are medical risks from COVID, or not work/be unemployed but medically safer?
Answer: Essential workers outside of the high calling of being involved in responding directly to the healthcare crisis in America are certainly supplying the rest of us services, goods, and a sense of normalcy that if they were not working we would not be able to have. But, life is more important and if they can, if I can, let’s take a break. Colorado is several weeks behind the east coast of the USA; our numbers’ll be comin’ around that mountain, I think, in about four weeks in Denver, that’d be first week of May, and mid-to-late May down here 70 miles south in Colorado Springs, and anothe 40 miles farther south in Pueblo. Today our media reported how two WAL-Mart workers lost their lives to COVID-19, and how the large corporation may indeed offer TWO WHOLE additional dollars to man jobs that they say they need to keep their store running. I say, drop the act; no one should be “shopping” anymore. The only food pantry I am sure that is staying open in my part of the woods is on East La Salle Drive; it’s run by a great family of its founders and oodles of volunteers from all over the city, and right away, they jumped into high gear shut down indoor operations, and went to a drive-through system. All the stores can do this too. We don’t need comfort from “normalcy,” anymore. We need to crush the curve. Thanks for the A2A, Andrew, and please wear your mask, sanitize, wash your hands, practice safe and stay well!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What do you think about churches that still hold services with large groups of people?
Answer: I think it is unfortunate - that the people who are still gathering in numbers in excess of whatever local, state or national mandates suggest during this time of staying at home and only doing essential errands and essential work are, in fact, missing the heart beat of God, whom I personally think is asking all of us to get quiet and think; to reflect on priorities and ways of doing things; to observe what happens when unified focus for the good of all is prevailing; to observe what silence, or at least quiet (outside of the emergency rooms, and the places where people are naturally wailing for the loss of loved ones), can do for the Earth and for mankind. They are missing the point. And, they seem to have a point to prove themselves, and instead of doing so, instead of glorifying God, they are supporting the killing off of some of their leaders and their friends, and neighbors. What a shame!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is something you are thankful for during this quarantine?
Answer: Time alone, time to focus a bit on the Lord, time with family, less interference with others, less traffic, less gas expenses, less eating out for no reason, less spent on fast food (healthier eating!), and the world around us seems to be getting quieter… There’s less of an atmosphere penetrated by constant push, go, more, here, now, let’s get it done, we can do it, over the top, activity by my fellow man and woman. It’s quieter… It seems like there is literally more “room” to breathe, to think, to slow down, to reflect. I love it. May it PLEASE be a PERMANENT RESET! If we lived like this all the time, and grew some of our own food, and collectively took care of animal protein needs through our own efforts, we could live until we’re 950 years old like Noah did. Thank you, Emily, for inviting me to answer your question. I think it might behoove all of us to think on it daily right now, or even write a bit in our journals through out this time period to see how we deal with it all and perhaps even GROW through it all. Blessings to you and yours, and safety, and protection!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How does Benny Hinn get people to fall down and act like they do once they are on the ground?
Answer: I thought it was phony. I had a then-older friend who had a mess of a house, a terrible childhood, widowhood from a man whom she might have been surely better off without as he used to beat her and their son, and she LOVED Benny Hinn. She was also a VERY powerful “prayer” warrior. Phenomenal at prophecy, though extremely humble and nearly non-existent ego. When I would stop by or call and hear Benny Hinn in the background, I said nothing, but I would just think, perhaps as you or MANY others do, “Well, if that comforts her, more power to her!” WOW, was I arrogant. I had NO idea this stuff was real. I mean NONE. Makes sense though, doesn’t it? For some of us who jump to conclusions that because our experience hasn’t been a certain way, a certain experience must be manufactured, false, or made up? I think so. Well, after my friend died, my son and I were invited to visit a Friday night meeting with a lady “prophet” who “walked in healing” and so on, (those quotes mean she has the spiritual gift(s) of healing and prophecy). People were going up and “getting slain by the spirit.” I thought, okay, what the heck… when my son asked if he should go up. I said sure, if you want. My son has some very special gifts anyway, and I had learned to trust his judgment on certain things, but I sure as heck didn’t need it. He went up, the lady put her hand on his chest, without any force really, then looked up at him when he didn’t “go down.” She stepped back and thought, or prayed, or both, and then put her hand on him again, with a little more force, and WHOMP, he went down and stayed down. Now, skeptics may feel, or conclude, this is hocus pocus, she pushed him down. Nah, my kid was 6′2″ and 170 pounds then and I can guarantee he wasn’t “pushed” down… But, you say, auto-suggestion… Nah, my son IS gullible in some ways… but NOT in this manner. He takes spiritual stuff seriously. He knows it’s not a game and he doesn’t take anyone else’s word, including his mother’s, for anything. Stubborn “young” fool that he is. Anyway, truly, he sorts it all out himself. Well, he went down and stayed down for a bit; when he came back to the chair next to me, he just felt to me to be a bit more relaxed. Okay, REALLY relaxed. But he didn’t say much to me about it until much much later, a couple YEARS later. We went to visit Charis Bible College here in Colorado Springs, Colorado, one Sunday for a special healing service where they had arranged to bring in a world renown “healer.” He had called on the Wednesday prior to let them know he couldn’t make it…. he was worn out and needed rest, and so he cancelled What were Pastor Lawson Purdue and Andrew Wommack to do? Well, they decided to go ahead and have the event, and they put themselves wholly into the event. My son and I were sitting in the back. There was a long time period after a lesson of sorts, of people of all ages sizes and shapes ministering to those who asked for healing all around the large auditorium off of Elkton (this is before their move up to Woodland Park). A minister of Lawson’s came up to me when I was interceding while others were praying for a woman wheelchair-bound with multiple sclerosis. “Ma’am, Do you need healing?” “Oh, no, I’m fine, I’M PRAYING FOR OTHERS,” I proudly announced, because you see, NO ONE’S GONNA fool around with MY BODY, MY HEALING, MY SPIRITUAL LIFE…. I’m no fool!!!! Oh, but what a fool I was, my intellect pierced through with pride. Fortunately for me, the band of do-gooders around this one woman in the wheelchair dissolved, and all of a sudden, I find myself faced with this Texan in a 10-gallon hat, saying, loudly, “MA’AM, may I pray for your?” And barely before I could get a syllable out, this guy has his hand on my neck, and I start feeling this INCREDIBLE feeling, this warmth, like I have never felt before in my life, or since. AND THEN this thing started happening… It was like a humongous, hot flapping butterfly was on top of my head, flapping his wings up and down, up and down, but I wasn’t letting go. I looked around, I weigh a good deal, and I thought, I am not going down with catchers around me… there seemed to be none; the phenomenon continued, all of a sudden, my son was behind me with another man, THEN I remembered what my son had finally told me one day about his experience with that lady, “I just knew, Mom, that if I let go it would feel really, really, good.” I let go. BAM… I went down into those men’s arms and laid on that floor for a bit. I had never had anything like this happen to me, though I was filled with the Holy Ghost when I had a priest in the Episcopal Church lay his apostolic bishopy hand on my head for confirmation in sixth grade… (I began to speak in tongues afterwards but did not know what that was). But, the most amazing thing about this experience, is that it didn’t end. For TWO WEEKS solid, I was in another world. It was like, and believe, me, I had never ever ever put these silly sounding words together in the same sentence before, and no, no one told me this is what you say, or what not, but it was like a few drops of “golden anointing oil,” had been spread throughout my whole being. It was one of the loveliest experiences I have ever had in my life. So, that’s MY experience. But it wasn’t about Benny Hinn. This one is: Todd White was meeting a drug dealer. Addicted to porn by age 10, drugs by 12, this then teen-ager, had conceived the brilliant plan (a way to get yourself shot, actually) to cheat a drug dealer by pretending he was an undercover cop and demanding on the goods…. When the shots started to ring out from the dealer’s 9mm, White was standing next to his car and only about 10 to 12 feet I think it was from the gun. The bullets did not hit him; It was as though they went THROUGH HIM into other objects around him. He got in his car and sped off in total shock and freaked out then heard a voice, “I took those bullets for you, Todd.” Great, Todd thought, now I’m f***ed with the dealer, gonna get killed, AND I’m losing my mind. But there is was again. And then he told Todd he was Jesus. Which freaked him out ever more. So, without going into more detail, Todd was saved that night, and began growing in the Lord right away, but was not getting the results he wanted. He wanted his laying of hands on people to work, just the way the bible says. He wanted to see the blind see and the deaf hear and lame walk. So, he decided to try some Christian conferences. At one, he decided to sit up front. All of a sudden, the speaker pointed at him and told him to come up front. Todd was surprised, but went up. The man looked at Todd, who was several feet from him, with two very large men behind him to “catch” him or help if anything went down. All of a sudden, the man said something, made a move with his arm toward Todd, and TODD AND THE TWO CATCHERS went up in the air four feet and BACK six feet as they heard what sounded like crackling in the air… something like thunder. Todd was stunned, the catchers were caught off guard. And as Todd came around, and sat up and then stood up, he stood in front of the man once more, and said, “AGAIN.” BOOM, up four feet (with the other two BIG guys, again) and back six. Todd was discombobulated. Could not speak. Was receiving power from on high and did not know his name hardly. The two ushers gathered their wits, readied themselves to carry Todd off the stage, then the man of God said to the Man of God, “I NEED MORE OF JESUS;” and ONE MORE TIME. Todd, he says in more than one testimony, was reduced to tears. They literally had to carry him OFF stage, and set him on the floor, where he remained in tears, sobs and so forth for the rest of the event. Now, that man, Todd, he’s got some courage. And the man standing in for God to wipe him out and see that he would be imbued with God’s power? Benny Hinn.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How well do you think Colorado is handling the pandemic?
Answer: Steve, I am not in the medical field and have no close friends or relations who are. On the CDC’s modeling, state-by-state of how many hospital beds will be needed when the wave “crests,” and how many ventilators and how much staff, we are at about half of what we need, in that model. My guess is that we will fare better than most because of the number of military installations, for instance in Colorado Springs, there is Fort Carson, Shriever Air Force Base, NORAD, Peterson Air Force Base, as well as the Air Force Academy. That means boots on the ground to help that are local, therefore more presence, hopefully, and standing of “local opinion.” I also think we will fare better because while we will not be in the first run of the crises, we also will not be undone by having done nothing, as our governor has been pretty pro-active. The hard thing about expecting or hoping that best practices will reach all our citizens is that aspect of the childhood game, OPERATOR… where you tell a secret next to you and pass it down… and by the time Rubber Baby Buggy Bumpers makes it to the last person, it might come out Rubber Pants Rub Us Wrong. The other thing that is going to be a challenge is the lack of experience of the front line and administrators with this kind of crisis. We’ll be lucky if we do have people come in from other states (without the virus, please) to help “naturalize” the process so that we aren’t learning by our mistakes. Last, in my mind, one of the most important hopes that I have seen, and that only the FDA can stand in the way of, as well as BIG PHARMA if it thinks it has nothing to gain and ANYTHING to lose, is the deployment of the strategy of getting the COVID-19 antigen-rich blood plasma of people who have recovered from COVID to those who need help the fastest. So far, from all I have read, the cases where this helped was near miraculous. I know, concurrence isn’t causation, but still…. It makes a great deal of sense that it would help. The only anecdotal info I have is that one of the hospitals erected the COVID-19 ward right next to the Maternity Ward (“because that’s where there was room”). I don’t know which Colorado Springs Hospital that is; hopefully they’ve made some other arrangements. The other thing I fear for the Springs, more than Denver, is that the poorer and more stressed people are, the more their brains go to shortcut stress and thereby rule out thinking creatively. They will forget things that HAVE been reported as being helpful; they might cut short certain procedures and protocol that makes a difference just because in their mind “It really won’t make a difference.” And of course, there’s always the blame game to watch out for, when it comes to the need to make objectively-based decisions. Like elsewhere in the States, Colorado has a bit of a shortage of nurses; this could also hurt our responsiveness. Thanks for including me in this A2A, Steve, and I am sorry to not be of more help.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What are pros and cons of live broadcasting Trump's daily COVID-19 press conferences? He often relays misinformation, rambles, rejects unfavorable questions, and limits the time of the educated, experienced professionals? British PM's is concise.
Answer: Concise isn’t ever going to part of President Trump’s speech. But, he is getting better. You’ve already covered the cons… misinformation, handing on pens from his hand to his staff, thereby setting the worst example, goes off on tangents, misemphasizes things that aren’t important to everyone to the same level… The advantages are relationship… while most of us are not in any “personal” relationship with our president, it does give one a feel of being connected to the White House. To those of us who like looking closely at a person’s behavior, to deduce things about their psyche or for other reasons, President Trump is a rich subject to study. What I find the most interesting about watching him is to see how far good training and possibly beds can go to help a person match their behavior to expectations and needs of a larger body, in this case, of the American public. I forget exactly when Tweeting Toddler Terrors were stopped, or drastically curtailed, but their occurrence definitely decreased dramatically, both in offensiveness, and in quantity and in size. The press conference he participated in this past Sunday, April 5, shows he is still working on being context-appropriate, giving others room to speak without interruption, reinforcing supportive output by his staff and colleagues, and many other things. Considering how short of breath he sounded at times during his address, and how old he is, I can’t help but admire the persistence aspect of his character and personality. This is a guy who doesn’t give up. He may not be the sharpest tool in the shed, but I betchya history is going to surprise a few people on what his High-D (high dominance) personality style accomplished. Many people in Europe across many economic, social and political spectrums expressed enthusiastic support for Trump in the beginning of his presidency as someone who would hopefully be less on the hook of the Power Elite; that his moves would not be overtly orchestrated to such an extent as other presidents’ agendas have been the past few decades. They were looking for a genuine leader with a real power base; they were hanging onto the (false) hope that America might be bringing forward such a leader in the “rich and worldly” Donald Trump. They were, of course, wrong.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What would you say to a friend or think of them for having such a strong hatred towards churches?
Answer: There are a couple of ways to look at a friend’s hatred towards churches. One, they could have been hurt, personally, or seen someone close to them hurt, by church. They could also be perceptive, and if they ever accepted Jesus Christ - ever believed on him, even as a child - they MAY have the spiritual gift of discernment, and with or without that gift, they may be seeing how deep people’s needs are right now, and what a horrific job church is doing in so many ways. I would take them to lunch or go on a walk and ask them what they see happening in Christendom, what their childhood exposure was, what their parents’ relationship was with organized religion and just see what you can gather as the foundation for their strong feelings. There are millions who have left church due to its own oral decay and lack of accountability in the last 60 years… What we need is for those people to come back in and change it. They have gifts the church needs. And what the church needs is a HUGE cleaning out and cleaning up campaign from within. Thanks for including me in this A2A and I hope this helps you be able to talk to your friend in a frank and kind manner without any fall out… at least six feet apart please!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why do so many pastors and churches have a disconnect with science? Why are so many not following the stay at home orders and opening the church up during this Coronavirus/Covid-19 pandemic?
Answer: It’s a little hard to understand it, isn’t it? It is like to some of those people they feel THEIR OWN PERSONAL FAITH is being tested by God (or that their own “flock” will find them LACKING). I am glad that in Colorado Springs the vast majority of churches are being closed; this isn’t an issue about healing not being available at church or through people who have faith in Christ; this is about not tempting faith AND submitting to governmental authority. The very first thing this defiance does is lose face for the church. The pastors that do this aren’t showing how good God or they are; they are showing that they think it’s okay to do whatever you want despite what your government says. This is quite unfortunate, and I am afraid it WILL and has ALREADY cost people lives. The way I have observed that most churches work is that they follow a certain set of guidelines and doctrinal positions in suit with what their individual denominational leaders and councils advise; so IF their “leaders” that are beyond their local pulpit say, “Hey the “dark state” government, or whatever, is trying to take control of all of us… then they fall in line and do what is suggested, which, perhaps is involved with those churches who have chosen NOT to shutter their doors. You think of how the early Christians “worshiped,” IN PEOPLE’S homes; there were no large places to meet, except occasionally, and then often in a rich person’s home. We have become awfully conditioned to think everything today has to be just like it was yesterday, and that, I think, is one very GOOD thing this COVID-19 will do… it just might shake things up enough to unhook people from their expectations and get them down to brass tacks about their lives. You’ve contended that this trend of keeping churches open is actually about a rift between men and women of science and men and women of, apparently in your mind, faith-and-therefore-no-science, but I don’t think that is the case with all. I say that because of an article Quora writer Judy Dodd brought my attention to about 44 rabbis dying since COVID-19 began, most of them in the USA. Rabbis are NOT anti-science. But convictions about their faith and meeting together are very strong. It caused me to reconsider that all such decisions to stay open were born of anti-scientism and instead entertain the thought that this may just be about deep convictions. The question about the separation of church and science, is really, an entirely different question than it in the context of decisions during COVID-19. And it is WAY too big of a question to add on thoughts about it right here. Ask the question separately and I will give it a go, Tony. Thanks for including me in your A2A.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What do you think about Jeff Bezos donating $100 million to food banks?
Answer: Praise GOD for that money coming out of Mr. Bezos’ bank account and into the hands of people who will help the hungry eat. And I honor and THANK Mr. Bezos for making this choice with this $100 million OF HIS money. Mr. Bezos could have put that cool one hundred million down on a bet in Las Vegas or on the Ponies, if he is a betting man… but he DIDN’T! HE SPENT IT ON FOOD for people. Thank you, Mr. Bezos. That was a good choice, sir. If that felt good, please do it again; if it didn’t, please do it again until you do feel good. God Bless Mr. Bezos!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How would you respond to a friend or family member who does not like the church and that anger still goes strong with them on their deathbed and they say to you it would offend them if you had their funeral at a church and any pastors could f$&k off?
Answer: First, I would agree with them. If they are not presently too sick to hear stories other than their own about this kind of trouble, I might share some personal horror stories of how my son when he was younger and myself as a first-time mother were treated… or how I’ve seen others treated. But my real concern would be this person’s soul. Their desire to be assured that their funeral would not be held at a church is something I would want to affirm; I might then ask what kind of moderator they would like, if not someone who is religious. I might volunteer to be such a moderator. I would ask permission to share from the bible, if he or she is not totally against that as well. Then, I would ask them for their story and try to locate that point in time where something happened that caused them to have a wound so deep, at such an inopportune time, that they have made whatever truth they felt they got from that event, and/or events similar to that one, their go-to place when they are afraid, sorrowful, disturbed. I would try to find out essentially what made them fixate on this wrong doing. It’s real, whatever hurt they suffered. It’s not in their imagination. It might have been something that cost them something in what was then held up as a promise in the future; it might be a person that took away their hope, or hurt someone they loved. So many things go wrong in life it is hard to truly be an over-comer. So, I would try to help them reclaim the parts of their soul that they left anchored in that mess from long ago… I gently coax them to see their responsibility which they also clearly neglected to make better of it. Then I would turn their face toward the future… Will they want to go to God, or to the “hereafter” with such unresolved anger and grief and heartache? If they are particularly recalcitrant, I would try to usher in a wind of change by suggesting they “take a vacation” from this burden for the rest of the day… then I might go home and pray for them, to have God and His Angels remove this burden from his soul supernaturally so that he could live the rest of his life unencumbered by the events’ talons. Then, if I had the time, I would continue, each day, visiting, maybe reading some of the more beautiful passages in the bible to him, one’s with imagery, try to draw him into imagining the scenes, without ANY emphasis on morals or faith or doctrine or anything vexatious; just comfort and encouragement. Some of us become jaded not just through the actions of others, but by our own dwelling in the “other person’s sins,” thereby stifling our own growth and comfort level in the world of the Spirit, and also, thereby, losing much time. This person NEEDS to hear about peace, forgiveness, God’s love for all, that there is an answer, and they may need to be reborn… they may need to be told they need to accept Jesus Christ as their personal savior and that may also mean they need someone to help get them first delivered from any demons that have found his soul a perfect resting place for their own desires and activities for so long. If this is a relative of yours, please do not take their animosity personally, EVER, and in a way, don’t take it too seriously. They CAN get over it, and this often will happen toward the end of life, in a minute, if SOMEONE will preach the good news to them in a way that their very desperate soul needs to hear it.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why are so many churchgoers cold-hearted, egotistical jerks? I am singling them out even though there are others who are this way because they tend to be self-righteous hypocrites.
Answer: Right there with ya, Donna! The overall best place I find where at least there is considerable pressure to be otherwise is the Catholic church, but, you’re right. There are a lot of cold-hearted, egotistical, self-righteous hypocrites that dust off their bible (because they haven’t read it all week) every Sunday morning and march into and then back out of church like they own the place…. And THAT is part of the problem… they often do. It would seem that the church system, since it rarely treats the poor the same as the rich, since it has set up systems of schooling and training primarily for men to find lucrative, lifetime careers pushing their ideas and other people around from the vantage point of a pulpit, since it doesn’t speak out very often on very serious social and economic issues (when’s the last time you heard (if ever) an entire sermon on the unfairness of jobs with wages that never go up, where one’s hours change from week to week, even if you’re part-time, where men but not women advance, and so on and son on…? Never you say? Me too. The people who make the decisions about how to set up their churches, the people in control of “doctrinal” interpretation of the bible and of other guidelines for Christian life, the folks who tithe the most and make sure the pastors and elder boards know it, and the people sitting in the pews paying for it (just like the shoppers at WAL-Mart who don’t seem to care that everything they are buying is paying for the rent and groceries of Chinese people but very few Americans), they are the ones to blame. But, with so many people warn out from modern life, who’s got the energy, time, or will to speak up about it? I guess it’s you and me sitting out most of the time, Donna. At least we can’t be called hypocrites.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the best hospital in Colorado for coronavirus treatment?
Answer: Thank you, Miss Blocher, for including me in this question; certainly you shall get some good answers from people who utilize aspects of our various health systems, hospitals, and medical professionals in Colorado. Fact is, my experience is extremely limited. I have not seen a doctor for close to 20 years and thank heavens have not been checked into a hospital since January 1996. Further, my associations are very limited, even within my faith-based communities- so I am not in contact with those who converse about these things. I can share University Hospital headquartered in Denver, Colorado, has expanded. It purchased the city hospital known as “Memorial,” in Colorado Springs where I live. University Hospital had a GI surgeon on staff at their Denver campus who saved my life. So, I could recommend people check out that hospital system for the innovative and conscientious spirit that attends their practice. Doctors there will know who on staff does what well and who does certain things not quite as well, though it would be in comments aside where such insights could be gained. Thank you for asking this question and I hope that all the hospitals in Colorado excel at helping those needing medical intervention vis-a-vis COVID-19. I do think it is time for localities, like El Paso County, in Colorado, to take the bull by the horns and get some things down to make sure help is needed when that wave crests… For instance, I sure would love to see innovative metal workers and medical technicians and engineers come together and decide they can build 500 to 1000 fantastic new modern ventilators to be ready within 30 days time from today, April 3, 2020. We should be shaking off that deer-in-the-headlights state of mind and being and stepping up with all the talents and inspiration God is willing to give us to help mitigate this virus’ rampage over our friends, family and neighbors.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the one thing you feel you need to have to be truly content with your life, and what all would you sacrifice to get it?
Answer: Number one thing: Reparations to all I have done wrong to or harmed, financially or otherwise. Especially, to my son, now an adult, whom I wronged through mistreatment. What all would I sacrifice to get it? First, my limited mindset about how best to produce financially has to go. Heretofore, I have operated out of only one framework: Start at the bottom, work hard, and rely on others to advance you. I need a better strategy. Presently, my son (and roommate) brings in more income than I; he is putting more money out for our overhead. It is reasonable, therefore, to be experiencing pressure to do better, both from within, and from without. Old habits die hard. They must be replaced by new ones with more payoffs. The biggest temptation is to hurry up and end the pain of cognitive dissonance, to get back up on that horse again, to once again join the majority of America’s lower-wage earners in a job with no benefits, where you don’t even know your schedule or number of hours from week to week, let alone are enabled to participate in a health insurance network that is worth your heard earned dough. But at least I’d be “doing my best,” right? “Doing right,” by “carrying my fair share,” isn’t that right? WRONG. All I would be doing is all that I have ever done before and it has NEVER worked. It ISN’T realistic that such an approach would ever work; it is an approach that has only functioned to bind me, to keep me down. You sit there in those positions, doing your best, all the while stilling your anger and discontent and reality-based worry about your future, thinking, “I’m doing the right thing;” Consoling yourself, “What else can be done?” Repeating mantras like, “It isn’t all my fault, that’s just the way things are.” Or worst of all, “Don’t worry, it’ll all be over soon.” I cannot and will not do that crap ever again in my life, period. So…. NEW STORY!! I’m flying off, like a straight-edged tangent, bouncing off that circle of enclosure over options that will never open to a different reality, earnestly applying myself instead to simple things, in order to change what has been the status quo in my life for years. I am shutting down what has been my modus operandi and risking being exposed for a phony, an ignoramus, an under-achiever who’s actually just stupid, or dumb, or whatever I think I might “really” be. Simple things first: I am treating my son with more kindness; finding ways to negotiate and stand up for myself with less scream and more “you and me,” not just me; focusing on progress and insisting I make some; making sure there’s something in it for him. In so doing, I am protecting that part of me that conceives; the heart/spirit/brain-womb in me, that captures reality potential floating through the air, that cannot lite upon the dry hard pan ground of sheer drudgery. Instead, I am refusing to off that fertile body’s offspring before it gets a chance to grow. I am protecting it, and in so doing, I am protecting me. Interestingly enough, it seems that baby ideas, like little babies in the human womb, only survive in safety, with something to hang onto. It’s not enough that an idea is good. Or, perhaps in respect of one of America’s biggest over achievers, Jeff Bezos, I can agree that inspiration is 1%, 99% of success is in execution. The support of branches, of a sturdy vine, a labyrinth of options to shelter that baby from what would strike it down, is what comes next. Therefore, besides setting aside many personal patterns related to having a work life that’s DOA, another sacrifice I must make is to let go of control in the establishing of and maintenance of relational connection with others. For the ideas I wish to incubate are nearly all related on one level or another to community building; I like seeing other people pick up the power cords to their own abilities and plug them in. Most of my ideas are related to improving the chances of that happening for individuals by establishing frameworks for community interaction that highlight both needs and opportunities - where the exposures of both of these sides of the coin of life exponentially increases the number of ways in which individuals can exert their own opinions and utilize their usually under-utilized skills, talents and abilities for the common good. I believe we human beings were made to function together like this. So, I am letting myself out of the prison yard of compulsion and death, and moving into the wilds of personal interactions with mindfulness of mutual respect and keeping an open mind, because you never know what you have that someone else needs, or what they have that you might need, or, in the case at hand, that your idea might need. Question: I rarely request days off but finally requested two days off 5 weeks in advance and was denied. What should I do in this case?
Answer: Thank you for including me in this A2A. I am sorry you were treated in a way that sounds like you may not be being treated fairly considering your not imposing on your company before or very infrequently at least for a change in your schedule. It is difficult to be assured as a responder here how helpful I can be without knowing more about your situation, but you might be able to think about what else I would want to know about your relationship with the company in order to design a strategy that can get you closer to your goal: After answer that, I would also ask you these questions: Do you think the denial is related to COVID-19 in anyway? For instance, is your company management concerned about making sure they have their “essential’ labor covered so that they can stay in business? Do you have a special set of skills or knowledge base that is unique and hard for a newcomer or substitute to harness? After you have an understanding from management’s perspective of these issues (remember, knowledge is power), then I would recommend that you make sure you understand the policies already in place prior to COVID-19 that govern taking days off. Now, if you are employed by a large corporate employer, like, say, WAL-Mart, even stated policies that are supposed to protect workers are often overlooked. The best way to handle a corporate culture of this nature is to first voice your concerns and needs to your immediate and then his or her immediate supervisor… go up the chain, face-to-face. Don’t let them beat you down; merely point out, this is what policy says, this is what I need, please respond without discrimination to my request. Ask for a timeline and if they say, we’ll get back to you in a couple days, and then a week goes by, call their HR line and have a conversation. This forces the message UPSTREAM, and in general, right now, while managers may want to exercise significant control over time off, once they know you will speak up for your rights, as long as you are doing your job reasonably well, I think upper management will return to you a reasonable counter proposal. One more thing, many times as employees, if we are trying hard to keep our job, we recognize the power the company has over our wages; therefore, we don’t want to rock the boat, and sometimes, that makes some of us shut down our best features… So, say for instance that two weeks you’re asking for is in part due to family coming in town for a wedding. Well, if that wedding is going to take place the first night of your time off, then you are the most brilliant employee your company has because you are recognizing the risk of bringing contagion back into the place, and you are sacrificing your own vacation time to self-isolate. Which is great. So, here, Jaime, I profess that you may be able to explain your gut instinct or reasoning behind this time off request in away that lets your employer know it is in their best interest to help you out. Good luck, and again, thanks for including me in your A2A!
