Question: What is the most effective way of asking for financial help?
Answer: Determining what is the best way to ask for financial help can be complicated, depending on the asker’s status, ability to pay back if any, purposes of the help, habits of asking for help in the past, ability of the giver/lender, likelihood and frequency of how often the giver/lender one is approaching has to deal with people or organizations coming to them for help. The most successful scenarios depend on the asker’s character and record of production within the community they are going to for help. If, for instance, you are a fantastic volunteer at your church, and have been tithing and an active member for several years, IF the church doesn’t have a policy against it, this person may find their need quickly met. I recall my father, a 13-year old when the Depression hit the USA in 1932, telling about the “only” time he ever borrowed money from someone other going to a bank for establishing a mortgage on a piece of real estate. It was 1945; he had been back from the war for two years, had two children as well as two step children off and on, and had been working for Alexander Film Company as a pilot and then in sales. He had earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration from the Colorado College before he signed up for the Air Corps, so he knew well the value of a dollar SAVED, and that renting was a losing proposition. A small house on Harrison Street came up for sale just a few blocks from the film company’s buildings on North Nevada Avenue, and it had a good price. He approached a man he worked with who was familiar with his work ethic and abilities, and indeed secured a personal loan of $3,000 to put down on what would become his home. By then immediately dividing the place in to an upstairs-downstairs duplex, and securing a solid couple to rent from him, he was able to pay that man back in short order, securing another step in establishing a good reputation which continued to build and be stable over a lifetime of living. If, Tim, you asked this due to the number of needs that may be arising out of COVID-19 based unemployment or paychecks missing in action, I think the best approach is to have a plan of how the need is not going to be reoccurring, because one thing many helpers do not want to do is “throw money down the drain.” Therefore, having a plan of how one will not need this money in the future, and explaining your creative ways and past ways of meeting such difficulties and overcoming them should help. IF someone anticipates needing such help, I would go NOW and ask, because if the COVID-19 situation lasts for a long time, or worsens, people are going to hold back on giving due to their own concerns as trouble comes lapping at their doors, and they will have already given as much as they can, AND their donations will be dropping severely in most cases during this time period. The other key thing about getting help, to me, is asking God first whether and how to meet a problem or need. If, after seeking such counsel, one feels free to ask for help, then do it with the resolve that you are going to get it, no matter what person #1, or person #2, or organization #3, say to you. Don’t let other people’s misgivings about you or helping others get in the way. That’s their issue, not yours. If you need help, go get it. There are plenty of people who have more than enough, and there are people who regardless of how much they have, they will help.

Many hurts that were with, in a sense, insignificant people, people outside of my family or closest of friends, or people whom I didn’t associate with for very long, most of them I have forgiven. But there are a few hurts, like from one of my son’s teachers whom I had great regard for, or some things relating to my ex-husband, where I’ve never just sat in the place of the child/person who got hurt. This is beyond or outside of or more primal than all the intellectual bracketing that one might do around how something came about; it is simply just about the hurt, and I am finding during this time of rest that the COVID-19 is permitting, that the Lord is asking me to turn these things over to him in order to truly forgive. Totally trusting Him, God, Our Father, Jesus, Our Friend, and letting Holy Spirit be in control, is impossible without letting go of these things. So, no. I won’t be at Easter Service. It is far more important to take advantage of this time to follow what will certainly (hopefully, anyway) become more critical directions from our government to shut down the virus’ curve and get the side benefit of becoming open to God’s healing and provision in my interior life. Thanks for asking, Joshua, and may you and yours stay well throughout this challenging time.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How do I change my religion from Christian to Wiccan?
Answer: Being “Christian” isn’t about “having” a religion; it’s about a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. Before you persist in your inclination toward error, ask more of yourself in your Christian life. Not exciting enough? Ask Christ “Why?” He will MAKE it more exciting… if you listen and do what he says. Wanting to see miracles? Ask Christ… He will let you know what part of self you are refusing to lay down and let go of… Then once you have laid that part down, he will lead you to where you can learn to walk in the power that raises the dead, heals the sick, causes the lame to leap for joy, the blind to see, the lepers to have fresh flesh instead of rotting, and so on. Or, you can go to tea with some of the most foul spirits in Creation and invite things into your soul, if you’re not saved, that can take years to get rid of. And every foul filthy thing you pick up will use you, pervert you, twist you, hurt you, and tell you lies about you, the friends you think you are making, the romance you think you’ll be having, the possessions you think you will inherit through this path, and even about the nature of reality itself. Time is short. You don’t rule when your time ends. What if you died right after reading this? Where would you be next?

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Do you want to see a change to a multiparty system in the United States?
Answer: Yes. You know what, if Quora wanted to do a real service at least in the USA, they might just run some simple votes on things like this. I would vote yes.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: My pastor says the Coronavirus COVID-19 is not a huge threat to our lives. Am I wrong to point out his incorrect convictions in front of the congregation during Holy Communion?
Answer: Focus on doing and saying what you SEE Jesus doing and saying… put him before your heart and eyes, and see what he is seeing, do what he is doing, say and speak what he is saying and speaking, WHEN he is saying and speaking it… This takes A LOT of practice, and it isn’t to be treated as a gimmick. And you must work on dying to self so you can Hear and See him. But if He, or Holy Spirit tells you to speak up, then SPEAK UP. The thing to guard and watch is your heart; it can be right on, and full of love and peace, and then when going ahead, you get attacked by people who are not at that moment anyway as close to God as you are and then it can get ugly because people WILL do to you what they did to Christ in small and even bigger ways when their false ways of ego and self-promotion and idol worship (like the idol worship of money, or religious idealism, or political icons, or whatever) are being threatened. There is a lot of witchcraft in the church… lot of influence through money, power and personality. This is not Jesus, this is Man or worse. Be true to him. Love on him. Take your directions from him. But make sure SELF is dead and gone as you make your moves….

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Would having church in the parking lot of churches be okay if everybody stayed in their cars, meaning more than the recommended number of 10 people could attend church because of the coronavirus?
Answer: This is the kind of “theoretical” question that your church leaders need to run past city authorities anonymously to feel them out over it. From a distance, such a gathering might not be well understood by people driving by or living in the area. This could lead to thinking like, “If they can meet, then why can’t I have a party?” Perhaps complying with state and local orders and protocols would be better for now. This is nothing like the trials the believers in the first century after Christ had to face; or like believers face daily finding places to meet to read the bible and worship in China, or other Christ-hostile place on this Earth. I do think it would keep the virus from contaminating church property or from it getting to other people… but why go to that trouble instead of just Facebooking the service, or catching up with one another in a different way? Glad you asked the question, Marcus. Hope you breeze through this time with no personal suffering or loss.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Is there a Christian equivalent to the Wiccan Rede, i.e. "And it harms none, do as you will"?
Answer: There is absolutely no comparison between the two walks. Wicca and its very close relatives paganism and satanism rely upon, foster, seek answers to life’s ills through the acquisition of power and its subsequent employment for reaching desired ends. It is entirely manipulative and never deals with the underlying issue facing all mankind, that issue being what I have recently been referring to as the Burden of Sin. Most Christians will just call the issue sin, but when dealing with Wicca practitioners, I have never met one that doesn’t actively, psychologically and emotionally, keep score. Many “even the score,” by extracting penalties as a way to get things back to an equilibrium. The problem with this “tit-for-tat” approach is that it does nothing to truly change the very platform or viewpoint from where people are relating to the Ultimate, or to the Earth, or to one another. It doesn’t cancel sin; it’s a work-a-round. It can’t overcome constantly taking everything back to the drawing board because of sin… The position Wicca and its close sister and brother take is always a position of power first, then everything else. Christianity is always founded on surrender first to the Ultimate, which is God and Christ and Holy Spirit. Never on power.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How do you deal with a spouse who never apologizes and thinks she's right all the time, especially if she's also a chronic church goer?
Answer: “Chronic” church goer? Obviously you presume she is compulsive at some level… or an “addict.” Many people who have such a “hard” exterior, or are that hard to reach, they’re hard to deal with. Therefore, it may behoove you to seek outside help. I agree with what one of your responders have said… that it sounds like things are not very happy between the two of you… Like she is functioning on one wavelength, and you another. Effective and enduring bridges for communication take a lot of practice and are most usually introduced by someone outside of the dyad. Someone who can deal with the two of you as equals, so in experiencing validation from him or her in a therapeutic session, that is served up to both of you regularly, the two of you can begin to try out the same mutually-respectful communication strategies at home. If you can make the effort to get her to want counseling, and if you both will give it your best shot, my completely shooting from the hip guess is that you will both be in quite a different position a year from now, and both of you will be happier and experience less stress. I have a feeling that you actually like this person, if only she would get off her high horse and probably an underlying strident need for control.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the most underhanded thing a co-worker did to you that they mistakenly thought went unnoticed?
Answer: I had a witch (well, if you stick to witches as females and males as warlocks, a warlock then) trying to pray me out of working at Xerox, in a call center where I worked in tech support helping pre-paid Verizon cell phone customers. His little cubby was connected at the corner to mine. He was SHOCKED when he realized in the middle of his “work” (whatever it’s called - prayers or chants or incantations or Hail Mary’s) that I was looking straight at him. I had stood up and was looking down at his mostly bald head after my computer and other electronics went haywire for about the third or fourth time that evening. No, I’m not superstitious, for those who don’t “believe.” I knew what he was, what he did, how he thought, and a few other things about him. He literally jumped in his seat when he looked up and saw me. It was a bit of comic relief, because it is such a pain to be pestered by, interfered with, harassed by the demonic that witches, warlocks, shamans, and so forth release. Some “practitioners” may know that this is what they are releasing> Most, however, are deceived and think they’ve tapped into some power that is ultra-human; it isn’t. It is demonic. The demons are using them. It’s rather like anything else we humans “use” in order to control things around us or within us (like our feelings, our status, our access and so forth) instead of focus on being deserving of the things we would have or enjoy and putting out the effort necessary to get them legitimately. Later that night, he would insist, out of nowhere, that the lady who was giving me rides home at night (the buses to that area of town stop at 5:45 PM, and she and I were slated to get off at 8:00), stay behind IN THE MIDST of a sudden, prolific snowstorm. But that just made me laugh as well (after perhaps a small sigh… as it was REALLY cold outside and the snow was literally already a foot deep AND I had no one else to call for a ride…), because I KNEW God would provide a ride AND that he would find out about it and that would only piss him off him more. So, instead of hemming and hawing after finding out what he did, I celebrated: I praised God within my Spirit, put on all my winter duds, went outside and after walking around the show shovelers in the front, began to enjoy a beautiful night winter scene. As I walked down the three block-long driveway from 2400 W Garden of the Gods to 30th Street, I thought about how long it might take me to walk the entire way… if worse came to worse. It was more than 10 miles. Then, I looked up, and just as I reached the intersection, there came my chariot, a black older jeep headed north on 30th, the street that goes right by Garden of the Gods Park. Waving my arm, the driver’s window rolled down and a young man asked, “Do you need a ride?” “Yes,” I happily cried out, “I do!” then added, “but it’s not in the direction you’re headed, and it might take you 30 minutes in this weather to get me home… Are you sure you want to?” “Sure, no problem,” as his female passenger began to open the door on the opposite side of the jeep and beckoned me in out of the cold. I got comfy, and marveled at how amazing God is, how PERFECT he is, how MUCH he cares for each of us, even me. I got to enjoy the ride home with young newlywed couple telling me all about how they met and where they felt their lives were headed. I couldn’t have picked two fast-friends better myself. 1 Peter 2:9 KJV “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light…” He pulls us OUT of darkness, into light, from every situation that is bleak, into new opportunities to live reclaimed and justified by Christ Jesus.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Can I still ask for forgiveness if I know that watching adult films is wrong, but I keep doing it anyway?
Answer: There is nothing wrong with asking for forgiveness, ever, about anything… The best thing in the world is to let God into any and every bad thing you do. I recall a bad habit I had that was a real time waster and certainly never added anything of real value to my life. I began killing that thing by bringing God into the experience… After all, angels, and in fact the cloud of witnesses, believers you knew when they are alive who are now in heaven, and other beings see every thing you do; they can’t all tell what you are thinking, but they can see everything you do and gather things about your thoughts by other indicators. So, first, I would think about the fact that God and his company ALL could see me. Then besides asking for forgiveness, I would ask for help. The point isn’t feeling badly, the point is to stop doing stuff that doesn’t help us. In the case of porn, some people say it helps to think of the people in the film as, well, people. They could be your sister, brother, father, mother, and so forth. Is it good for them that there is a demand for their product? I don’t think so. Asking for forgiveness is a beginning; considering the arena of heaven watching helps a person see their activities as a testimony for or against Christ, and to see that their own little world is much more important than they think (which should actually INCREASE self-esteem, not destroy it, which encourages self-empowerment); and humanizing those you are objectifying can also help break up that compulsion. The behaviors I have dropped as a result of this type of reflection were further destroyed by truly recognizing the impact of the behaviors on my feelings. I felt badly after I did certain things, or didn’t do things I was supposed to. I began to understand that while I thought I was getting away with something, I was actually participating in victimizing myself. It took time, but I got sick of the cost. That is another part of the equation, one’s focus or framework, for evaluating a behavior… Focusing on the cost if you DON’T want to keep doing something (and on the BENEFIT, if you DO want to get yourself to do something. So, no, there is nothing wrong, EVER, with asking for forgiveness. It is a step in the right direction.

Instead, it MUST accomplish on a large scale, what those Men of Old did… it MUST admit, if JESUS SAID IT “Because I go to the Father, YOU WILL DO MORE THAN ME…” WE WILL DO IT. This part of the Christian life isn’t just about signs and wonders, in fact, signs and wonders are ancillary to the more important “works” of living outside of time, in and through other realms… WALKING in heaven… SEEING in the Spirit…. and STOP rejecting the supernatural life in Christ. HE WANTS US TO WALK ON WATER and called us OF LITTLE FAITH when we balked at and did not understand that stuff. TOO MANY believers and certainly leaders thereof have TOTALLY written off “that stuff” as unnecessary, and OFTEN as completely suspect, even corrupt, or heretical. My God, my God, Jay, many don’t even believe in healing… As IRIS Ministries (Mozambique) co-founder Heidi Baker said Jesus told her, when she was balking at giving up her and her husband’s mission and orphanage in the Philippines to go serve the children and poor in Africa, I DIED SO THERE WOULD ALWAYS BE ENOUGH. When she went ahead and, again, “believed,” God started producing the miracle of supernatural reproduction, and not just of food, but of other things as well. So, READ ENOCH. Jesus quoted him. READ IT. And figure out, with God’s help, HOW TO DO WHAT JESUS DID, and EVEN MORE.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why has it become so hard for me to find a church home?
Answer: You divulge nothing of your quandry that could help me help you get a better outcome… I don’t know what you are looking for, what you have or are doing in order to “find” it, or what you think of as “so hard.” Do you conflict with people? Are you hurting from a “last” encounter at a prior place of fellowship and worship? Have you recently dropped an affiliation with a particular denomination? Was your search begun by a geographic move? Are there other things in the constellation of support in your life (family, friends, marriage, school, work, hobbies…) that have changed making you perhaps disoriented in life in general? Did someone die? There are all things, and there are more, that could make making a new acquaintance, a new friend, getting a new job, all difficult, let alone finding the pathway to a good (i.e. long-term/lasting) decision about selecting a good church for you. I can provide with only some general thoughts about such a quest, and I can share some frustrations I have had in “church” life in general the last several years, and perhaps if you relate, my sharing could help you figure out how to set a path for a successful church-home search. One, there are some things you can get out of many churches, even if you aren’t ready to settle down yet. For instance, you can both serve a place you don’t know but are visiting by making a small donation, or even by bringing some store bought cookies (still in their wrapper) or other food treat, just call the office of the place you are going to visit and ask them what time their services are and arrive 15 to 20 minutes in advance and find the person who takes care of treats or coffee hour. If you approach your visits this way, it puts you in control of the visit, which you want to be, because you are researching these places to find one that fits you. No one else can tell you which place that will be. It also allows you to be dutiful, which is a big plus in the Christian walk of life, as it, first, gets your mind off of you, and two, puts you on Jesus’ wavelength in terms of being concerned about your neighbor. Two, take a note pad and when the preacher/pastor/priest/minister begins his or her lesson, write some notes. Review them later; it will remind you where you were and it may help you make a good decision when you feel you are ready. Three, keep that note pad handy and put down a couple phone numbers of people you meet there to call with follow up questions. One important question, I think, is “How long have you been at this church?” While length of sojourning isn’t the whole picture, if you discover there are several, or many or even half of the congregation that have stayed with the organization, AND if you think these people are healthy, intelligent, fun, sane, then this is something that you should pay attention to and perhaps credit them a bit on your list as you reflect on whether or not this or that church is for you. Four, when you are doing suggestion two, (writing notes on the lesson), think HARD about how much the points apply to you. I find that no matter where I attend church, God is ALWAYS got good points to make to me about how to solidify my commitment to him, and how to live and practice Christian virtues and way of life. When you are reviewing the many options out there, think upon what you like, and sense, and what you do not like… EVERY human institution on Earth is flawed; EVERY human being, including every priest, pastor, minister, is FLAWED. So, we have to find ways to work with others, build relationships with others where we minimize their damage to us and ours to them that might spring up because of our shortcomings, and maximize the extent to which our relations may be mutually advantageous. If, Quora question writer, you are lonely, or in a state of denial about something in our life, or in grief about something, you will have to be careful; and in fact, sometimes the seeking out of professional counseling before you decide to “tie the knot” with a religious fellowship might benefit you. I am in transition, and I do attend a church up the street from me. My experience tells me that God is VERY purposeful about where we go in life… that is to say, God is ALWAYS laying out provision for us to learn from and to glean from so that we can get on with our mission that he wants us to accomplish for him. For me, this little church up the hill, there are many negatives. They are stodgy, their spiritual eyes for the most part are yet closed; most of their members either work for the pastor or are related to those who do, or are close friends and/or relatives to the other leaders there; new people do not return; their attempts to extend their reach are failing and have for year; and it’s kind of a 25–55 age group. The strengths however are good marriages; commitment; devotion; seriousness of purpose; true and genuine love of God and one another; regular effort and consistency in their pursuits. As a believer, I don’t know if you feel this way, but it is almost impossible for me to NOT like and even love everybody on some level; I think that’s just how God the Holy Spirit operates within me/us. What I have to realize, and perhaps you will find this to be true as well, my time is VERY VERY VERY important to me today. I don’t want to waste it. Therefore, I insist that I have reasons for what I am doing, where I am going; how I am talking to others and so on. The costs associated with not being mindful are just too high. I have no idea if what I’ve shared will help you or anyone else who reads this, but I hope it does. Feel free to PM me in Quora if you wish. God bless you on your search, and don’t give up. Sometimes things have to be worked out behind the scenes, even in our own souls, somewhat unconscious to us, before we can move forward. Again, may the Good God you know, bless you with wisdom and patience for this important endeavor. Shalom!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How would you describe your ideal church?
Answer: My ideal church is not a church, per se, it is the VERY modest worship place in the midst of a larger compound of also very modest structures that together serve as admin and supply headquarters for a local mission. The worship “center” is NOTHING to boast about; it may hardly have walls… but enough protection to keep the wind, rain, drifting snow, and very cold months out… The floor might not even be anything but dirt or mats on some dirt; but the dirt is soft enough to stand on barefoot, to sit on, the kneel on, to get on your face before the Lord on. It is not a fancy place. But people over the days, weeks, months and years, they have left offerings of sorts, shawls, colorful textiles, to serve as helpful barriers against the wind along the walls. The chairs might be plastic, or old card table chairs, though not with sharp or rusted edges; it’s probably a mixture. There might be some small rugs here and there for the older or the ones with problems or coming in with children in tow, to sit on during service/sermon; to gather on to listen to a slower song or melody. There is an upraised stage… but not very high; you see this is not a big place and never will be because this is a place where people don’t disappear into a crowd. They can be private, and they can keep to themselves, but that is there choice; we don’t do mobs here. When it’s big enough to go bigger, we don’t hang on and control it; we send the new off like a little ship at sea… It becomes a tree; IT now then serves as a new oasis for those who will come to God. The people there are every color, every educational background, though, frankly, most, not so much, because many educated people think they don’t need God or are too busy for God or …. whatever. There are ALL ages here. THERE are A LOT of older people here; very old. Not just 70’s or 80’s. There are people here who are blind, lame, smelly, even stinky, corroding even… But most don’t stay that way. There are a LOT of children here. They are allowed to sing and dance and they often lay hands on people, even the very very very young… two year olds… three year olds…. laying hands on the deaf, and they hear; people with MS get healed; odd broken bones straighten when the 10-year old boy lays his hand on them. There is a minister and his wife, or a minister and her husband; they didn’t think they would stay here for long. They thought they were just sent for a “season,” but it’s now been 30 years, and they don’t call the place they came from “home,” anymore, for this has become their home. They build houses for people with nothing; they move God’s hand to bring in doctors to people who cannot afford them; they believe in the abandoned, the wretchedly treated, the foul-looking ones, the ones with firey anger in their eyes and a sour look on their faces. They don’t give up on thieves, lepers, polio victims. They’ve seen the miracle working power of God over and over and over and over again. They’ve been at their wits’ end time and time again where God was merciful to them, brought them sustenance, encouragement, education, training, help, means, transport, healing, protection, promotion, enhancement. They know a God who always knows where they are and how they are and they know a Father who never forgets them and always enjoys being with them; they know a friend named Jesus who is SO HAPPY to be with them. He is among FRIENDS when he is with them. They delight God, and he abides in them, bringing unquenchable hopefulness, birthing unstoppable determination, seeding a multitude of spiritual crops in them all the while watching his friends follow in his footsteps. This is my ideal church, it is filled with God, not things. It is filled, once rectified to God and reconciled to love, and on the right path, with people who are filled with love for all. It does not covet, IT does not kill, IT does not betray, lie, steal; IT stands, rejoices, persists, gives, stretches out, receives, returns, sows and reaps all according to his auspicious will which never leads them astray. It might look a little like this (and it would be utterly undone if ever compared to such a place as this): Courtesy Pinterest “What Mama Heidi’s World Looks Like In Mozambique” IRIS MINISTRIES where snakes are beheaded and the demonized are freed.

Question: What are you most afraid of during Covid 19?
Answer: SOCIALLY: Spreading it to someone else… I do not have it to the best of my knowledge, but it would be awful to carry it to someone vulnerable and cause them any suffering or worse… POLITICALLY: Watching events unfold to the point of everyone being asked to receive a mark in the hand or forehead to buy or sell. Name: Sara Stone
Question: Does Joel Osteen of the Lakewood Church preach a mix of positive bias and Christianity?
Answer: I watched Joel watching his guess speaker, Singapore Mega-church pastor Joseph Prince, speak. What I think I saw on Joel’s face was relief from strain. While it is impossible to know through the distance of television, I think I see evidence of Joel Osteen being a genuine Christian. His relief, I think, was from having a peer (a super rich Christian pastor who sticks, in large part, to a “positive,” uplifting tone) up on his stage, as though it was comforting to see someone else espouse basically positive stuff. Christianity IS a positive bias: It is positive toward LIFE, the EARTH, ALL human beings, HOPE, LOVE. Science has proven that smiling literally releases endorphins which help the brain engage in productive problems solving, whilst anger drops the IQ like 40 points immediately when it comes on a person. I think people speaking positively drive some people nuts, Christian or not. Some people walk around comforted by the cloak of cynicism and pessimism to buffer them from the ups and downs of the world’s ability to punch holes and dents into our small and big dreams. These guys don’t do that. Maybe it’s because they have learned positive begets positive and negative only seeds negative. As I’ve said before, I see self-discipline, patience, joy, long-suffering and other positive things in Joel Osteen; it takes a lot in this world, and it is good if what supports one is fidelity and commitment, to keep even a positive face on, even if it’s fake. I don’t think Joel Osteen is fake. I see signs of suffering, which to me, is where the pedal hits the medal in the Christian walk, if the believer being observed has consistent signs of facing suffering without picking up that old rusty sword of the flesh, based in appetites and aggression that likes to get its own will done at any cost. But, I could be wrong.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Could Mormons be considered a cult or heresy by the actual definition due to how much they deviate from other Christians?
Answer: They are considered heretical because they do not believe in the divinity of Christ. They believe in being Christ-like but they do not believe He is God. Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is it like living in Colorado during the coronavirus?
Answer: It’s really kind of whacked. Like the rest of the country, we get updates nearly daily from the governor and from our city mayors… and today I saw how our state is banning get togethers that number 10 or more… It’a like wow, for real? But I’m for it, and I think most of the public are, if it will save lives. Really it’s kind of exciting… The amount of data this outbreak is furnishing scientists of all sorts, in the medical/health related sciences, in economics, the social sciences… logistics… fascinating, really. I don’t mean to make light of the suffering. Obviously this is very threatening to people who end up having to engage their all to get this thing out of their way in order to continue living! Tonight, driving my son home from a super WAL-Mart where he works… the streets were empty… it was 10:30 at night on a Wednesday, and you can really see the impact. Our Mayor Suthers has shut down all restaurants and even the historic Golden Bee at the classic Five Star Resort, The BroAdmoor Hotel, got its covers pulled when a local TV station decided to do story on them not shutting their doors…. The weirdest tales are the ones from the “field” my family comes in closest contact with… the world of WAL-Mart… The cashiers there have been ordered to not allow sales of more than one toilet paper package per customer… and if a customer tries tag-teaming it with a friend, or spouse, the cashiers are supposed to deny the purchase and grab the extra packages to restock. The people in Asset Protection have been given new duties. Now, in this department, there are novices (they “guard” the doors and check your receipts and try to stop people walking out with a basket full of goods….) and there are specialists with a higher pay grade. Just last night, or the night before, they had to stop this lady who had a cart filled to the brim with food… she was in panic mode and they caught her… took her in the side room… The police that come to this particular WAL-Mart in Colorado Springs come in one or two patrol cars and stay much of the day. They help check backgrounds and take down folks that are unfortunate enough to try and rip WAL-Mart off. But this, apparently, is not enough, as the WAL-Mart staff sit and watch a multitude of screens running video feeds from hundreds of cameras in the store that are fixed to the walls, ceiling, and now in the aisles as well, those cameras can even READ YOUR TEXT ON YOUR PHONE - I’ve seen it!) to catch shoplifters. This didn’t stop one person sleeping in an aisle three nights in a row apparently. But anyway, Asset Protection has been given a new duty due to the novel corona virus… they’ve been assigned at times to stand IN the toilet paper aisle to keep people from violating the new maximum purchase: One package per customer. At a different WAL-Mart, an employee was literally knocked to the floor when trying to break up a fight between to customers over TP. The employee suffered an injury because of it and the hours of access to the store for the public were cut. Everyday you go in there, something new is all out… First it was the TP, as everybody knows, and the hand sanitizer, and the rubbing alcohol, and Vitamin C and wipes. Then the thermometers. Then certain canned goods. Tonight as I picked up wet and dry food for our two wonderful felines, behold, three shelves of one half of a 80-foot long dairy and juice aisle were TOTALLY empty. Even CHIPS, yeah, CHIPS, are being stocked up on. My son joked about how the guy buying all the chips up must have been the first one to stock up on TP… he’s just moved from something super necessary if you’re going to go be holed up for several months, to the joys of life, like salsa and tortilla chips! The social distancing thing, it’s actually kind of great… I mean, if you think about it, who wants to rub shoulders with every stranger out there on a regular basis? We dropped into a Dollar Store today where the people in line were respecting the six-foot rule. It was great. Gosh, maybe we can actually re-acclimate the entire population to respect one another… Maybe we can help people understand that cussing, cursing, hitting others, yelling, bailing on other people, are actually really beyond rude to others… they’re also bad for the person doing those behaviors. We also saw for the first time tonight our first “COVID-19 Test Here” across from Memorial Park and the Velodrome (close to downtown) which has been shut down for the next several weeks. Churches aren’t meeting. Kids are home for extended break. My son has a friend with an 8 year old son… she has been having a hard time finding work, and now this hits. But there’s no day care while the kids are on this extended break, so, now things are getting super desperate for her. The city 211 phone line in Colorado Springs advertised that there is a special fund being set up for people out of work to help with rent, utilities and so on… but frankly, there just isn’t THAT MUCH “free money,” around, so I seriously doubt there will be much funds for that unless the state pulls it off with help from the feds. This state, and especially this city, are conservative in certain ways… spending being one of those ways. They’re going to be saving money for those ventilators that some people might need… But, overall, Michael Trivedi, it’s okay here in Colorado Springs, and hopefully in the rest of the state as well.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Do you fear for your life during COVID-19?
Answer: Not exactly. I have been working with disease symptoms for a few years to identify how some mental and emotional habits seem to influence how my body receives, rejects, or just totally ignores certain disease patterns… That may sound like a bunch of gobbly gook but I observed a pastor several years ago in his early 70’s (he’s passed away now) who was a marine gunner in the Vietnam War and got hit with Agent Orange while there and after returning from Vietnam, got real sick, a year after he met Jesus Christ and was “saved.” He had tremors, periodic blindness, became so debilitated he had to use a wheelchair, but he kept reading this bible thing that said Jesus paid for our healing with the stripes ripped into his back by the Roman soldiers. If that was true, he asked himself, why wasn’t he manifesting that healing? So, the man, named Elery Mayo, one of the kindest, most loving and honest pastors I’ve ever met, “pressed in.” He said it took him seven years to learn to walk in the healing that Jesus Christ paid for for all mankind on that cross that day… By the time I knew Elery, he said he only experienced MS symptoms when he was trying to help someone heal from MS… It had been fully 30 years since he had had any symptoms apart from that kind of interaction. He admitted he had gone in for testing some years prior which showed there were still lesions on his brain or somewhere… but he no longer paid any visits to the doctors for anything… I find, frankly, that when I focus on the symptoms, I start feeling them, or some may say “manifesting” them… then when I get absorbed in some other thoughts, they literally disappear. So, I’m not walking around terrified… It isn’t pleasant to think about it. I do know, beyond any shadow of a doubt, that these things originate in the spiritual realm, both the individual things we may encounter as well as these things which are more “global…” But I know where to take my fear… and on a very basic level, there are things that bother me about me far more than anything my body manifests. There is so much crap still hanging around me because of my own attachment to obstacles. It’s a good thing that some of these old mental and emotional habits CAN impact us physically, otherwise, we might get the idea that we have to keep on staying the same old way, even if it’s killing us. Thank you for including me in this A2A, Ann. Hope you and yours stay free from all illnesses now and always.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are narcissists really hiding low self-esteem?
Answer: You know, I really don’t know or understand the field of psychology’s definition and portrayal of narcissism. There are for instance, a lot of traits that experts in this field discuss as being demonstrated by President Trump. But I hear so much jealousy at times, and so much underestimation of the complexity of the human mind and soul, I just can’t get into the label. It seems like most of the other Cluster B personality types are treated with some deference if not compassion, but narcissists seem to get crucified, not just by people who “fell for the ploys” of a so-called narcissist (and here’s something, by the way I wonder why even the mental health professionals never ask those people who were “so hurt” by the N, which is WHY did you fall for it? Why were you SO hungry for what they were offering that you bought into it? THOSE questions I had to answer in order to get free of ANY resentment I had about a guy I met who ran baths for me, cooked for me…. etc etc, but ended up being HIGHLY controlling and abusive) but also by the professionals who are supposed to help them. This makes no sense to me, as if it is a sickness, or disorder, why in the world are mental health professionals so “mad” at them? It’s like getting mad at the alcoholic… Or at a toddler for spilling milk. What’s the point? That’s why I think NPD is an invalid assessment of root causes and configuration of drives, motives, thinking and feeling patterns and so on. In fact, when it comes to Cluster B, my personal opinion is that much of the “hysterical” components are driven by rage/fear/terror that was caused by genuine abandonment. It’s like nerves to certain central aspects of human functioning were left raw and uncovered. I witnessed a lady, OMGod, leaving her, OMGod, I cannot hardly write about stuff like this because it is so wretched and so PERMANENTLY damaging unless people are really reached by unusual love or even miraculous power and insight from God, she left her baby older than a few months, but not that much older, in a crib crying and crying and crying for HOURS because the authorities told her that was okay while she tended to her studies. OMGOD don’t you know those vocal chords are all they got. I didn’t do that with my child. I did what a pediatrician Sears suggested… I was BONDED, on-demand bonding. At great personal sacrifice, I answered that baby’s call. And when his father took a two-week drop in to see him a few times when he was 18 months old, he was amazed and said the child was one of the happiest he’d ever seen. And he was. The bad stuff in me didn’t happen until later (dominating, stupid yelling, unreasonable expectations, and so on and so on it would make you barf)… If my kid made a face at food (he got all organic good stuff and basically loved everything - and still will try anything, even squid (no thank you for me), octopus etc… because if he made a face0 I just mirrored it and THEN let him make his own decision. I should have done that with every other aspect of his life. Point is, that slightly less than a toddler that lived down the hall from me did NOT learn to self-comfort, because he wasn’t getting comforted, over and over and over again. Instead, he was left in a state that can only be called cruel. My God, how can people abandon all sense and do that to a child. So, if the ONLY way a child can get his basic needs met, including for attention, one of the most primal needs of all, and his parents essentially REQUIRE him to manipulate to do so, why is the child the bad guy even when he grows up??? Doesn’t make sense to me. So, I can’t answer if N’s are fighting low “self-esteem;” I postulate that most of their outward behaviors arose out of specific, consistent conditioning for empty performance that made his or her PARENTS feel good; it is like he or she is a mirror or echo chamber for them. In the case of that less-than-a-toddler’s mother, she was just plain selfish. It takes a LOT to give to an infant. A LOT. It takes everything you’ve got. And in the case of my son, and one child does not a study make, but one thing about him, his memories are intact. He remembers nursing, he remembers teething, he remembers things from his first year, and no, this is not about hearing about it and then imagining it. I think memories stay intact when calm and comfort and low fear is present and that the opposite happens when there is wickedness that hurts a child. I think THAT’S one reason why such people described as narcissists are so hard to help; they don’t know what they are dealing with and it’s at such a deep deep level it’s hard to get to. But not impossible. Nothing’s impossible. I also think they are hard to help because people who are inclined to “hate” them, have pride about their own, what they perceive, as manners, or even altruism; empathy… People who have pride about these so-called “good,” or “desirable” behaviors (which many assume indicate some better internal state) just plain learned to do them from watching them over and over and over again, and hopefully, being treated with empathy and so forth in their own cribs, playpens, highchairs, and laps. What did I hear recently from some movie… what was it? Oh yeah, from a Netflix Original Marvel show… “If you want to know the truth, don’t have an opinion.”

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is one piece of simple advice that actually changed your life?
Answer: There is an unhappy record of suicide in three generations on my dad’s family’s side… now, keep in mind, nothing is an absolute, and in each of these cases, there was not just a parent from my father’s line, but also a parent from another family line, but the stats are not good: 1) My father’s cousin committed suicide in her 70’s - started a fire in the townhouse when no one else (thankfully) was there. 2) My father’s brother’s eldest son committed suicide in his late 20’s. 3) My father’s brother’s other son had a son, who at age 17, a day or two off Prozac for depression, committed suicide. In none of these cases was alcohol a habit. Therefore, one of the best pieces of advice I ever got related to why no one would want to become a suicide if they knew some important facts up front. The advice giver, an exegetical bible study teacher/pastor, explained suicide is the biggest joke, in hell: “The” Devil laughs because he knows suicide cuts short the rewards we WILL get on Earth, no matter how long we live or how much we suffer, as well as the rewards we will get in Heaven.” I reaped from this man’s input two profound benefits: First, I recognized suicide as a thing, a force, an event, that was “beyond” me… that I possibly could not control its rising up or its eventuality. This gave me humility in the face of it as a threat to my life and to any possibly good outcome in my life. Humility in turn, if desire to confound a thing rather than to be confounded by it is present, allows for one to study to become more prepared to deal with possible risk. Second, it helped me gain objectivity… that is, it helped me see the thing, suicide, as something that in a sense, that plays a role, possibly, in SOMEONE ELSE’S PLANS. That piece of news helped because when it comes to THAT player, “the devil,” I was not motivated to agree with his plans. In fact, I should like to rob him of anything and everything that he thinks he has coming to him. Therefore, whenever I have had to deal with my own tendency toward depression, which got acutely bad after my son was born, for literally about four to five years, and then later on for a couple years as I neared the age of 60, I was conscious of the risks involved in letting myself get too low. It prompted me to be both conscious about my state of mind, AND about attempting to activate some “possibility” thinking about addressing those low feelings BEFORE they ripened into something worse. I appreciate being asked to contribute to this library of answers on this question about advice and truly hope it benefits someone who might also be facing a challenge in this area of life.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What do you think of the theory that says that Padre Pio self-inflicted stigmata?
Answer: It is nonsense . The prolific spiritual fruit of Padre Pio, including the carrying of incredible priestly workload of performing five masses a day and taking 100′s of confessions per day, trans-locating (through the spirit of God being moved in his yet-ultra-dimensional body to thousands of places all over the world), keeping up with copious correspondence from admirers, inquirers and personal friends from all over the world (the Vatican had to acquire additional garages in the environs around San Giovannii Rotundo to store it), the manifestation of yet other perfected-in-Christ miracle-working power, like healing broken bones, curing cancer, re-establishing sight, does not come from a manipulator or a phoney. This fellow, this son of Italy, this man of God, this loyalist to the Catholic Church was (and is today) the real thing. The theory had been perpetuated by haters of God, and/or by those who believe God is a well-mannered being who would never forcefully through the demonstration of other-worldly power… i.e. God would never do “that,” (be so grotesque a Supreme Being that he would manifest miracles), and by mere satanists who just will do anything to avert man’s understanding of the true revelation of God and of his own destiny in God, which includes, for the supremely self-motivated and devoted to dying to self, WALKING IN THAT POWER. There is also plenty of biographical information on Padre Pio from first hand accounts, by scientists and doctors, trying to replicate the wounds the way Padre Pio’s were through the application of reddish serums, like mixtures of iodine with other things, that it would be impossible to do so. Padre bled two pints of blood per day, it is said, through seven wounds of Christ (two hands, two feet, the crown of his head, the stripes on his back and the wound on his side), as well as suffered an eighth wound (on one of his shoulders) that came from Jesus carrying the cross. His pain and suffering was highly amplified every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, when he would endure a “repetition” of the pains from Christ’s passion. His disposition which was in the natural genteel and understanding from childhood (where he would watch his fellows play soccer in the field as he laid by on grass sunlit reading the bible), but transformed utterly and majestically through his 53 years as a cloistered monk bonded to his duties as a spiritual father, and assisting untold thousands all over the globe. When it was time to plan for the future, his pet project was the building of a hospital for those who would not be touched by the miraculous touch of God to their bodies, and to do this, he touched and moved the souls of many around the Earth to help with funding the “La Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, the Home for the Relief of Suffering,” which opened on May 5, 1956 [wiki stats]. To make sure Godly hands were on the staff, in one case, he informed a parishoner who had consulted him on his need for a job, that he would be the chief cook for the new institution. When told this, the man was incredulous and expressed his doubt to the Padre, stating, “But I do not know how to cook at all!” Yet, when the hospital was finished and the man stepped into the kitchen for the first time, he exclaimed how he didn’t understand how he knew where everything was and that the knowledge of how to cook and run a kitchen was instantly in him. The bible says that if one were to write every thing that Christ did, it would fill the whole Earth; yea, it is so with every supreme follower of Christ, willing to truly DIE TO SELF and live for God, which means living for their fellow man. It is certainly so with kind and loving Padre Pio, friend to the sinner, saint, and all those in between.

Question: What is the most unbelievable thing you have ever heard preached during church?
Answer: I think the worst service to church attendees I have ever heard, and it still makes me just flutter my eyes at Fate’s cruel twists and turns, was the one at Chapel of Our Savior by Rev. Dayle Casey right after 9 - 11. Now, Father Casey is a diligent man, and known within his Episcopal denomination for his theology… his thinking about God stuff. The place was PACKED. Now, I am saying it far more simplistically than it was… for Father Casey is a thorough man with a broad reaching intellect, a good memory, and an abiding interest in things that make sense, but he wouldn’t fall into the category of ever just reaching PAST man’s corrupt mind, through the obstacles that surround his heart to that beating heart throb within that needs to know and be often reminded that God loves us, that we are to love God, and that we are to love others. Boy I would have handled that differently if I were in that pulpit that day. I wouldn’t have been talking theory, or good points of theology, I would have been talking to my fellow American about our need for one another, our need for God, our need to COME TOGETHER for many cooperative ventures, INCLUDING maintaining and growing our churches for the equipping of the saints and the succoring of those in trouble or in need. I was aghast. The deep needs that were in the hearts of people there, who needed, desperately to hear the Gospel in the simplest of forms and ways… but that is beyond many, not just the likes of the Reverend Casey.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: I was learning about the Book of job and Jobs sufferings and it almost made me tear up, does anybody feel the same way when reading it?
Answer: Thank you for making me aware of the opportunity to answer this interesting question. No, I have not felt that way about Job… But I have felt what I think is that same sentiment in other cases, where there is a walking next to the characters in the bible, sharing in their sorrow, frustration or consternation. Name: Sara Stone
Question: Is sinning the same thing as being selfish?
Answer: The Kingdom of God is not this place; and sin is not about morals and laws. Sin is done by a mind run by the temporal… not by the Love of, or Love From God. If a person abides in God, they will not sin. Sometimes God will indeed make our “needs,” even our “wants” (which are both inherently selfish) a priority. He is a GOOD Father… and a good Father sees that his kids are fed, clothed and protected from the elements… A woman who is a mom to six kids under 12 is worn out, put out, ignored by her husband, her in-laws, her own parents, and about to become undone. Is she sinning, OR selfish by putting her foot down and making arrangements that will remove her from the chance of a nervous breakdown? I think not. But the real issue to me, isn’t the touch not, taste not, steal not, murder not; it’s the LOVE bit… Love God, and Your neighbor as yourself… This is the solution. It’s not an “opposite” framework, it’s a “my ways are high above your ways” thing… It’s a bringing heaven to Earth thing, or vice versa. The biggest downfall of the modern church, which crept into it like a wee bit of leaven in a big big loaf, is moralism. The retention of rules and regulations that continue to focus man on sin and to maintain a “sin consciousness,” as opposed to insisting on the truth thru example and a truly different way of life all the time… Living BY faith and Walking in THE Power of God. His Will for us is to Love Him madly, and to love others as ourselves. There is only ONE way to do that, and that is to abide in Him so closely and fervently that you will often look like nothing other than just plain weird to the rest of the world. But even they will like the results… the miracles, the healings, the words fitly spoken, the conscientiousness where we serve and do our labors not as men-pleasers but always as unto to the Lord. Takes a lot of work and effort, but without that Love thing goin’ on; it’s all just clanging cymbals. Thanks for the question, Richard Joseph Strachan!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Should Christians participate in Halloween?
Answer: John Ramirez’s father was a genuine, demon-lead, demon-run, warlock… John began his training when very young. Over time, John learned to make sacrifices to various demonic idols, to set curses on people that would result in their literal deaths; to drink the blood of animals and more… Then John Ramirez was saved in 1999, after 25 years of continual “work” for the “other” side. He calls Halloween “The Devil’s Holiday…” and when he said this, I thought to myself, this is just someone who is being overly cautious… but I recalled his mentioning that witches and warlocks and worse go through the grocery stores where you and I buy their Halloween candy, lay hands on it and set curses and enchantments to bring YOUR kids, MY kids, into a world of darkness that will take over their lives. Then I saw a young man and his wife sharing on Facebook how they participate in Halloween because they won’t let the devil stop them from enjoying something that is fun for kids… that they won’t be done in by fear or by having someone else telling them what to do. Hm. Self-will - NOT a friend of Believers. I know the genuine faith-based reasons for All Saints Day; it was initiated in 609 by Pope Boniface IV to honor all believers who, as the church put it back then, “had attained heaven” [WIKI]. It’s not a bad idea… and I don’t think its intentions were evil, but today, this “Holy-Day” (or rather the night before… “Hallow-eve”) has become defiled. Satanist, witches and warlocks, have appropriated not just Halloween, but the entire month of October for their dedication to all that can come against God’s plans for mankind, which is redemption for every soul… the resurrection of every dead spirit in every man, woman and child who is presently separated from God. I believe that it is a GOOD thing to think upon examples … people who have gone to a place in their Christian faith that stir us to repentance, action, devotion, better ways of thinking and living… A day set aside to reflect upon good examples, or even 10 minutes every day of every year… Wonderful! But Halloween? Not in my house. Not any more. The potential cost is WAY too high. Remember, it’s CHILDREN that you’re putting out there to whatever door, physical or spiritual, is out there in what EVER neighborhood you travel to to get the good goods. Be wise, avert danger, unnecessary risk. Find a different way to meet those needs, or desires of our joy-filled, INNOCENT, children.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: As a United Methodist, which of the two branches of the new divided church will you attend, and why?
Answer: Well, I am not a Methodist, though I will take this minute to thank them for the many kindnesses they showed me when my son was an infant and there’s was the church I could walk to being then car-less…. Those old ladies were so sweet… “We just LOVE to hear your baby… even when he cries; don’t ever feel badly about bringing him even if he’s fussy. It’s like music to our ears!” But I did participate in the Episcopal Church for many years and my Christian foundation was formed in it. When it split (the Church of Nigeria, Anglican Communion took the folks that were against LGBITG from becoming official clergy) due to this same issue, I saw nothing but disaster on the horizon for the “tolerant,” (read please, “don’t care enough to actually tell you the truth and help you walk it out”), and dried up religious compunction on the other. So, I left both. Both sides, IN THE USA, are dead, spiritually, nearly. They do NOT obey the Holy Spirit in matters that are quite significant; they do not fully live for God, and they put marks on people who stand up for the real truth. Instead, they try to establish rules, like fences, to establish a culture that is gone… For me, I must go where the Holy Spirit leads; I must be IN THE SPIRIT as much as possible through praying ceaselessly and in tongues much. The best shelter has always been His Wings… Neither doctrine nor self-satisfying “love” for others (that has no sacrifice in it) holds water during the worst of storms. Only Christ provides a way under all circumstances and conditions.

There are certain kinds of gifts that come, but riding the blue wave of spirituality into prosperity ALSO comes at a price that involves dedication, study, self-discipline, discipleship, and earnest watchfulness. I know a young lady from South Korea in whose hand God places diamonds, flecks of gold and other jewels. When I see this, I get so WOWED. And it isn’t the “Oh, my gosh, isn’t God amazing?” or “Oh my gosh, isn’t she special?” It’s the OH MY GOD I WANT TO BE THAT CRUCIFIED!!!” because she didn’t get that by doing nothing. And, indeed, she didn’t “work for it,” but she DID work at precisely what the bible calls us to do, she LABORED TO ENTER THE REST of God, and pursues abiding in Him earnestly (which is an understatement). Question: How do you tell if a Christian is actually trying to live a Christian life or not?
Answer: Suffering… if you see suffering, there is a good chance that they are “trying” to live a Christian life. What do I mean by suffering? I mean specifically that their conscience bothers them when hey do wrong. When they do wrong, if they suffer pangs of conscience, even if they don’t figure out how to change their behavior, even if they lag in making a positive change, they are probably trying to live a Christian life. If their suffering, however, is only about how miserable they FEEL when they experience the consequences of sin, instead, if you are a friend, or even just a church or other-believing community member, go to him or her per the instructions in the bible, in this example, Gal 6:1: “Brothers, if someone is caught in any wrongdoing, you who are spiritual should restore such a person with a gentle spirit, watching out for yourselves so you also won’t be tempted.” If this person is a member of the opposite sex, even if they are in your family, take a person with you who is their same sex. It will harder for them to play mind games with you. It’s like what people do in what is called “Twelve Step” programs… They know how tough the “demon” (or you can just call it a force of illogic tied into our instincts by dysfunctional emotional and psychological programming) of alcohol, or cocaine, or compulsive overeating, or sex addiction is. THEREFORE, they never go on 12-Step calls (which is reaching out to someone struggling with addiction) alone; they always take a buddy.

Question: What can I do? I’m a 27 year-old adult on my way to recovery. My parents are still caring for my 12 year-old sister and they are both emotionally abusive. She confides in me about these things, but doesn't want me to talk to them.
Answer: If you mean by “on my way to recovery” that you are either going to a treatment center for getting off of alcohol or drugs, or that you are in a program, free or paid for, that is helping you do so, and you are in the first year or even more years, remember this: The TWO most common “hooks” back into using are FAMILY and romantic relationships. Steer clear til you have some genuine humility, which seems to come at about five years of sobriety/clean time/abstinence. Humility is about being able to see “right size…” At this point in time, you are not the “right size” to help your younger sister. Remember, there is a higher power working in your younger sister’s life as well. I would not recommend compromising your relationship with her (i.e., if you tell what she shares in confidence with you to your parents, she will know that FOR SURE she has NO ONE to trust). Don’t focus on other people; focus on your own health and all the action steps needed to improve, protect and enhance it

Question: I want to be most holy as possible, what does a Christian need to do in order to be as holy as possible and what do they call those people?
Answer: You pose a question that is pregnant with possibilities for perfection… and for prolific spiritual fruit as a believer in Christ Jesus. First of all, you must be born again… are you? Second, if you are born again, it may be helpful to you to think about how the human being is constructed. I134. Gateways of the Spirit lays out one way to understand how we are made. Now, those with a godly mindset might say that the purpose of knowledge is to be able to put it to a good end. So, once you have a look at that diagram, I advise you to constantly recall that the Spirit in you - your spirit, resurrected at the moment of your salvation - needs to have the reins of control over both your soul (which includes all the human faculties like your subconscious, conscious and unconscious mind, your will, your conscience, your emotions, choice, imagination and reason, and your body. This is a feat in and of itself, but it will lead you into holiness. Thomas Keating, a cloistered Catholic monk and then Monsignor at an abbey in Snowmass, Colorado, says in the book (Centering Prayer, The Contemplative Dimension of the Gospel) that gives some wise counsel about how to make our own capacities more subject to control of the Holy Spirit, that the two main channels to contain and focus the power of the Spiritual Life are Service and Devotion. Service is what we do for others and for the Body of Christ as a whole, and Devotion is both our personal time with God as well as time spent learning about God. Therefore, these two things, service and devotion, taken seriously, and attended to diligently, will foster the kind of development that you wish to have. There is also much to be learned from diving into histories of the historic Catholic “saints” - both the “desert Fathers” as well as modern day saints to see how they lived and what God might tell us about what models we might want to emulate, seeking first, of course, all those things in us which He wants to see. I also HIGHLY recommend, if you are drawn to her example, viewing/listening to Heidi Baker, a missionary born in Laguna Beach, California, co-founder with her husband Rolland Baker of IRIS Ministries, on YouTube. These will be sharings from her speaking at various conferences. The older the video, the better, as what a good student will see is the progressive laying down of self (“dying to self”) that she did in order to get closer and closer to God, the Father; and to Jesus. It is a process, this dying to self thing, therefore the last thing I mention is that you need good friends who love you and who love Jesus as much as you do. This is important, for you need human love too, and we need sometimes someone else to lift up our face to the Lord so we can keep our heads above water. Your question and your desire are GOOD. DO NOT be distracted by people who say forget it, or don’t worry about it, or just obey… You are SMART to ask this question, and the desire (to be holy) should be taken SERIOUSLY… The results in the spiritual life are not unlike the results in every other area of human endeavor… those who work diligently and with serious effort get the most out of it and give the most to others and to God along the way…. Good luck!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What are the primary Biblical and theological arguments for and against infant baptism?
Answer: I will answer the question that was in my inbox; it isn’t this one, but it comes to this one… The Question I received was “Does baptism and repentance have a time frame?” This is a MUCH better question, in my opinion, than the one above… (“What are the primary Biblical and theological arguments for and against infant baptism?”).. THE question I received that is boldfaced above, has jumped OUT of the box of man’s doctrine that tends to please him but not God, and INTO the realm of no time - the realm of eternity… God’s place. Baptism and repentance DOES have a time and a frame. The time for one’s initial baptism, is in the beginning… the beginning, of what, you ask? Of different things, depending upon the kind of baptism… The baptism related to salvation is at the BEGINNING of a new life for ANY who receive Him. It does involve the remission of sins, and the resurrection of our dead human spirit. The baptism related to what is described in ACTS, where the spiritual gift of tongues begins seems to be a distinctly different event, though they can be close together and perhaps even occur at the same time as the initial one for some. What about repentance? Depends… I think babies are aware… just because they cannot talk or form words yet doesn’t mean they cannot think in some way and that they don’t understand… Are infant baptisms then acceptable? I really don’t bother myself with these things. My job is to follow the two commandments and to pursue the Great Commission and look and labor to be pleasing to God in all ways. So, repentance. For most of us, it must or should happen on a daily basis; on some days, on an hourly basis. When we are tired and cranky and fretting, perhaps every half hour! So, the TIME for repentance is whenever we have sinned, in the attitudes of our heart, in the words of our mouth, in NOT sending forth the right word at the right time, or not speaking His Word over situations, our own minds and circumstances, or INTO the lives and minds and hearts of others. So, for repentance, i’ts perfect time is any time and all the time. Thanks for including me in this adventure on Quora.

Question: My mom is having self doubts, is panicking and tells me that nobody loves her. What should I do?
Answer: Hug her. Again, and again, and again. Tell her you KNOW she can find a way to be important to others by making them important to her. Don’t let her let others use her; that will leave you dead as a rusty door nail in an old pot. Instead tell her every one of her words and deeds matters, and that there is MUCH left to be done. If you have family, make certain they know, that your mom is needing attention, RIGHT AWAY, so they can pitch in. She’s not the only one who feels this way, but YOU may be the only one who knows how she is. So, if you have to tell a few people, don’t be discouraged at all. Just pick up the phone or go visit, and throw your mom a surprise party.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Were you affected by Mel Gibson’s movie Passion of the Christ?
Answer: Yes, I was affected by Mr.. Gibson’s The Passion of the Christ. It was an amazing movie. There were so many things that were remarkable about that film to me and that rang true in my spirit… Jesus being attractive… he is called “winsome” in one of the gospels. Jesus being a man, a real man, with a mom, friends, a home, a way of making a living. I thought it was remarkable and brought me closer to him. I felt Mr. Gibson’s portrayals of both significant characters like Pontius Pilate and Herod, as well as insignificant ones, like the demons that chased Judas into his own self-made hell, were helpful, made the story “real,” got it out of my imagination and into a more accountable, objective reality. Nearly everything rang true to me about the various scenarios. I think what came through to me the most was Jesus strength of character and integrity and purpose, which was exceeded only by his extraordinary care and tenderness with which he handled each individual he dealt with. The way he dealt with Pontius Pilate… Pilate’s wife knew who Jesus was; but Pilate did not yet. But Jesus gave him room, and let Pilate ask the questions he had. Jesus didn’t blame him; AND let him know the power to seize, torture, and crucify him wasn’t available except through the express permission and provision of our Creator, and His and Our Father. This was true, AND gave Pilate space to deal with his own impressions of Jesus over time. One of the impressions, of course, was at how absurdly excessively his (Roman) soldiers had scourged Jesus. The beaten pulp of a man that stood bruised before him, he was stunned. He had given directions, and they didn’t include going so far. A disciplined man doing things for purpose and on purpose, and not for any over indulgence of the senses, Pilate saw first hand the odd rejection and irrational hate that Jesus Christ brings out in those who reject him. This hate, and at times violence, is a necessity, because there is no true and genuine defense against The Christ. There is only One Way, One Truth, and One Door. There are not a multitude. A human being (female or male) MUST resort to violence as their cloak, hatred and judgment, because otherwise they MUST do the opposite, which is to lay down their lives for the Man of Truth, of Love, of Power. There really isn’t any middle ground. You either love Jesus, or you HATE him. And Pilate saw this. This, I think, if anything, though his wife’s sensitivities I am sure paved the way as well, is what may have lead him to come to know Jesus Christ as his personal Lord and Savior. The giving to Jesus of a cup of water while he is being bullied up the Via Dolorosa by a young woman, the sweetness in that moment, is the most perfect example of how God loves us, especially through Jesus Christ. In the midst of absurdly impossible situations, He comes. No pageantry, no fanfare, just the meeting of a simple need. It is so simple, meeting someone where they are at. We may be novices, even late in life, but being right there for someone. It’s what every moment is pregnant with, the possibility of Life and Life being honored. The turning of the Roman soldier’s heart toward Jesus at the last, when he is touched by the blood of Christ from the cross… Every heart must be melted so that our wick, our Spirit, can bare itself upon the shoulders of the One who died on that cross. We cannot depend upon anything else, ever. Our PRIMARY goal, sustenance, subjection, is ALL to the CROSS, ALL to Jesus, for he have HIS ALL, and it isn’t about sentiment, though what else can possibly bring forth more emotion than the Cross, than Jesus? There is no satisfaction in JESUS without being constantly at his feet, though he will pull you up all the time, you will end up there again, amazed at his unending example of being BREAD to the world, WINE to mankind, TRUTH to decision makers, LAPS and ARMS to children, widows, bereaved fathers crying for their boys that did not come home from the wars. He is My Everything He is My Everything, Even when Nothing is Missing, He is My Shining Star, Even When It is Bright Outdoors. He is the Song on the Wing of the Wind, The Referee at My Games of Chance. He Holds the Goal Posts for the Balls I Drive Down the Field, And the Stretcher That Carries Me Off When My Errors or Others Excesses Grind Me Into That Place O Pour Yourself Out, O Man Soothe the Aching Joints; Ease the Burdened Backs, Be a Seat of Rest for the Weary. Show Your Neighbor Love, BE Complete in Your Reaching Out; Extend Your Purse to Pour Good Things O’er Others, Your Brawn to Bolster the Weak. Bring Home the Abandoned and Rejected, Bind Up the Wounds of Their Hearts. Sing Joy Back Into Their SORE Bones, And Justice Into Their Minds… Righteousness Into Their Posture, and New Hope Into Their Lives. O Sing, Little Finch, of the King, Little Finch, That Reliably Brings Along Spring! SING! Big Blue Bird Your Rhythms, March Winter Right Out of the Court. Hoot, Big Owl to Warn Us, Of That Rattler Fat on the Ground; Stomp, Stallion, on Scorpions, And Breathe FIRE upon that Grate. That Grate that Leads to the Dungeon, That No Man Woman or Child Can Escape. It Sounds at First Like a New Idea, But Betrays Its Intentions Right Away. As Your Heart Begins to Harden, And Your Chance for Heaven Evaporates.

Question: Why do Evangelicals get a tax-free ticket when they aren't even listed among the top 100 charitable organizations in the United States?
Answer: If you please, provide a bit of clarification: Thank you for addressing these details if time permits. If time does not, perhaps it might be worth contributing this perspective from someone who has struggled quite a bit with today’s “church.” When it comes to money and churches, I think of statistics shared at one very UN-charismatic church I attended. The pastor (who, with his family, took 7/12 of the church’s $120,000 annual budget for their needs of this tiny church supported by maybe three dozen families) stated that less than $1 of every $100 put into the church coffers (not sure if this includes the Catholic empire or not), historically, has gone to missions. But missions have been the most successful at reaching whole people groups with a basis for understanding and being willing to attempt to live by the rule of law; this is because the entrance of Christ into one’s being pulls people out of the economy of hell and into the economy of heaven. When this is accomplished in a group of people, this frees people up to trust, to forgive, to work with one another. So, that reflection aside, what I think of when people hint or blast the plentiful faults of today’s church, I think of Claudia Wintoch Wilson, a native of Austria, who when she got saved, was so grateful to Jesus, she said, “Lord, send me where NO ONE wants to go.” He put her in the middle of Mali; a land-locked nation in north Africa… whose biggest claim to fame is that the largest gold route ever known to man used to run right though it… hence our saying about Timbuktu, which is a city in Mali that terrorist groups have used as of late to hunker down in. She was given land almost immediately, as white women are seen sometimes in those countries as being full of unlimited influence… so, why not make a friend? Never mind that the locals have taken back the land that she then built an orphanage upon for about 60 full-time children. The children come from all over the city, Bamako, as Mali is of course dirt poor. Half of the nation’s population is under 15 years of age. While the country’s constitution guarantees freedom of religion, 99% declare affiliation with Islam as Muslims often run the businesses there and therefore control economic opportunity… no different than the reason so many others have affiliated as Christian in other cases. Now, to be a good Muslim there, every family is expected to give one of their children to their local mosque… But Mali is broke, including the mosques, so the mosque sends the children to the street to beg… or to do whatever it takes… to bring home money to their caregivers. The children that wander dazed from hunger, rape, total usurpation of any of their human faculties to generate direction or optimism, some end up with Claudia. Their road to sanity is often long. And the locals don’t like it, because, frankly, while the the vast majority of the locals profess Islam, probably at least half if not more are actually into devil worship/witchcraft. Question: How can I "build up" a church with no youth and no money?
Answer: Not every group of people that own a yard or two of land and all itself a church should be “saved.” Many churches must die, God himself removes his candlestick… removes the Angelic coverage, and vacates the property, which, I think, is DIRECTLY related to people NOT being faithful to the “part” of the Triune God which is Holy Spirit.
