Question: What’s the best way to politely decline a group of Mormons at your door that are extremely persistent?
Answer: Well, here’s what I do… I go outside with them, because I find that while there are some Mormons that have gotten a hold of Christ, quite a few have not and some of them are treated in vile ways by authoritative/absent parents. So, the card I play when I see Mormons is to value them. I ask them what they are doing, I tell them I admire many things about their church, which I do… they are extraordinarily good at practical teaching for their youth… and I ask them what kind of goals are they working on for their mission work. Really, all they are is people trying to do what they think, or what someone else thinks, is a good thing to do. So, Kennedy, greet them happily the next time they come to your door. Walk with them outside and ask them about their journey and their education and their hopes and dreams. Name: Sara Stone
Question: How can I bring myself to go back to church, after a pastor tried praying the autism out of me, and I don’t know how to be less uncomfortable of going back?
Answer: Dear Fellow Sufferer of the Hands of An Uneducated, often UNCARING, Church: IT ISN’T YOU, IT’S THEM. Dear Jenna, if this happened to you or to someone close to you, I am sorry. I do believe all things can be healed, and that God’s good pleasure is to do so, and I also believe it’s a journey. If I hadn’t been exposed to the “charismatic” part of Christianity by people who had high integrity and intelligence, I may have given up on the whole enterprise. The first thing I had to do, Jenna, is get in touch with what I was truly longing for from God, from Christ, from Holy Spirit. Often, the church (or nearly all the churches and/or ministries I have ever been involved with) summarily expects you to bow, curtsy, genuflect precisely when it is their congregation’s expectation that you do so, and you’re even supposed to read their minds to figure out these expectations. This, of course, is social bullying and not of Christ. Jesus didn’t expect people to be different than what they were. He came to GIVE them life; not to take it from them by making them feel worse about themselves, unless they were holding fast to false idols… then the pride, which is what allows us to rationalize such affection, has to go. What I would recommend is taking your bible, whatever the favorite parts are TO YOU, and start your day out with the Lord. Spend 15 minutes reading the bible WITH the Lord. Just start talking to him Jenna. He knows how you feel, he knows what you desire and dream for, he knows everything. He knows your heart. He would not have you hurt over this for anything. Spend at least a month or so with just Jesus and the book and try to pray throughout the day. I love a consummate teacher of Christ named Graham Cooke (United Kingdom and very findable on YouTube and Facebook); he preaches with such warmth and a good sense of humor… and he is seasoned and KNOWS what he is doing. No ego, or at least it’s not leading the show. He can coach you on having an effective prayer life. I find that starting out with prayer by remembering God’s character… that he send his only begotten son into this mess FOR ME, that he loves me THAT much, helps. And, that Jesus calls us FRIENDS in the bible… So, I can be natural with him. We just kind of talk back and forth… sort of… I ask him to bring out of me His will; I ask him to help me… with all my large and looming defects of character and quirks. And by continuing to talk to him throughout the day about a lot of little things, well, my day goes a LOT better. ASK ASK ASK, Jenna, ask for little things… and big things, but the little tend to build us up to be strong enough to believe for the better things. There’s even a person who has been healed of Down Syndrome.. completely healed… that means GENETICALLY. And there’s a guy in Australia who had a steel bar go through the center of his head; HE was healed and FUNCTIONS normally, serving God PROLIFICALLY. NO ONE is forgotten by God; it’s us who turn away. Oh also, along the way, pray for the pastor that prayed for you and the autism you are experiencing. Just remember no one is God except God. Last, I have finally learned it really is okay to be me. And that means a lot of people don’t like me sometimes. But I decided that to whatever extent I am going to participate in church, I am going to stand up for what I think is right and call a spade a spade. If people judge me to such an extent that I no longer enjoy the place, then, well, there’s other churches to go to. It is not a sin to “church-hop.” After all, the Wind goes where it will. Holy Spirit will sometimes take us on a winding journey… That doesn’t mean YOUR journey needs to be like that; just means you need to protect yourself as best as possible, and DO NOT make ANYONE into your teacher, rabbi, “father” and so on. Feel free to pm me in Quora system if you have specific concerns and I will do my best to be of help to you, or any other reader. God bless you, Jenna. The Lord loves you, very much. He will hold no good thing back from you.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Have you ever known someone that was healed by faith?
Answer: Is it wrong to answer a question with a question? If not, here is the beginning of my questions for you: Did Jesus walk “by faith” across the Sea of Galilee? Or something else? If it was something else, was it something, “material?” Like an invisible cloak? If it was an invisible cloak, can we put that on? Can we “walk on water” while standing on such a thing? Are carbon nanotubes willing to be at our command if we have faith? Would it be the same thing or things that helped the Monks of Skellig build a steep path of stones up the side of Skellig Michael, a crag in the British Isles, 1300 years ago? Do I stay well because I “believe” I am, or will be well? Or because I acknowledge God is in me and He doesn’t get sick, period? So, do I know someone who was healed “by faith?” Does that mean “faith healing…” like someone laid hands on them and they got well? I can tell you this. I have met two people who “had” multiple sclerosis and in the case of one, then in her 70’s when I met her, she had been free from MS symptoms ever since she had, what she experienced as a healing from God… no big event, just as a “result” of her faith in God and she believed God healed her, more than 20 years prior. A second man, Elery Mayo, a Vietnam Marine Veteran, (see some clips here if you can: https://vimeo.com/user5873730 was “saved” in Christ, in 1973, but in one year, he was in and out of a wheel chair, paralyzed, blind, with doctors trying to figure out what “it” was, and eventually finding out it was MS. Now Elery believed the Lord, he had faith, and he KNEW the words in the Good Book were true, that whosoever believed on Jesus and followed him would indeed do the same works, AND BETTER, Jesus said, but it can take some time… it is a learning process. He explained that this learning process as it applied to his body and disease, took “seven years to learn to walk in the healing that Jesus died for us to have access to…” So, as Elery put it, “Now, if they x-rayed my grey matter, they might still find those plaques… they were still there the last time I got those pictures… “ but the last time was more than a decade ago… “but fact is, the only time I get symptoms is if someone comes up who is trying to get healed from MS.” My own personal introduction to what I might call the physics of faith (though I am not talking just in terms of what might be some of the thinking in “Christian Science”) was through Elery… he taught the SUPRA-natural world behind this one… and gradually I have gotten more and more into the Spirit. God is big on not just believing in him (the “devils believe and tremble…” but we know where they live), but in obeying him. The closer we STAY to him, the more we can walk in a way where illness is not common. For me this is how it works: We must remember our position in God. He is our FATHER, it’s not just a metaphor; it’s REAL. IF WE ARE HIS SONS, then we can do what he does, PERIOD. But it does take practice; harnessing control over our emotions and thought life is the elusive key, but bible reading, fellowship with other believers in Christ, and related activities, like just doing what’s good for you and others, helps. Thanks for the A2A, Mike S.

Question: How can the elements and dynamics of a particular type of Christian spirituality contribute to reaching a state of Christian unity?
Answer: This is a very interesting question and as of late somewhat on my mind. I am thinking of Nehemiah and how he knew as did other Jewish leaders of the time exactly what types of skills and “inborn” talents lay with which tribes, when he assigned different groups to each gate and section of the wall to be rebuilt around Jerusalem. Nehemiah’s brilliant activities to reestablish Jerusalem began with an understanding of identify and was worked out by continuing to acknowledge the identify of each person and groups of people. My son, since a VERY young age, even four years old, has had a passion for unifying the church. I do not think there is time in these times for a totally new “structure” to be built, but I do think a smart leadership tactic would be calling out each fundamentally gifted part of the Body of Christ to partake in those areas that they are strongest at. Catholics, for instance, perhaps more so than any other denomination, invested hugely in education, in the search for wisdom through biblical studies AND through studies of the sciences (think of the “father” of genetics, Gregor Mendel: 1865 | Gregor Mendel, the father of modern genetics, presents his research on experiments in plant hybridization). Perhaps we call them to re-establish these traditions presently. The Baptists, while some actively deny the power of God (unbelief… in miracles, signs, wonders and so on), are very good at aspects of familial relations, and the social sciences… Perhaps we call on them to share how they operate to preserve and enhance this vitality in their own families. The Mormons, so many of them not in ANY personal relationship with the Christ at all, nonetheless, have been practicing practical things for decades to where their putting aside of food for pantries, their prepping, their teaching of practical life skills (like budgeting, cooking, and project planning). What about calling out ALL the church to go learn from them what may be increasingly important things to know and do in the coming years??? The “Jesus Culture” people, perhaps more truly emotional than evangelical, could we really do anything great for Jesus without a willingness to LOVE JESUS personally? I think not and therefor, let Bethel in. Let Windsong breathe their notes across our spirit… The Episcopalians know how to get their staffs paid by providing donation opportunities for the communities they are in where retail purchases result in both income for their church teaching staff AND for a few paid people in their clothing and household stuffs stores. Let’s learn how to re-invigorate our budgets, personal and otherwise, from them! They are also really good at form and structure. So we see here, though this summary is quite superficial, just how strengths shared and emulated may help the diverse community of believers that exist within every denomination and church mature and become more excellent; coming together is one way to get the good stuff to rub off on us. We can also challenge the things that we see might be holding some people’s walks back a bit, once we are collaboratively working toward some good common goals. This is how, in general, I would see the variety of giftedness within the different parts of the Body coming together into unity.

Question: Are Ouija boards really dangerous in a way that a demonic entity can be let in?

Question: Can the devil hurt a righteous person?
Answer: Yes. Padre Pio, one of the few documented priests in the history of the Catholic Church to have suffered the stigmata (the wounds of Christ) was literally wrestled to the ground and attacked repeatedly from time to time by demons. Padre Pio’s “righteousness” was unquestionable; for those who knew him closely and for his spiritual sons and daughters, the works of faith Christ did through him were prolific. For 53 years, this man was a cloistered monk at San Giovanni Rotunda in southern Italy. He performed mass five times a day and took literally hundreds of confessions per day as well. Question: What does a minor do when his parents beat him and the pastor just says 'Obey your parents because it says so in The Bible'?
Answer: Being beat is different from being disciplined. If you are an adult and are aware of a situation you think is abusive, which means the actions will leave the child worse off in terms of facing life’s many challenges, or even worse, that the actions will cut that child’s life short before he or she even reaches adulthood, than, as Bruce Willis’ character, John McClane, says in Live Free or Die Hard, YOU’RE THAT GUY. No, not all the time. Yes, tried to do better. Yes, sought counseling. Yes, yes, yes. Yes, invested myself in him, went to soccer games, showed up at all school events, told him I was sorry, made sure certain things were special, and so on… But you know what I needed? No support of ANY kind from the father and my family? Oh, don’t ask. The isolation made me close in on myself. If not that, then, 2) Someone to come in a beat my ass and warn me that if I ever lost my temper even once again they would break my legs. Seriously. I was never beat or hit as a kid; in fact, spanked, only once, hardly never got yelled at, but I was seriously over indulged and not held accountable. I think it would have helped. And that would have helped my son. To see justice, early. To know things didn’t have to be as bad as they were. So Ron, go do the right thing. As for the minor, a human being, even young, knows instinctively when they have had enough, and where their breaking point is; if and when they are old enough, they can find their way if they have some grit… They can try the system, instead, to begin the process of emancipation. One friend told me his alcoholic mother stopped beating him when he got big enough to stand up to her and took after her with a broom. She never bothered him again. With a father, if he’s big and strong, that can be a difficult option to come by. If the abuse is really bad, phones can video tape and maybe you can do that for the minor. If your question really is about the bible, the parents needs to know this verse as well: EPHESIANS 6 1 Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. 2 Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; 3 That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth. 4 And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. Takes a whole lot of nurturing to make up for, if it ever can, rage-driven beatings. My mother was a faithful wife and good mother, but the beatings her father gave her never completely left her mind, making her toss her head to and fro, in the last couple weeks of her life before she died of acute lymphocytic leukemia, saying, “No, no, stop, I didn’t do it….” Sad.
